descriptionByLocale.en:
PhD position in Global Trade, Supply Chains and Climate Shocks

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

Research Division KOF Lab of ETH Zurich’s KOF Swiss Economic Institute is seeking a PhD candidate to study the propagation of weather and climate shocks in quantitative trade network models. The position is part of the National Centre of Competence in Research project Climate Extremes and Society: Strengthening Resilience (NCCR CLIM+). NCCR CLIM+ is a new, interdisciplinary, Switzerland-wide climate research community involving multiple investigators at ETH Zurich and other Swiss institutions.

Job description

• The project at KOF Lab will center around assessing and promoting the resilience of supply chains by building and solving quantitative global equilibrium models of trade networks.

• We will use firm-level data to estimate the industry/country-level effects of various weather and climate shocks and input the estimated impacts into the model.

• To this end, the doctoral candidate will leverage theoretical, computational, and econometric tools to study public policy questions related to the resilience of global supply chains to climate change.

• The doctorate will be conducted within the doctoral program of D-MTEC (Department of Management, Technology, and Economics) and is expected to be completed within four years.

• The candidate will be supervised primarily by Professor Hans Gersbach and Dr. Kieran Walsh.

• The position is for up to four years. The salary is in accordance with the PhD regulations of the Swiss National Science Foundation, which funds the NCCR.

Profile

• The applicant should have a master’s degree in economics or finance. We will also consider candidates with a master’s degree in mathematics or statistics, provided they have completed some coursework in economics and are prepared to do intensive economics PhD training.

• Applicants must be highly proficient in English.

• The applicant should be proficient in either MATLAB, Python, or Julia and willing to work in MATLAB.

• Prior coursework in (i) trade theory and (ii) environmental economics would be a major asset.

• Experience with panel data econometrics would be beneficial.

Workplace

We offer

• We offer the opportunity to apply cutting-edge economic theory to practical policy issues at the intersection of trade and climate change.

• Candidates will have the opportunity to contribute to NCCR CLIM+ research discussions.

• We offer the opportunity to join KOF, which is Switzerland’s leading academic institute for applied economic research. It provides independent and objective data and facts, as well as timely assessments to support decision-makers in politics and business in making fact-based decisions for the benefit of Swiss society.

• KOF PhD students are part of a large and vibrant community of economic researchers. The broader economics community in Zurich offers the opportunity to participate in numerous workshops and conferences spanning all fields of economics.

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application until 10 July 2026 with the following documents:

• A letter of motivation, which should include a proposed starting date

• Your CV, which should include contact information for three references (no letters are needed at this point)

• Your university transcripts

• A chap

Postdoc Position in Experimental Quantum Engineering (EQE) Group

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Experimental Quantum Engineering (EQE) group at ETH Zurich and the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) invites applications for a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher to work at the interface of quantum optics, quantum information science and quantum many-body physics.

Led by Prof. Wenchao Xu , the EQE group develops programmable quantum systems based on neutral atoms and Rydberg interactions to advance both fundamental quantum science and next-generation quantum technologies. Our research combines atomic physics, quantum control, and scalable architectures for fault-tolerant quantum computation, hybrid quantum simulation, and quantum-enhanced sensing.

Project background

Our group addresses key challenges in quantum science by building and exploiting hybrid quantum systems consisting of individually controlled atoms and atomic ensembles.

Current research directions include:

• Demonstrating scalable architectures for fault-tolerant quantum information processing, featuring reconfigurable local control, rapid quantum non-demolition readout, and fast error-syndrome extraction

• Developing strong atom–light interfaces to enable quantum interconnects and modular quantum systems

• Investigating non-equilibrium quantum many-body dynamics and quantum information dynamics in programmable atom arrays

Job description

We seek a postdoctoral researcher to contribute to a new experimental platform based on dual-type tweezer atom arrays.

The project aims to demonstrate the unique advantages for:

• Reconfigurable local quantum control

• Rapid, non-demolition state detection of both single- and multi-qubit states

• Novel phenomena in quantum dynamics arising from the interplay with measurement

These capabilities enable new routes toward fault-tolerant quantum computation and open exciting opportunities for exploring frontier problems in quantum information dynamics.

The successful candidate will:

• Design, build, and operate state-of-the-art neutral-atom experiments

• Demonstrate novel quantum control and measurement protocols

• Lead research projects and mentor students

• Collaborate closely with researchers at ETH Zurich, PSI, and international partners

More information about the project and the group can be found on our website .

Starting date: flexible in 2026

Employment: full-time

Profile

• PhD in physics or a related field

• Strong background in experimental AMO physics or quantum optics

• Experience with cold atoms, optical tweezers, lasers, or quantum control techniques is highly desirable

• Strong interest in neutral-atom quantum technologies and many-body quantum physics

• Ability to work both independently and collaboratively

• Good communication skills in English (German is a plus)

Workplace

We offer

• A highly creative and collaborative research environment

• Freedom to develop independent research directions

• Access to world-class infrastructure at ETH Zurich and PSI

• Opportunities for interdisciplinary and international collaborations

• Competitive salary and benefits

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents:

• CV (with publication list)

• Cover letter

• 2-3 references

Please submit your application through our onli

PhD position in light controlled variable stiffness for soft robotics

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Robotic Materials group is looking for a highly motivated PhD student for the topic of light programmable stiffness for reconfigurable soft devices and robots. This 4-year PhD position is funded by our ERC Starting Grant .

Project background

The introduction of fiber optics in the 1970s has revolutionized the telecommunications industry upon the replacement of copper wires and played a major role in the advent of the Information Age - One high bandwidth fiber optic cable can replace thousands of electrical links to transmit the same amount of information. As a parallel to the thriving fields of soft devices and robots controlled by electrical signals, soft optics is emerging as a new platform that uses the modulation of light in soft matter to encode multifunctionalities in the optical path.

The first part of this project will center around developing light-stimulated stiffness programming methods that surpass the performance of current variable stiffness benchmarks. The second part will focus on the application of this principle in several soft device/robot systems to demonstrate reconfigurability and multifunctionality for real-world tasks.

Job description

• Creation of methods to program material stiffness in-situ with light. Goals: high stiffness contrast (rigid-soft), fast transition (

This is a full-time position that starts as soon as possible. Applications are evaluated on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Profile

• MS degree in Materials Science and Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related fields from a top-notch university

• Candidates with strong track records of research in soft robotics, smart materials, or related fields (especially with experience of working on variable stiffness materials and robots) are highly welcomed to apply

• Excellent problem-solving abilities and a passion for interdisciplinary research

Workplace

We offer

• A productive working environment with training and guidance from the PI on a regular basis

• Competitive salary according to ETH standards (fully funded, full-time, fixed term position)

• An interdisciplinary, international, and diverse team of talents and a stimulating, vibrant, collaborative group

• Strong connections with academic, industrial, and clinical partners in materials science, robotics, and healthcare.

descriptionByLocale.en:
Postdoc position in soft optical fiber-based artificial muscle for biomedical applications

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Robotic Materials group is looking for a highly motivated postdoc for the topic of soft optical fiber-based artificial muscle for biomedical applications . This position is funded by our ERC Starting Grant .

Project background

The introduction of fiber optics in the 1970s has revolutionized the telecommunications industry upon the replacement of copper wires and played a major role in the advent of the Information Age - One high bandwidth fiber optic cable can replace thousands of electrical links to transmit the same amount of information. As a parallel to the thriving fields of soft devices and robots controlled by electrical signals, soft optics is emerging as a new platform that uses the modulation of light in soft matter to encode multifunctionalities in the optical path.

The focus of this project is to create biocompatible, high performance soft actuators multiplexed by light, all integrated on a miniature fiber, delivering advanced robotic and biomedical functions as minimally invasive surgical tools and implantable devices.

Job description

• Develop biocompatible soft actuators controlled by light with performance matching benchmarked soft robotic actuators

• Design and microfabrication of soft optical fibers densely distributed with actuators

• Develop actuator multiplexing methods for individual addressability

• Demonstration for advanced robotic functions as minimally invasive surgical tools

• Integration with bioelectronic functions (e.g., sensing) for closed-loop controlled diagnostic and therapeutic functions.

• Demonstration as robotic/biomedical devices for real-world application through collaborations.

• Supervise master/bachelor students

• Teaching assistant for the robotic materials class

Profile

• PhD degree in Materials Science and Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related fields from a top university.

• Strong research track records in one or more of the following: bioelectronics, soft robotics, flexible electronics, fiber-based devices, functional materials, wearable systems, or biomedical devices.

• Hands-on experience in device design, prototyping, experimental characterization, and TRL 3-5 demonstrations.

• Knowledge of biomedical soft materials, textile/fiber processing, microfabrication, or soft actuators is highly desirable

• Excellent problem-solving abilities and a passion for interdisciplinary research.

Workplace

We offer

• A productive working environment with training and guidance from the PI on a regular basis

• Competitive salary according to ETH standards (fully funded, full-time, fixed term position)

• An interdisciplinary, international, and diverse team of talents and a stimulating, vibrant, collaborative group

• Strong connections with academic, industrial, and clinical partners in materials science, robotics, and healthcare.

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your application with the following documents as a single PDF:

• A cover letter

• CV

• Publication list with a few sentences highlighting representative works

• Contact details of two referees

• Optional: transcripts of academic records

The preferred start date is as soon as possible in the third quarter of 2026 .

L'obiettivo di questo progetto è di espandere sia le capacità di azionamento che di rilevamento con la luce. Il progetto creerà una rete di sensorimotori artificiali con attuatori e sensori densamente distribuiti simili alla neuromascolatura biologica. La prima parte del progetto svilupperà una singola fibra ottica morbida con attuatori multimodali distribuiti che sono anche auto-sensibilizzanti. La seconda parte studierà il comportamento raggruppato di questi “pacchetti muscolari” per consentire il coordinamento muscolare per movimenti complessi/adaptivi/efficienti. Descrizione del lavoro

Postdoc position in light multiplexed, fiber-based artificial sensorimotor network

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Robotic Materials group is looking for a highly motivated postdoc for the topic of light multiplexed artificial sensorimotor network . This position is funded by our ERC Starting Grant .

Project background

The introduction of fiber optics in the 1970s has revolutionized the telecommunications industry upon the replacement of copper wires and played a major role in the advent of the Information Age - One high bandwidth fiber optic cable can replace thousands of electrical links to transmit the same amount of information. As a parallel to the thriving fields of soft devices and robots controlled by electrical signals, soft optics is emerging as a new platform that uses the modulation of light in soft matter to encode multifunctionalities in the optical path.

The focus of this project is to expand both actuation and sensing capacities with light. The project will create an artificial sensorimotor network with densely distributed actuators and sensors similar to the biological neuromasculature. The first part of the project will develop a single soft optical fiber with distributed multimodal actuators that are also self-sensing. The second part will study grouped behavior of these “muscle bundles” to enable muscle coordination for complex/adaptive/efficient movements.

Job description

• Based on existing light actuators in our group, develop self-sensing methods where the transducer serves both for actuation and sensing, and is feedback controlled with onboard optoelectronics

• Design and microfabrication of a soft optical fiber distributed with such transducers configured for multiple modalities, and enable individual addressability through light multiplexing, based on the group’s expertise

• Demonstrate the single artificial neuromuscular fiber for advanced robotic functions arising from the distributed and multimodal actuators and sensors

• In the second part, create grouped neuromuscular bundles with extremely high functional density approaching orders of magnitude of biology

• Investigate emergent coordinated bundle behavior and motion patterns arising from biologically similar redundancy with collaborations of control and learning

• Demonstrate for advanced robotic functions

• Supervise master/bachelor students

• Teaching assistant for the robotic materials class

This is a full-time position that starts as soon as possible. Applications are evaluated on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Profile

• PhD degree in Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science and Engineering or related fields from a top university

• Strong research track records in one or more of the following: micro robots, soft robotics, fiber-based robots, or related

• Hands-on experience in robot design, prototyping, experimental characterization, and TRL 3-5 demonstration

• Knowledge of reconfigurable/multifunctional microrobots, small-scale soft robotics, feedback controlled soft robotic systems is highly desirable

• Excellent problem-solving abilities and a passion for interdisciplinary research

Workplace

We offer

• A productive working environment with training and guidance from the PI on a regular basis

• Competitive salary according to ETH standards (fully funded, full-time, fixed term position)

• An interdisciplinary, international, and diverse team of talents and a stimulating, vibrant, collaborative group

• Strong connections with academic, industrial, and clinical partners in materials science, robotics, and healthcare

chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht Postdoc position in light multiplexed, fibre-based artificielle sensorimotor network 100%, Zurich, print à terme fixe Drucken Le groupe Robotic Materials recherche un postdoc très motivé pour le thème du réseau de capteurs artificiels multiplexed light. Ce poste est financé par notre subvention de démarrage du CEE . Contexte du projet L'introduction de la fibre optique dans les années 1970 a révolutionné l'industrie des télécommunications en remplaçant les fils de cuivre et a joué un rôle majeur dans l'avènement de l'ère de l'information - Un câble fibre optique à bande passante élevée peut remplacer des milliers de liaisons électriques pour transmettre la même quantité d'information. Parallèlement aux champs florissants d'appareils et de robots doux commandés par des signaux électriques, l'optique douce apparaît comme une nouvelle plateforme qui utilise la modulation de la lumière en matière douce pour coder les multifonctions dans le chemin optique. Ce projet vise à développer les capacités d'action et de détection avec la lumière. Le projet créera un réseau de capteurs moteurs artificiels avec des actionneurs et des capteurs densément distribués semblables à la neuromasculature biologique. La première partie du projet développera une seule fibre optique douce avec des actionneurs multimodaux distribués qui sont également auto-sensibilisants. La deuxième partie étudiera le comportement groupé de ces faisceaux musculaires afin de permettre la coordination musculaire pour des mouvements complexes, adaptés et efficaces. Description du travail

• Démontrer la fibre neuromusculaire artificielle unique pour les fonctions robotiques avancées issues des actuateurs et capteurs distribués et multimodaux
• Dans la deuxième partie, créer des faisceaux neuromusculaires groupés avec une densité fonctionnelle extrêmement élevée approchant les ordres de grandeur de la biologie

• Démontrer pour des fonctions robotiques avancées

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

We invite applications for a PhD position in the field of quantum computing, to be advised by Dominik Hangleiter and co-advised by Renato Renner. In our group in Zurich, you will find a welcoming, open, and highly interactive research environment. Our work is collaborative and interdisciplinary, and it is firmly embedded in the international quantum computing community.

Job description

• The topic of your PhD will be at the interface of theoretical computer science, quantum computing architectures, and the foundations of quantum computing with a focus depending on your interests

• If you want to read more about the kind of research questions and challenges that we investigate in our group, you can find more detailed information on our website at dhangleiter.eu

Profile

• We strongly encourage you to submit an application if you have an academic background in computer science, mathematics, or theoretical physics

• You are highly motivated to pursue a PhD, and if you are enthusiastic about collaborating and working together with others

Workplace

We offer

• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents in a single merged pdf file in this order :

• your CV, including the contact details of one or two references (max 2 pages),

• a statement explaining how you came to be interested in the theory of quantum computing, a question you are particularly excited about, and why you want to pursue a PhD (max. 500 words),

• a transcript of records (Bachelor’s and Master’s),

• a sample of your own academic writing, for example, a thesis or essay.

We are starting to consider applications and contact your references on June 15, 2026 , but applications can still be submitted until the job is filled. The starting date is flexible.

Further information about D-PHYS can be found on our Website . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Dominik Hangleiter, dhangleiter@ethz.ch (no applications).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading universities specialising in
science and technology. We are renowned for our excellent education,
cutting-edge fundamental research and direct transfer of new knowledge
into society. Over 30,000 people from more than 120 countries find our
university to be a place that promotes independent thinking and an
environment that inspires excellence. Located in the heart of Europe,
yet forging connections all over the world, we work together to
develop solutions for the global challenges of today and tomorrow.

Posizione del PhD nel sensore del veicolo e analisi di rilevamento remoto per la sicurezza stradale 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo La Cattedra di Gestione delle Infrastrutture, guidata dal Professor Dr. Bryan T. Adey all'interno dell'Istituto di Costruzione e Gestione delle Infrastrutture del Dipartimento di Ingegneria Civile, Enviromentale e Geomatica, ha un'apertura per uno studente di dottorato. Questa posizione si concentra sulla leva dei sensori del veicolo, il telerilevamento e l'apprendimento automatico per supportare l'analisi moderna della sicurezza stradale urbana come parte di un progetto UE più ampio. Sfondo del progetto Il nuovo progetto EU Horizon promuove l'assorbimento e la ricerca di una mobilità attiva sicura introducendo un approccio basato su prove umane che integra la sicurezza reale e percepita per pedoni, ciclisti e utenti di micromobilità. Passando oltre i convenzionali approcci focalizzati agli urti, cattura vicino-misses, interazioni dinamiche e esperienze di sicurezza incarnate che modellano il comportamento e la scelta della modalità. Il progetto combina il traffico multi-fonte, l'infrastruttura, il veicolo e i dati sanitari con la sperimentazione immersiva eXtended Reality (XR) e l'intelligenza artificiale spiegabile per analizzare situazioni di sicurezza-critical che sono rare, sottovalutate, o eticamente impossibili da osservare nel traffico reale. La Spiegabile AI garantisce trasparenza e interpretabilità, sostenendo fiducia, trasferibilità e rilevanza politica. Il progetto traduce queste intuizioni in metodologie di valutazione armonizzate, modelli predittivi e indicatori convalidati, consentendo una valutazione e un confronto robusti di interventi normativi, infrastrutturali, tecnologici e comportamentali tra gli stakeholder di Safe System Approach. Particolare attenzione è posta sulle interazioni tra utenti con diverse masse e velocità, tra cui e-bike, e-cargo bike, e-scooters, sia per la mobilità personale che per la logistica urbana. I piloti su larga scala in quattro città europee convalidano i metodi nel traffico reale, supportano l'apprendimento trasversale e garantiscono l'applicabilità in diverse condizioni di sicurezza, infrastruttura e cultura. Implementato da un'ingegneria multidisciplinare di collegamento consortile, scienza comportamentale, XR, AI, pianificazione urbana e politica, il progetto offre una guida attuabile e standardizzata che accelera sistemi attivi e di micromobilità più sicuri e inclusivi in tutta Europa. La pianificazione di sistemi di trasporto urbano sicuri è intrinsecamente complessa: gli interventi durano per decenni, richiedono un investimento significativo, devono adattarsi all'interno di spazi limitati, e devono soddisfare le esigenze degli utenti in continua evoluzione. I moderni metodi di raccolta dei dati - come i sensori di veicoli a bordo ad alta frequenza e le immagini di computer-visione - sono adatti per catturare queste complessità attraverso intuizioni in tempo reale, ad alta risoluzione. Tuttavia, la raccolta, l'elaborazione e la operativizzazione di questi grandi volumi di dati è una sfida a causa di strutture di dati eterogenee e pesanti richieste computazionali. Descrizione del lavoro Questo dottorato mira a far progredire lo stato dell'arte nella fusione dei dati del sensore e del telerilevamento per l'analisi della sicurezza delle infrastrutture di trasporto urbano. Il candidato svilupperà nuovi strumenti e metodi che integrano grandi dati, visione del computer e machine learning. I compiti principali del candidato includono:
• Sviluppare una Pipeline di rilevamento scalabile: progettare e implementare un'architettura software/tool in grado di elaborare sensori, telecamere e flussi di dati di telerilevamento
• Identificazione automatica delle caratteristiche e dei fattori: Modelli di apprendimento della macchina da treno e visione del computer all'interno della pipeline per rilevare automaticamente le caratteristiche dell'infrastruttura dell'ambiente costruito e i fattori correlati che influenzano la sicurezza e il comfort della micromobilità
• Genera mappatura e uscite diagnostiche: Assicurarsi che il software accetti diversi input e genera uscite di dati strutturate e di alta qualità ottimizzate per mappatura spaziale, diagnosi di rischio e modellazione di sicurezza predittiva a valle
• Collaborare tramite Real-World Pilots: convalidare e perfezionare la pipeline utilizzando i dati reali delle città pilota del progetto, lavorando in stretta coope

PhD Position in Vehicle Sensor and Remote Sensing Analysis for Road Safety

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Chair of Infrastructure Management, led by Professor Dr. Bryan T. Adey within the Institute of Construction and Infrastructure Management of the Department of Civil, Enviromental, and Geomatic Engineering, has an opening for a PhD student. This position focuses on leveraging vehicle sensors, remote sensing, and machine learning to support modern urban road safety analysis as a part of a larger EU project.

Project background

The new EU Horizon project advances safe active mobility uptake and research by introducing a human-centred, evidence-based approach that integrates actual and perceived safety for pedestrians, cyclists, and micromobility users. Moving beyond conventional crash-focused approaches, it captures near-misses, dynamic interactions, and embodied safety experiences that shape behaviour and mode choice. The project combines multi-source traffic, infrastructure, vehicle, and health data with immersive eXtended Reality (XR) experimentation and explainable Artificial Intelligence to analyse safety-critical situations that are rare, underreported, or ethically impossible to observe in real traffic. Explainable AI ensures transparency and interpretability, supporting trust, transferability, and policy relevance. The project translates these insights into harmonised assessment methodologies, predictive models, and validated indicators, enabling robust evaluation and comparison of regulatory, infrastructural, technological, and behavioural interventions across Safe System Approach stakeholders. Special focus is placed on interactions between users with differing masses and speeds, including e-bikes, e-cargo bikes, and e-scooters, for both personal mobility and urban logistics. Large-scale pilots in four European cities validate methods in real traffic, support cross-city learning, and ensure applicability under diverse safety, infrastructure and cultural conditions. Implemented by a multidisciplinary consortium bridging engineering, behavioural science, XR, AI, urban planning, and policy, the project delivers actionable, standardised guidance that accelerates safer, more inclusive active and micromobility systems across Europe.

Planning safe urban transport systems is inherently complex: interventions last for decades, require significant investment, must fit within constrained spaces, and must satisfy ever-changing user needs. Modern data collection methods - such as high-frequency on-board vehicle sensors and computer-vision imagery - are well-suited to capture these complexities via near real-time, high-resolution insights. However, collecting, processing, and operationalizing these big data volumes is a challenge due to heterogeneous data structures and heavy computational demands.

Job description

This doctorate aims to advance the state-of-the-art in sensor and remote sensing data fusion for urban transport infrastructure safety analysis. The candidate will develop new tools and methods that integrate big data, computer vision, and machine learning. The candidate’s core tasks will include:

• Develop a Scalable Sensing Pipeline: Design and implement a software/tool architecture capable of processing multi-source vehicle sensor, camera, and remote sensing data streams

• Automate Feature & Factor Identification: Train machine learning and computer vision models within the pipeline to automatically detect built-environment infrastructure characteristics and related factors affecting micromobility safety and comfort

• Generate Mapping & Diagnostic Outputs: Ensure the software accepts diverse inputs and generates structured, high-quality data outputs optimized for spatial mapping, risk diagnosis, and downstream predictive safety modelling

• Collaborate via Real-World Pilots: Validate and refine the pipeline using real-world data from the project’s pilot cities, working in close coope

Poste de doctorat en analyse du capteur de véhicule et de la télédétection pour la sécurité routière 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Purée La chaire de gestion de l'infrastructure, dirigée par le professeur Bryan T. Adey à l'Institut de construction et de gestion de l'infrastructure du Département de génie civil, environnemental et géomatique, a une ouverture pour un doctorant. Cette position vise à tirer parti des capteurs de véhicules, de la télédétection et de l'apprentissage automatique pour soutenir l'analyse moderne de la sécurité routière urbaine dans le cadre d'un projet plus vaste de l'UE. Contexte du projet Le nouveau projet Horizon de l'UE favorise la mobilité active sûre et la recherche en introduisant une approche axée sur l'homme et fondée sur des données probantes qui intègre la sécurité réelle et perçue des piétons, des cyclistes et des utilisateurs de la micromobilité. Au-delà des approches conventionnelles axées sur les accidents, il capte les quasi-incidents, les interactions dynamiques et les expériences de sécurité incarnées qui façonnent le comportement et le choix du mode. Le projet combine des données multisources sur le trafic, l'infrastructure, les véhicules et la santé avec l'expérimentation immersive eXtended Reality (XR) et l'intelligence artificielle explicable pour analyser des situations critiques en matière de sécurité qui sont rares, sous-déclarées ou impossibles à observer sur le plan éthique dans le trafic réel. L'IA explicable assure la transparence et l'interprétation, appuyant la confiance, la transférabilité et la pertinence des politiques. Le projet traduit ces informations en méthodes d'évaluation harmonisées, en modèles de prévision et en indicateurs validés, permettant une évaluation et une comparaison solides des interventions réglementaires, infrastructurelles, technologiques et comportementales des parties prenantes à l'approche du système sûr. Une attention particulière est accordée aux interactions entre les utilisateurs avec des masses et des vitesses différentes, y compris les vélos électroniques, les vélos e-cargo et les e-cooters, pour la mobilité personnelle et la logistique urbaine. Des projets pilotes de grande envergure dans quatre villes européennes valident des méthodes de trafic réel, soutiennent l'apprentissage interurbain et garantissent leur applicabilité dans des conditions de sécurité, d'infrastructure et de culture diverses. Mis en œuvre par un consortium multidisciplinaire d'ingénierie, de science comportementale, de XR, d'IA, d'urbanisme et de politique, le projet fournit des orientations concrètes et standardisées qui accélèrent des systèmes actifs plus sûrs, plus inclusifs et de micromobilité dans toute l'Europe. La planification de systèmes de transport urbain sûrs est intrinsèquement complexe : les interventions durent des décennies, nécessitent des investissements importants, doivent s'adapter à des espaces restreints et doivent répondre à des besoins changeants des utilisateurs. Les méthodes modernes de collecte de données - telles que les capteurs de véhicules embarqués à haute fréquence et les images de vision par ordinateur - sont bien adaptées pour saisir ces complexités grâce à des aperçus à haute résolution en temps quasi réel. Cependant, la collecte, le traitement et l'opérationnalisation de ces volumes de mégadonnées sont un défi en raison de structures de données hétérogènes et de fortes demandes de calcul. Description de l'emploi Ce doctorat vise à faire progresser l'état de la technique en matière de fusion des données de détection et de télédétection pour l'analyse de la sécurité des infrastructures de transport urbain. Le candidat développera de nouveaux outils et méthodes qui intègrent les mégadonnées, la vision informatique et l'apprentissage automatique. Les principales tâches du candidat seront les suivantes :
• Développer un pipeline de détection évolutive : concevoir et mettre en œuvre une architecture logicielle/outil capable de traiter des flux de données multisources de capteurs, de caméras et de télédétection de véhicules
• Automatiser l'identification des caractéristiques et des facteurs: Train machine learning et les modèles de vision informatique dans le pipeline pour détecter automatiquement les caractéristiques de l'infrastructure bâtie et les facteurs connexes affectant la sécurité et le confort de la micromobilité
• Générer la cartographie et les sorties diagnostiques : s'assurer que le logiciel accepte divers intrants et génère des sorties de données structurées et de haute qualité optimisées pour la cartographie spatiale, le diagnostic des risques et la modélisation de la sécurité prédictive en aval
• Collaborer via Real-World Pilots: Valider et affiner le pipeline à l'aide de données réelles provenant des villes pilotes du projet, en travaillant en coope proche

80%-100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The ETH Zürich Competence Center for Materials and Processes ( MaP ) is a multidisciplinary scientific network devoted to tackling the grand challenges in materials, processes and manufacturing technologies. We foster cross-disciplinary research, education, and outreach to other academic institutes, industry and society in this field. Current major initiatives of MaP are the MaP Doctoral School and ETH Sabbatical | CAS AMaP continuing education programme. To lead the executive office as the central coordination hub, MaP is currently hiring a new Executive Director, starting from 1 July 2026 or earlier on agreement.

Project background

We are seeking an individual who is highly motivated to manage and develop MaP , together with the Steering Committee and the community of over 80 affiliated research groups . The Executive Director is responsible for leading the executive office, including managing strategy, human resources, finances, as well as operations and activities, governance and communications. The main focus of this key interfacing role is on community building and managing multi-stakeholder collaboration across a broad range of themes, therefore requiring a broad understanding of the grand challenges in Materials and Processes. The position embraces the designing, managing and overseeing of all research, education and outreach programs of MaP , including the MaP Doctoral School and ETH Sabbatical | CAS AMaP .

Job description

Strategic Leadership & Office Management

Ricercatori post-dottorali per progetti di 3 anni su reti quantiche e rilevamento quantistico 100%, Zurigo, stampa a tempo fisso Drucken Il Gruppo Ottico Nanomateriale nel Dipartimento di Fisica dell'ETH Zurigo sta cercando due ricercatori Postdoctoral per progetti di 3 anni su reti quantiche e rilevamento quantico. I circuiti integrati fotonici promettono funzionalità avanzate per applicazioni come elaborazione delle informazioni quantiche e rilevamento di precisione. Thin film niobate (TFLN) è una piattaforma fotonica in grado di integrare la conversione di frequenza, sorgenti di luce quantistica e modulazione elettro-ottica ad alta velocità su un singolo dispositivo. Nel Gruppo Ottico Nanomateriale, siamo specializzati nella nanofabrificazione e caratterizzazione ottica dei circuiti fotonici TFLN per applicazioni in ottica non lineare, comunicazione quantistica e rilevamento quantistico. Le posizioni aperte lavoreranno su (1) circuiti TFLN per reti quantiche e (2) circuiti TFLN per il rilevamento quantistico – entrambi i progetti sono lunghi 3 anni.
• Le reti quantistiche comportano l'intreccio di memorie quantistiche distanti, tuttavia molte delle memorie quantistiche principali operano a lunghezze d'onda visibili. Ci proponiamo di utilizzare fotonici TFLN per fonti di fotoni non degenerati impigliati con un fotone alla lunghezza d'onda di memoria quantistica e l'altro fotone nella banda di telecomunicazioni per la trasmissione a lunga distanza su fibra ottica. Questa posizione fa parte di un consorzio svizzero su reti quantiche
• La luce quantistica può migliorare il rilevamento attraverso misurazioni di stima e assorbimento di fase con fotoni non rilevati. Ci proponiamo di utilizzare fotonici TFLN per la generazione di vuoto spremuto per applicazioni di rilevamento del gas, dove le guide d'onda periodicamente inquinate e il rilevamento della risoluzione dei numeri fotonici forniscono un vantaggio quantico. Questa posizione fa parte di un progetto QuantERA con l'Imperial College London, l'Università di Oxford e il profilo ICFO
• Stiamo cercando i Ricercatori Postdoctoral con esperienza nell'area come fotonici integrati, ottica non lineare, fotonica quantistica, informazioni quantistiche e down-conversion parametrico spontaneo
• I Ricercatori Postdoctoral lavoreranno sulla teoria dello sfondo, la simulazione, il design, alcuni aspetti della nanofabrificazione, e informazioni di carattere I Ricercatori Postdoctoral lavoreranno con altri studenti Postdoc e PhD coinvolti nella nanofabricazione e caratterizzazione ottica, e interagiranno con il gruppo attraverso progetti regolari e riunioni di gruppo Le date di inizio di destinazione per queste posizioni sono tra il 2026 ottobre e il gennaio 2027. Postdoctoral Researchers for 3-year projects on quantum networks and quantum sensing

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Optical Nanomaterial Group in the Physics Department at ETH Zurich is looking for Two Postdoctoral Researchers for 3-year projects on quantum networks and quantum sensing.

Job description

Photonic integrated circuits promise advanced functionality for applications such as quantum information processing and precision sensing. Thin film lithium niobate (TFLN) is a maturing photonics platform that can integrate frequency conversion, quantum light sources and high speed electro-optic modulation on a single device.

In the Optical Nanomaterial Group, we specialize in the nanofabrication and optical characterization of TFLN photonic circuits for applications in nonlinear optics, quantum communications and quantum sensing. The open positions will work on (1) TFLN circuits for quantum networks and (2) TFLN circuits for quantum sensing – both projects are 3 years long.

• Quantum networks involve entangling distant quantum memories, however many of the leading quantum memories operate at visible wavelengths. We aim to use TFLN photonics for sources of non-degenerate entangled photon-pairs with one photon at the quantum memory wavelength and the other photon in the telecom band for long distance transmission over optical fiber. This position is part of a Switzerland-wide consortium on quantum networks

• Quantum light can enhance sensing through phase estimation and absorption measurements with undetected photons. We aim to use TFLN photonics for generating squeezed vacuum for gas sensing applications, where periodically poled waveguides and photon number resolution detection provide a quantum advantage. This position is part of a QuantERA project with Imperial College London, the University of Oxford and ICFO

Profile

• We are searching for Postdoctoral Researchers with experience in the area such as integrated photonics, nonlinear optics, quantum photonics, quantum information and spontaneous parametric down-conversion

• The Postdoctoral Researchers will work on the background theory, simulation, design, some aspects of nanofabrication, and characterization of photonic circuits, and perform quantum information experiments

• The Postdoctoral Researchers will work with other Postdocs and PhD students involved in nanofabrication and optical characterization, and will interact with the group via regular project and group meetings

Target start dates for these positions are between October 2026 and January 2027.

Workplace

We offer

• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

• PhD degree

• Contact information of two referees

Job Description Photonische integrierte Schaltungen versprechen fortschrittliche Funktionalität für Anwendungen wie Quanteninformationsverarbeitung und Präzisionssensorik. Dünnfilm-Lithiumniobat (TFLN) ist eine ausgereifte Photonikplattform, die Frequenzumwandlung, Quantenlichtquellen und elektrooptische Hochgeschwindigkeitsmodulation auf einem einzigen Gerät integrieren kann. In der Optical Nanomaterial Group haben wir uns auf die Nanofabrikation und optische Charakterisierung von TFLN-Photonikschaltungen für Anwendungen in der nichtlinearen Optik, Quantenkommunikation und Quantensensorik spezialisiert. Die offenen Stellen werden an (1) TFLN-Schaltungen für Quantennetzwerke und (2) TFLN-Schaltungen für Quantensensorik arbeiten - beide Projekte sind 3 Jahre lang.
• Quantennetzwerke beinhalten die Verschränkung entfernter Quantenspeicher, aber viele der führenden Quantenspeicher arbeiten bei sichtbaren Wellenlängen. Unser Ziel ist es, TFLN-Photonik für Quellen von nicht-degenerierten verschränkten Photonenpaaren mit einem Photon in der Quantenspeicherwellenlänge und dem anderen Photon im Telekommunikationsband für die Fernübertragung über optische Fasern zu verwenden. Diese Position ist Teil eines schweizweiten Konsortiums zu Quantennetzwerken
• Quantenlicht kann die Wahrnehmung durch Phasenschätzung und Absorptionsmessungen mit unentdeckten Photonen verbessern. Unser Ziel ist es, TFLN-Photonik zur Erzeugung von gequetschtem Vakuum für Gassensoranwendungen zu verwenden, bei denen periodisch gepolte Wellenleiter und Photonenzahl-Auflösungserkennung einen Quantenvorteil bieten. Diese Position ist Teil eines QuantERA-Projekts mit dem Imperial College London, der University of Oxford und dem ICFO-Profil

Chercheurs postdoctoraux pour des projets de 3 ans sur les réseaux quantiques et la détection quantique 100%, Zurich, tirage à terme fixe Drucken Le groupe de nanomatériaux optiques du département de physique de l'ETH Zurich recherche deux chercheurs postdoctoraux pour des projets de 3 ans sur les réseaux quantiques et la détection quantique. Description du travail Les circuits intégrés photoniques offrent des fonctionnalités avancées pour des applications telles que le traitement quantique de l'information et la détection de précision. Film mince lithium niobate (TFLN) est une plate-forme photonique mature qui peut intégrer la conversion de fréquence, les sources de lumière quantiques et la modulation électro-optique à grande vitesse sur un seul appareil. Dans le groupe des nanomatériaux optiques, nous nous spécialisons dans la nanofabrication et la caractérisation optique des circuits photoniques TFLN pour des applications dans l'optique non linéaire, les communications quantiques et la détection quantique. Les positions ouvertes travailleront sur (1) les circuits TFLN pour les réseaux quantiques et (2) les circuits TFLN pour la détection quantique – les deux projets sont de 3 ans.
• Les réseaux quantiques impliquent des mémoires quantiques lointaines, mais beaucoup des mémoires quantiques principales fonctionnent à des longueurs d'onde visibles. Nous visons à utiliser la photonique TFLN pour les sources de paires de photons enchevêtrés non dégénérés avec un photon à la longueur d'onde de la mémoire quantique et l'autre photon dans la bande télécom pour la transmission longue distance sur fibre optique. Cette position fait partie d'un consortium suisse sur les réseaux quantiques
• La lumière quantique peut améliorer la détection par des mesures d'estimation et d'absorption de phase avec des photons non détectés. Nous visons à utiliser la photonique TFLN pour générer le vide pressé pour les applications de détection de gaz, où les guides d'ondes périodiquement poolés et la détection de résolution de nombre de photons offrent un avantage quantique. Ce poste fait partie d'un projet QuantERA avec Imperial College London, l'Université d'Oxford et le profil ICFO
• Nous recherchons des chercheurs postdoctoraux ayant une expérience dans le domaine comme la photonique intégrée, l'optique non linéaire, la photonique quantique, l'information quantique et la conversion spontanée en baisse paramétrique
• Les chercheurs postdoctoraux travailleront sur la théorie de fond, la simulation, la conception, certains aspects de la nanofabrication, et la caractérisation des circuits photoniques, et effectueront des expériences d'information quantique
• Les chercheurs postdoctoraux travailleront avec d'autres postdoctorants et doctorants impliqués dans la nanofabrication et la caractérisation optique, et interagiront avec le groupe par le biais de réunions régulières de projets et de groupes. Lieu de travail Nous offrons

descriptionByLocale.en:
Research Assistants (Access to Justice)

10%-30%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Law, Economics, and Data Science research group, headed by Prof. Elliott Ash at ETH Zurich, is seeking Research Assistants (Access to Justice). We are looking for highly motivated law students with an interest in legal technology, artificial intelligence, and access to justice.

The position offers an opportunity to contribute to research on how AI can improve access to legal information and legal services. Research assistants will work closely with faculty members and researchers on projects involving legal datasets, judicial decisions, legislation, and emerging AI tools for legal analysis.

Successful candidates will join an interdisciplinary research team at ETH Zurich working at the intersection of law, data science, and public policy.

Job description

As a student research assistant, you will contribute to a range of research activities, including:

• Gathering, organizing, and digitizing legal materials from legislative, judicial, and archival sources

• Collecting and curating datasets of statutes, regulations, court decisions, and legal scholarship

• Conducting legal and policy research using both traditional legal methods and technology-assisted approaches

• Preparing annotated bibliographies, literature reviews, research memoranda, and concise research summaries

• Supporting the evaluation and validation of AI systems used for legal research, legal information retrieval, and legal analysis

• Assisting with data quality assurance, annotation, and documentation for empirical research projects

• Collaborating with researchers from law, economics, computer science, and related disciplines

Depending on experience and interests, research assistants may also have opportunities to contribute to empirical legal studies, legal data engineering, and the development of AI tools for legal applications.

Profile

We welcome applications from advanced law students, preferably in the later stages of a Bachelor's degree or enrolled in a Master's program.

You are interested in legal research and curious about how new technologies are transforming legal practice, legal institutions, and access to justice. You enjoy working independently while also contributing to collaborative research projects.

Ideally, you bring:

• Strong academic performance in legal studies

• Excellent legal research and writing skills

• Attention to detail and the ability to work carefully with complex legal materials

• A bias to action

• An interest in legal technology, empirical legal research, artificial intelligence, or access-to-justice issues

• Strong organizational skills and reliability in managing research tasks

• Fluency in German and English

• Prior research experience is an advantage but not required

Workplace

We offer

• The opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge research on law, artificial intelligence, and access to justice

• Close collaboration with an international and interdisciplinary team of researchers

• Exposure to empirical legal research methods, legal data analysis, and emerging AI technologies

• Flexible working arrangements that can be combined with academic studies

• Competitive compensation according to ETH Zurich standards

• A dynamic and intellectually stimulating research environment at one of Europe's leading universities

• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

descriptionByLocale.it:
Assistente di ricerca/insegnamento per l'innovazione pedagogica e seminari pratici sui materiali rigenerativi 60%-100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Drucken La cattedra di edilizia sostenibile presso l'ETH di Zurigo intende radicare la sostenibilità nelle discipline dell'ambiente costruito. Puntiamo a settembre 2026 come data di inizio (o previo accordo). La crisi climatica richiede un cambiamento rapido e sistemico nel modo in cui progettiamo, costruiamo e apprendiamo. La cattedra di edilizia sostenibile presso l'ETH di Zurigo è un gruppo di scienziati, ingegneri e architetti che mirano a radicare la sostenibilità nelle discipline dell'ambiente costruito. L'obiettivo è identificare i parametri rilevanti che influenzano gli impatti ambientali degli edifici per implementare pratiche rigenerative attraverso lo sviluppo di strategie innovative adatte a ciascun attore. Implica lavori interdisciplinari e si basa sull'LCA, sul metabolismo urbano e sulla scienza dei materiali. Oltre alla ricerca e alle collaborazioni con l'industria, offriamo workshop sperimentali per studenti (laurea triennale, magistrale) e professionisti (CAS, MAS) per sensibilizzarli e formarli sull'uso di materiali rigenerativi. Negli ultimi 10 anni abbiamo sviluppato contenuti didattici che possono essere caratterizzati come transmateriali e transdisciplinari. Descrizione del lavoro Cerchiamo un collega per rafforzare l'innovazione pedagogica e il programma di educazione pratica sui materiali rigenerativi. La posizione combina pedagogia, sperimentazione, pratica dei materiali e coordinamento: progettare, coordinare e fornire formati di apprendimento sperimentali (2 ore, mezza giornata, giornata intera, una settimana) che traducono la scienza dei materiali in pratica architettonica e ingegneristica.
• Sviluppare una pedagogia coerente fondata su:
• Imparare facendo e sperimentazione iterativa.
• “La materia prima della materia”: comprendere le fasi granulare, fibrosa, legante, molle e acquosa attraverso esperimenti intuitivi, controintuitivi e fenomenologici.
• Esercizi multisensoriali che favoriscono la comprensione intuitiva.
• Ponti visibili-invisibili: strumenti che rivelano comportamenti micro-macro (time-lapse, luce polarizzata, immagini macro) per collegare microstruttura, prestazioni dei materiali e forma strutturale/architettonica.
• Intervento transdisciplinare basato sul gioco di ruolo e sul design thinking
• Co-creare e gestire workshop su terra/argilla, leganti minerali, fibre e altro, inclusa la preparazione dei materiali, protocolli di laboratorio sicuri e logistica (spazio, strumenti, trasporto).
• Costruire e mantenere una libreria digitale e fisica di risorse didattiche: fogli di esperimenti, spiegazioni passo passo e moduli educativi aperti.
• Formazione dei formatori: sostenere il personale dell'ETH, gli assistenti didattici e i partner esterni nell'adozione e nell'adattamento della pedagogia; promuovere la scalabilità e la riproducibilità.
• Contribuire a un insegnamento allineato alla ricerca: collegare gli approfondimenti del workshop con i progetti di cattedra in corso su progettazione del mix, caratterizzazione e ottimizzazione dei processi.
• Aiutare a sviluppare input didattici coerenti per lo sviluppo di materiali adattati alle risorse locali e al pubblico specifico (ingegnere, architetto, impresa di costruzioni). Profilo
• Passione per l'edilizia rigenerativa e il futuro dell'ambiente costruito; entusiasmo per la creazione pratica.
• Interesse per le risorse locali, le tecniche vernacolari e le reinterpretazioni contemporanee che si allineano con la costruzione in scala, circolare e a basse emissioni di carbonio.
• Background accademico o professionale in uno o più tra: architettura, ingegneria civile/dei materiali, scienza dei materiali, progettazione ambientale, formazione nel design o un campo correlato. È valutata la laurea magistrale o il dottorato di ricerca.
• Esperienza dimostrata in:
• Progettazione e fornitura di istruzione superiore sperimentale o formazione professionale.
• Facilitazione di workshop con forti dinamiche di gruppo e cultura della sicurezza.
• Caratterizzazione e formulazione dei materiali (preferibilmente terra/argilla e materiali a base biologica), o capacità di apprendere rapidamente e collaborare a stretto contatto con i ricercatori.
• Creazione di media di apprendimento coinvolgenti (protocolli, immagini, brevi video, time-lap
descriptionByLocale.en:
Research / Teaching Assistant for Pedagogical Innovation and Hands-on Workshops on Regenerative Materials

60%-100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Chair of Sustainable Construction at ETH Zurich intends to ground sustainability in the disciplines of the built environment. We are targeting September 2026 as starting date (or upon agreement).

The climate crisis demands swift, systemic change in how we design, build, and learn. The Chair of Sustainable Construction at ETH Zurich, is a group of scientists, engineers and architects aiming to ground sustainability in the disciplines of the built environment. The objective is to identify the relevant parameters that influence the environmental impacts of buildings to implement regenerative practices throughout the development of innovative strategies adapted to each actor. It involves interdisciplinary works and draws on LCA, urban metabolism and material science.

Alongside research and industry collaborations, we deliver experimental workshops for students (BSc, MSc) and professionals (CAS, MAS) to raise awareness and train them on the use of regenerative materials. Over the last 10 years, we have developed teaching content that can be characterised as trans-material and trans-disciplinary.

Job description

We seek a colleague to strengthen pedagogical innovation and the hands-on education program in regenerative materials. The position combines pedagogy, experimentation, material practice, and coordination: design, coordinate, and deliver experimental learning formats (2h, half-day, full-day, one-week) that translate materials science into architectural and engineering practice.

• Develop a coherent pedagogy grounded in:

• Learning by doing and iterative experimentation.

• “Matter before material”: understanding granular, fibrous, binding, soft and water phases through intuitive, counter-intuitive, and phenomenological experiments.

• Multisensory exercises that foster intuitive understanding.

• Visible-invisible bridges: tools that reveal micro-to-macro behaviour (time-lapse, polarized light, macro imagery) to connect microstructure, material performance, and structural/architectural form.

• Transdisciplinary intervention based on role play and design thinking

• Co-create and run workshops on earth/clay, mineral binders, fibres, and more, including preparation of materials, safe lab protocols, and logistics (space, tools, transport).

• Build and maintain a digital and physical library of teaching resources: experiment sheets, step-by-step explanations, and open educational modules.

• Train-the-trainer: support ETH staff, teaching assistants, and external partners to adopt and adapt the pedagogy; promote scalability and reproducibility.

• Contribute to research-aligned teaching: connect workshop insights with ongoing chair projects on mix design, characterization, and process optimization.

• Help to develop coherent teaching input for material development adapted to local resources and specific public (engineer, architect, construction company)

Profile

• Passion for regenerative construction and the future of the built environment; enthusiasm for hands-on making.

• Interest in local resources, vernacular techniques, and contemporary reinterpretations that align with scale up, circular and low-carbon construction.

• Academic or professional background in one or more of: architecture, civil/material engineering, materials science, environmental design, design education, or a related field. Master or PhD degree is valued.

• Demonstrated experience in:

• Designing and delivering experimental higher education or professional training.

• Workshop facilitation with strong group dynamics and safety culture.

• Material characterization and formulation (preferably earth/clay and biobased materials), or the ability to learn quickly and collaborate closely with researchers.

Forschungs-/Lehrassistent für pädagogische Innovation und praktische Workshops zu regenerativen Materialien 60%-100%, Zürich, befristetes Drucken Drucken Der Lehrstuhl für Nachhaltiges Bauen an der ETH Zürich möchte Nachhaltigkeit in den Disziplinen der gebauten Umwelt verankern. Als Starttermin streben wir September 2026 an (oder nach Vereinbarung). Die Klimakrise erfordert einen schnellen, systemischen Wandel in der Art und Weise, wie wir entwerfen, bauen und lernen. Der Lehrstuhl für Nachhaltiges Bauen an der ETH Zürich ist eine Gruppe von Wissenschaftlern, Ingenieuren und Architekten mit dem Ziel, Nachhaltigkeit in den Disziplinen der gebauten Umwelt zu verankern. Ziel ist es, die relevanten Parameter zu identifizieren, die die Umweltauswirkungen von Gebäuden beeinflussen, um regenerative Praktiken im Zuge der Entwicklung innovativer, an jeden Akteur angepasster Strategien umzusetzen. Es umfasst interdisziplinäre Arbeiten und stützt sich auf Ökobilanz, Stadtstoffwechsel und Materialwissenschaft. Neben Forschungs- und Industriekooperationen bieten wir experimentelle Workshops für Studenten (BSc, MSc) und Fachleute (CAS, MAS) an, um das Bewusstsein für die Verwendung regenerativer Materialien zu schärfen und sie zu schulen. In den letzten 10 Jahren haben wir Lehrinhalte entwickelt, die als transmateriell und transdisziplinär charakterisiert werden können. Stellenbeschreibung Wir suchen einen Kollegen zur Stärkung der pädagogischen Innovation und des praktischen Bildungsprogramms für regenerative Materialien. Die Stelle vereint Pädagogik, Experimentieren, Materialpraxis und Koordination: Entwerfen, Koordinieren und Durchführen experimenteller Lernformate (2 Stunden, halbtags, ganztags, eine Woche), die Materialwissenschaften in die Architektur- und Ingenieurpraxis übersetzen.
• Entwickeln Sie eine kohärente Pädagogik, die auf Folgendem basiert:
• Lernen durch Handeln und iteratives Experimentieren.
• „Materie vor Material“: Verständnis der körnigen, faserigen, bindenden, weichen und wässrigen Phasen durch intuitive, kontraintuitive und phänomenologische Experimente.
• Multisensorische Übungen, die das intuitive Verständnis fördern.
• Sichtbar-unsichtbare Brücken: Werkzeuge, die das Mikro-zu-Makro-Verhalten aufzeigen (Zeitraffer, polarisiertes Licht, Makrobilder), um Mikrostruktur, Materialleistung und strukturelle/architektonische Form zu verbinden.
• Transdisziplinäre Intervention basierend auf Rollenspielen und Design Thinking.
• Gemeinsame Erstellung und Durchführung von Workshops zu Erde/Ton, mineralischen Bindemitteln, Fasern und mehr, einschließlich der Vorbereitung von Materialien, sicheren Laborprotokollen und Logistik (Raum, Werkzeuge, Transport).
• Erstellen und pflegen Sie eine digitale und physische Bibliothek mit Lehrressourcen: Experimentierblätter, Schritt-für-Schritt-Erklärungen und offene Bildungsmodule.
• Train-the-Trainer: Unterstützung von ETH-Mitarbeitern, Lehrassistenten und externen Partnern bei der Übernahme und Anpassung der Pädagogik; fördern Skalierbarkeit und Reproduzierbarkeit.
• Tragen Sie zu einer forschungsorientierten Lehre bei: Verbinden Sie Workshop-Erkenntnisse mit laufenden Lehrstuhlprojekten zu Mischungsdesign, Charakterisierung und Prozessoptimierung.
• Helfen Sie bei der Entwicklung kohärenter Lehrinhalte für die Materialentwicklung, die an lokale Ressourcen und spezifische Zielgruppen (Ingenieur, Architekt, Bauunternehmen) angepasst sind. Profil
• Leidenschaft für regeneratives Bauen und die Zukunft der gebauten Umwelt; Begeisterung für das handwerkliche Gestalten.
• Interesse an lokalen Ressourcen, einheimischen Techniken und zeitgenössischen Neuinterpretationen, die auf Scale-up, zirkuläres und kohlenstoffarmes Bauen ausgerichtet sind.
• Akademischer oder beruflicher Hintergrund in einem oder mehreren der folgenden Bereiche: Architektur, Bau-/Materialtechnik, Materialwissenschaften, Umweltdesign, Designausbildung oder einem verwandten Bereich. Ein Master- oder Ph.D.-Abschluss wird geschätzt.
• Nachgewiesene Erfahrung in:
• Konzeption und Durchführung experimenteller Hochschul- oder Berufsausbildung.
• Workshop-Moderation mit starker Gruppendynamik und Sicherheitskultur.
• Materialcharakterisierung und -formulierung (vorzugsweise Erde/Ton und biobasierte Materialien) oder die Fähigkeit, schnell zu lernen und eng mit Forschern zusammenzuarbeiten.
• Erstellen ansprechender Lernmedien (Protokolle, Bilder, kurze Videos, Zeitraffer).

Assistant de recherche/enseignement pour l'innovation pédagogique et ateliers pratiques sur les matériaux régénératifs 60%-100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken La chaire de construction durable de l'ETH Zurich entend ancrer la durabilité dans les disciplines de l'environnement bâti. Nous visons septembre 2026 comme date de début (ou après accord). La crise climatique exige un changement rapide et systémique dans la façon dont nous concevons, construisons et apprenons. La Chaire de construction durable de l'ETH Zurich est un groupe de scientifiques, d'ingénieurs et d'architectes visant à ancrer la durabilité dans les disciplines de l'environnement bâti. L'objectif est d'identifier les paramètres pertinents qui influencent les impacts environnementaux des bâtiments pour mettre en œuvre des pratiques régénératives tout au long du développement de stratégies innovantes adaptées à chaque acteur. Il implique des travaux interdisciplinaires et s’appuie sur l’ACV, le métabolisme urbain et la science des matériaux. Parallèlement aux collaborations entre la recherche et l'industrie, nous organisons des ateliers expérimentaux destinés aux étudiants (BSc, MSc) et aux professionnels (CAS, MAS) pour les sensibiliser et les former à l'utilisation des matériaux régénératifs. Au cours des 10 dernières années, nous avons développé des contenus pédagogiques que l’on peut qualifier de trans-matériels et trans-disciplinaires. Description du poste Nous recherchons un collègue pour renforcer l'innovation pédagogique et le programme d'éducation pratique sur les matériaux régénératifs. Le poste combine pédagogie, expérimentation, pratique des matériaux et coordination : concevoir, coordonner et dispenser des formats d'apprentissage expérimentaux (2h, demi-journée, journée complète, une semaine) qui traduisent la science des matériaux en pratique de l'architecture et de l'ingénierie.
• Développer une pédagogie cohérente fondée sur :
• L'apprentissage par la pratique et l'expérimentation itérative.
• « La matière avant la matière » : comprendre les phases granulaires, fibreuses, liantes, molles et aqueuses à travers des expériences intuitives, contre-intuitives et phénoménologiques.
• Exercices multisensoriels qui favorisent la compréhension intuitive.
• Ponts visible-invisible : outils qui révèlent le comportement micro-macro (time-lapse, lumière polarisée, macro-imagerie) pour relier la microstructure, la performance des matériaux et la forme structurelle/architecturale.
• Intervention transdisciplinaire basée sur le jeu de rôle et le design thinking.
• Co-créer et animer des ateliers sur la terre/argile, les liants minéraux, les fibres, etc., y compris la préparation des matériaux, les protocoles de laboratoire sécurisés et la logistique (espace, outils, transport).
• Construire et entretenir une bibliothèque numérique et physique de ressources pédagogiques : fiches d'expérimentation, explications étape par étape et modules pédagogiques ouverts.
• Former les formateurs : aider le personnel de l'ETH, les assistants d'enseignement et les partenaires externes à adopter et adapter la pédagogie ; favoriser l’évolutivité et la reproductibilité.
• Contribuer à un enseignement aligné sur la recherche : relier les idées de l'atelier aux projets de chaire en cours sur la conception de mélanges, la caractérisation et l'optimisation des processus.
• Contribuer à développer une offre pédagogique cohérente pour le développement de matériaux adaptés aux ressources locales et à des publics spécifiques (ingénieur, architecte, entreprise de construction). Profil
• Passion pour la construction régénérative et l'avenir de l'environnement bâti ; enthousiasme pour la fabrication pratique.
• Intérêt pour les ressources locales, les techniques vernaculaires et les réinterprétations contemporaines qui s'alignent sur la construction à grande échelle, circulaire et à faible émission de carbone.
• Expérience académique ou professionnelle dans un ou plusieurs des domaines suivants : architecture, génie civil/matériau, science des matériaux, conception environnementale, éducation au design ou domaine connexe. Un diplôme de maîtrise ou de doctorat est valorisé.
• Expérience démontrée dans :
• La conception et la prestation d'un enseignement supérieur expérimental ou d'une formation professionnelle.
• Animation d'ateliers avec une forte dynamique de groupe et une culture de sécurité.
• Caractérisation et formulation de matériaux (de préférence terre/argile et matériaux biosourcés), ou capacité d'apprendre rapidement et de collaborer étroitement avec les chercheurs.
• Création de supports d'apprentissage attrayants (protocoles, visuels, courtes vidéos, time-lap)

descriptionByLocale.en:
PhD Researcher in Trustworthy and Human-Centred AI Development

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The KOF Swiss Economic Institute at the ETH Zurich is the leading institute for applied research in economics in Switzerland.

We are a research group within the KOF Swiss Economic Institute at ETH Zürich. Our work sits at the intersection of economic research and AI: we study money systems and democracies, and we build AI systems that engage with these domains — for research, for policy, and the public. We are now looking for a PhD Researcher who combines strong engineering fundamentals with serious attention to how these systems behave in the world and who they serve.

Job description

As a PhD Researcher, you will pursue independent research on trustworthy and human-centred AI while contributing to the systems we are building in this space. The work spans methodological research and concrete implementation, and treats questions of reliability, accountability, and human-AI interaction as research questions in their own right and not as deployment afterthoughts. You will work alongside researchers and engineers in an international team and will have the room to shape the direction of your own thesis. An example of a system to be developed are trustworthy AI voting assistants in the context of Supported Democracy .

Your responsibilities will include:

• Conducting research on AI reliability, security, trustworthiness, and human-AI interaction, with a focus on high-stakes settings.

• Publishing at top venues in AI and responsible AI research (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, FAccT, EAAMO, AIES, CHI, etc.).

• Designing, building, and iterating prototypes that take their real-world context seriously, including who uses them, under what conditions, and with what consequences.

• Working hands-on with large language models: evaluating their behavior, improving their reliability for concrete use cases, and integrating them into systems with particular attention to security, explainability, and the interaction between humans and AI.

• Contributing to the development of LLM-based systems, including prompting strategies, tool use, evaluation, retrieval-augmented workflows, and adaptation.

• Designing and running user studies to evaluate how people interact with the systems we build, in collaboration with other members of the team.

Profile

We are looking for someone who is technically strong and who is comfortable moving between research, engineering, and the broader questions of how AI systems affect the people and institutions that interact with them.

You should bring:

• A master’s degree in computer science, machine learning, HCI, or a related field.

• Strong foundations in machine learning and familiarity with current AI tools and practices.

• A solid understanding of large language models, in particular their reliability, security, and explainability characteristics.

• Familiarity with the technical and human-factors sides of human–computer interaction.

• The ability to work independently, communicate clearly, and navigate open-ended research question

The following would be a plus:

• Practical experience building with LLM APIs, open models, evaluation pipelines, orchestration frameworks, and related tooling.

• Familiarity with model adaptation, fine-tuning, or related optimization methods.

• Experience with cloud infrastructure, MLOps or LLMOps, containerization, or production deployment.

• Frontend and/or backend development skills.

Workplace

We offer

ETH Zurich offers internationally competitive working conditions. The starting date for this position is August or September 2026 and he position is initially offered for 18 months, with the prospect of extension for the normal four- to five-year duration of the doctorate, subject to satisfactory progress.

We offer the opportunity to pursue a high-quality PhD at renowned institutions in a dynamic and collaborative research environme

We at the Department of Safety, Health and Environment (SGU) advise, support and train all organizational units and members of ETH Zurich on questions relating to safety and health at work. In order to be able to fulfill these tasks professionally and efficiently, we are looking from 1. September 2026 or by arrangement a dedicated personality as section manager training and communication (m/f/d).
