PhD Researcher - Micro-Multiphysics 100%, Singapore, fixed-term Drucken The Singapore-ETH Centre was established in 2010 by ETH Zurich - The Swiss Federal Institute of Technology and Singapore’s National Research Foundation (NRF), as part of the NRF’s CREATE campus. As ETH Zurich's only research centre outside of Switzerland, the centre has strengthened the research capacity of ETH Zurich to develop sustainable solutions to global challenges in Switzerland, Singapore and the surrounding regions. Set in Asia, in a rapidly urbanising region, the Singapore-ETH Centre aims to provide practical solutions to some of the most pressing challenges on urban sustainability, resilience and health through its programmes: Future Cities Lab Global (FCL Global) and Future Health Technologies (FHT) . The centre serves as an intellectual hub for research, bringing together principal investigators and researchers from diverse disciplines and backgrounds. To promote the exchange of ideas and expertise, our researchers actively collaborate with universities and research institutes and engage with industry and government agencies to translate knowledge to practical solutions to real-world problems. Project background Micro-Multiphysics Agent-Based Modelling for Simulation of Patient-Specific Bone Remodelling Fragility fractures are among the most serious consequences of impaired skeletal health in older adults and often lead to reduced mobility, loss of independence, and long-term disability. Although current standards of care provide important tools for assessing skeletal health and fracture risk, they do not fully capture how individual differences in bone remodelling, inflammation, mechanical loading, and biological tissue response influence fracture progression over time. Osteoporosis and related age-associated bone disorders are highly heterogeneous, with patients differing in bone formation capacity, osteoclast activity, inflammatory status, mineralisation dynamics, and capacity for mechanoadaptation. Computational models that integrate these biological and clinical differences could support more personalised strategies for fracture prevention and musculoskeletal care. Building on the dynamic bone organoid culture platform developed in the Laboratory for Bone Biomechanics at ETH Zurich, this project aims to develop micro-multiphysics agent-based models (micro-MPA) that link patient-derived organoid readouts with clinical and imaging data. The doctoral researcher will develop computational workflows to simulate bone remodelling processes, mechanical-cytokine microenvironments, cellular dynamics, and patient-specific fracture risk trajectories. Biological outputs from patient-derived 3D bone organoids, including mineralisation dynamics, osteoclast activity, immune-bone interactions, inflammatory profiles, and mechanical response, will be translated into model parameters and integrated with relevant clinical datasets. The resulting modelling framework will support the prediction of patient-specific bone remodelling trajectories and fracture risk under different biological and mechanical conditions, contributing to data-driven and human-relevant approaches for precision fracture prevention. Junior Administration & Logistics Assistant 100%, Zurigo, permanente stampa Druppo Il governo federale svizzero ha approvato sei nuovi centri nazionali di competenza nella ricerca (NCCR). Questi programmi forniranno una forza a lungo termine per le principali aree di ricerca strategiche in Svizzera. L’ETH di Zurigo è a capo di tre dei sei NCCR approvati, vale a dire il NCCR “Genesis”, e vede questo come una grande opportunità per l’istruzione, la ricerca di alto livello e il trasferimento di conoscenza all’industria e alla società. “Genesi” indaga l’origine della vita come transizione graduale dalla materia inanimata agli organismi viventi. Il centro sarà gestito in stretta collaborazione con l'Università di Losanna (UNIL). Il progetto riunisce più di 100 scienziati provenienti da tutte le parti del paese, colmando il divario tra biologia, chimica, astrofisica, Terra e scienze planetarie. Sfondo del progetto Al fine di rafforzare il piccolo team di progetto e sostenere il Direttore NCCR nei suoi compiti, stiamo stabilendo il nuovo ruolo "Administration & Logistics Assistant". Questa posizione riporta al NCCR Finance & Administration Manager. Descrizione del lavoro
• Fornire un supporto amministrativo generale di giorno per giorno al Finance & Administration Manager, ad esempio il trattamento degli ordini di acquisto, fatture, spese e il monitoraggio delle spese minori
• Organizzare e coordinare la logistica per incontri, workshop, conferenze, recensioni tra cui prenotazioni in camera, viaggi, alloggi, catering e in loco
• Assistenza in on/offboarding del personale dell'ETH di Zurigo (aspetto amministrativo) Profilo
• Hai un diploma commerciale, Matura o Handelsmittelschuldiploma e hai acquisito la prima esperienza di lavoro (probabilmente in un ambiente universitario o di ricerca)
• Esperienza nel trattamento di fatture, spese e ordini di acquisto
• Ottima pianificazione e capacità organizzative, preciso stile di lavoro
• Ottimo scritto e parlato tedesco e inglese
• Atteggiamento pratico e proattivo, affidabile e preciso
• Giocatore di team di mentalità aperta con un interesse per le scienze naturali, specialmente quelle legate alle origini della ricerca sulla vita Luogo di lavoro Offriamo
• Il tuo lavoro con impatto: Diventa parte dell'ETH di Zurigo, che non solo supporta lo sviluppo professionale, ma contribuisce attivamente al cambiamento positivo nella società
• È possibile aspettarsi numerosi vantaggi, come i biglietti per la stagione dei trasporti pubblici e la condivisione delle auto, una vasta gamma di sport offerti dalla ASVZ , l'assistenza all'infanzia e le interessanti prestazioni pensionistiche

ETH Zurich heads three of the six approved NCCRs, namely the NCCR “Genesis”, and sees this as a major opportunity for education, top-level research and knowledge transfer to industry and society. “Genesis” investigates the origin of life as a gradual transition from inanimate matter to living organisms. The project brings together more than 100 scientists from all parts of the country, bridging the gap between biology, chemistry, astrophysics, and Earth and planetary sciences. descriptionByLocale.en:
Financial and administrative officer 60%-80%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The NCCR CLIM+ is a new National Center of Competence in Research that is establishing the first fully interdisciplinary, Switzerland-wide climate research community that tackles pressing issues related to climate extremes such as heatwaves, floods, heavy rainfalls, droughts, wildfires, and further compound events. It will thereby interact with stakeholders ranging from public health to finance, agriculture, and water management. tp produce actionable climate solution pathways related to adaptation and mitigation, forming a new transdisciplinary nexus between science, society, practice, and politics. Project background NCCR CLIM+ is led by ETH Zurich and the University of Bern, and includes 20 partner institutions across Switzerland. At ETH Zurich, NCCR CLIM+ is led by Prof. Sonia I. Seneviratne and Prof. David N. Bresch, with a total involvement of 17 professors and research groups from 8 departments. The other leading house is the University of Bern (co-director: Prof. Karin Ingold; deputy co-director: Prof. Olivia Romppainen-Martius). In total, the NCCR CLIM+ has 57 project partners from a range of institutions from Switzerland. The first phase of NCCR CLIM+ is planned until April 30, 2030, with a possible extension for an additional 4–8 years (up to 12 years in total). NCCR CLIM+ will also lead the development of a newly founded long-term Center for Climate Extremes and Resilience in Swiss Society (CERESS). Further information about NCCR CLIM+ can be found on our website . Job description The Financial and administrative officer position is part of the NCCR CLIM+ Management Center, which is headed by an Executive manager. The Management Center also includes a Communications Officer, as well as Technical and Scientific officers from the NCCR CLIM+. The main responsibilities of the NCCR CLIM+ Financial and administrative officer will be as follows:
• Establishment of the NCCR CLIM+ Management Center at ETH Zurich in collaboration with the Executive Manager, as well as Prof. Sonia I. Seneviratne and Prof. David N. Bresch
• Budget management and accounting of NCCR CLIM+, including distribution and financial controlling of SNSF funds allocated to the principal investigators of NCCR CLIM+
• Budget management and accounting of ETH Zurich funding within NCCR CLIM+, including financial controlling
• Financial reports for SNSF and ETH Zurich
• Financial, human resources, and general administration of the Management Center
• Timely execution of all activities and services in accordance with the SNSF' and ETH Zurich’s guidelines and process requirements
• Correspondence and communication with the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF), ETH Zurich Administration, and NCCR CLIM+ PIs on financial and administrative matters
• Co-organization of site visits, conferences, workshops, reports, and proposals in collaboration with NCCR CLIM+ Executive Manager, as well as Prof. Sonia I. Seneviratne and Prof. David N. Bresch Profile
• Demonstrated expertise and experience in finance management and budget controlling
• High degree of autonomy
• Excellent command of English (written and spoken)
• Excellent command of German (written and spoken)
• Expertise and experience in administrative management (particularly finance and human resources)
• Expertise and experience in event management and reporting
• Solid computer skills (office, internet, budget accounting); ability to use programs and applications to solve complex problems and tasks quickly and independently
• Efficient and precise work style
• Sense of responsibility, quick learner, ability to take initiative, and organizational skills
• Interpersonal skills, flexibility, and ability to work under pressure
• Experience with university administrative processes is a plus
• Experience in the administration of interdisciplinary research projects is a plus
• Teamplayer Workp

descriptionByLocale.it:
Postdoctoral Researcher - Bone Organoids 100%, Singapore, fixed-term Drucken The Singapore-ETH Centre was established in 2010 by ETH Zurich - The Swiss Federal Institute of Technology and Singapore’s National Research Foundation (NRF), as part of the NRF’s CREATE campus. As ETH Zurich's only research centre outside of Switzerland, the centre has strengthened the research capacity of ETH Zurich to develop sustainable solutions to global challenges in Switzerland, Singapore and the surrounding regions. Set in Asia, in a rapidly urbanising region, the Singapore-ETH Centre aims to provide practical solutions to some of the most pressing challenges on urban sustainability, resilience and health through its programmes: Future Cities Lab Global (FCL Global) and Future Health Technologies (FHT) . The centre serves as an intellectual hub for research, bringing together principal investigators and researchers from diverse disciplines and backgrounds. To promote the exchange of ideas and expertise, our researchers actively collaborate with universities and research institutes and engage with industry and government agencies to translate knowledge to practical solutions to real-world problems. Project background Advanced Patient-derived 3D Bone Organoids for Personalised Osteoporosis Drug Screening Fragility fractures remain a major consequence of impaired skeletal health in older adults, frequently resulting in reduced mobility, loss of independence, and long-term disability. While current standards of care provide valuable tools for evaluating skeletal health and fracture risk, they do not fully capture patient-specific biological responses to altered bone remodelling, mechanical loading, inflammation, and pharmacological intervention. Osteoporosis and related age-associated bone disorders are highly heterogeneous, with individuals differing in bone formation capacity, osteoclast activity, inflammatory status, mineralisation dynamics, and mechanoadaptive potential. These biological differences can influence both fracture risk and response to therapy, highlighting the need for human-relevant models that can support more personalised approaches to osteoporosis care. Building on the dynamic bone organoid culture platform developed in the Laboratory for Bone Biomechanics at ETH Zurich, this project aims to further develop and apply patient-derived 3D bone organoid models for in vitro osteoporosis research and personalised drug screening. The postdoctoral researcher will lead the optimisation of workflows to 3D print patient-derived mesenchymal stromal cells, guide osteogenic differentiation under dynamic mechanical stimulation, coculture with peripheral blood mononuclear cells, and assess donor-specific responses to pharmacological interventions. The resulting organoid models will enable the investigation of osteoporosis-related remodelling, immune-bone interactions, age-related comorbidity effects, and personalised drug-response profiles. Biological readouts from these models will contribute to predictive modelling frameworks for bone remodelling trajectories, treatment response, and fracture risk, supporting the advancement of precision musculoskeletal care. Job description The Postdoctoral researcher will interact closely with engineers, clinicians, biologists, computational researchers, to generate robust biological datasets for personalised modelling of bone remodelling drug response, and fracture prevention. Some key components in the work are:
• Development, optimisation, and standardisation of patient-derived 3D bone organoid models for in vitro osteoporosis research and personalised drug screening.
• Establishment of workflows to integrate peripheral blood mononuclear cells into bone organoids to model immune-bone interactions, monocyte-derived osteoclast activity, inflammation, and bone remodelling.

descriptionByLocale.it:
Scienziato fondatore - Anticorpo/Nanobody Drug Discovery 100%, Basilea, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Il gruppo del Prof. Andreas Moor (D-BSSE, ETH Zurich, situato a Basilea) è alla ricerca di uno scienziato eccezionale e di mentalità imprenditoriale per guidare un programma anticorpo/nanocorpo di prevenzione della metastasi-colorettale-cancro dalla scoperta verso la clinica (iniziare immediatamente o per accordo). Il vostro cammino: dalla comunione alla fondazione Nel corso dei 12 mesi si guida il programma anticorpo verso i dati di livello investitore e una proprietà IP rafforzata, lavorando hands-on con la nostra rete di traduzione. Il percorso previsto per la persona giusta è quello di crescere in un ruolo fondante e scientifico-leadership nell'impresa come prende forma. Sfondo del progetto Si lavorerà alla convergenza della ricerca fondamentale e dello sviluppo traduttivo, avanzando leganti nanocorpo/anticorpo contro un obiettivo validato e rilevante nella metastasi del colorettale-cancro (costruire sul proprio lavoro di scoperta pubblicato del laboratorio) dalla scoperta precoce verso un robusto pacchetto preclinico e IP. Le responsabilità includono la scoperta, lo screening rigoroso e la caratterizzazione dettagliata di nuovi leganti proteici, in un ambiente che tratta la traduzione, l'IP e la formazione di impresa come parte della disciplina scientifica. Accogliamo i candidati con un MSc o PhD in biotecnologia, biologia molecolare, scienza delle proteine, o un campo correlato, desiderosi di applicare le loro competenze alle sfide ad alto impatto. L'esperienza precedente con l'ingegneria delle proteine, le tecnologie di visualizzazione (esposizione di sangue, lievito o ribosome), o test basati sulle cellule è vantaggiosa. Descrizione del lavoro
• Sperimentazione: progettazione ed esecuzione di studi per sviluppare e caratterizzare nuovi anticorpi e nanobodies.
• Ottimizzazione: applicare biologia molecolare e ingegneria delle proteine per migliorare i leganti per affinità, specificità e stabilità.
• Sviluppo del saggio: creare e convalidare saggi organoidi a base cellulare per valutare il potenziale terapeutico e definire la finestra terapeutica.
• Proprietà traduttiva: contribuire a trasferire la tecnologia, la proprietà intellettuale (divulgazione dell'invenzione, revisione della letteratura FTO), e l'evoluzione della pipeline terapeutica - tra cui la preparazione dei materiali per, e la partecipazione a, tech-transfer, partner, e discussioni degli investitori.
• Team: supervisionare e mentore un tecnico di ricerca, assumendo la responsabilità della produzione di un piccolo team. Profilo
• MSc o PhD in un campo rilevante, con una comprovata registrazione manuale nei flussi di lavoro rilevanti.
• Forza tecnica attraverso: ingegneria proteica e purificazione; saggi di visualizzazione (fissaggio, lievito, o ribosome); ELISA e BLI; citometria di flusso, ordinamento cellulare, microscopia di fluorescenza; cultura cellulare mammifero.
• Creatività e pensiero "out-of-the-box"; capacità di operare sotto pressione e fornire alla linea temporale e al budget.
• L'esposizione regolatrice/droga-sviluppo e l'esperienza di sperimentazione animale sono un vantaggio. Questo ruolo è personalizzato per gli scienziati che
• Sono appassionati di terapeutici anticorpo/nanocorpo e vogliono vedere la ricerca evolversi in soluzioni cliniche tangibili.
• Sono eccitati dalla proprietà e guidando un progetto avanti sotto incertezza del mondo reale.
• Valore un ambiente in cui l'indagine scientifica incontra lo sviluppo strategico (IP, spinoff e commercializzazione) e desidera l'esposizione hands-on ad esso. Luogo di lavoro Offriamo
• Un percorso di fondazione concreto: un programma già sulla pista di spinoff, e l'opportunità esplicita di crescere in un ruolo fondante, scientifico-leadership come incorpora.
• Esposizione manuale allo sviluppo IP, trasferimento tecnologico, strategia di brevetto e formazione di impresa - formazione di società di apprendimento dall'interno di un programma dal vivo, accanto alla nostra rete permanente.
• Un team di ricerca traduttiva pionieristico con un percorso chiaro dalla scoperta allo sviluppo della droga.
• Un ambiente interdisciplinare accanto a esperti accademici e industriali, e la reale proprietà di un programma con potenziale traduttivo e commerciale. chevron right Lavoro, insegnamento e ricerca presso l'ETH di Zurigo Valoriamo di
descriptionByLocale.en:
Founding Scientist - Antibody/Nanobody Drug Discovery 100%, Basel, fixed-term print Drucken The group of Prof. Andreas Moor (D-BSSE, ETH Zurich, located in Basel) is seeking an exceptional, entrepreneurially minded scientist to drive a colorectal-cancer metastasis-prevention antibody/nanobody program from discovery toward the clinic (start immediately or by arrangement). Your path: from fellowship to founding Over the 12 months you will drive the antibody program toward investor-grade data and a strengthened IP estate, working hands-on with our translational network. The intended path for the right person is to grow into a founding and scientific-leadership role in the venture as it takes shape. Project background You will work at the convergence of fundamental research and translational development, advancing nanobody/antibody binders against a validated, disease-relevant target in colorectal-cancer metastasis (building on the lab's own published discovery work) from early discovery toward a robust preclinical and IP package. Responsibilities include discovery, rigorous screening, and detailed characterization of novel protein binders,in an environment that treats translation, IP, and venture formation as part of the scientific discipline. We welcome candidates with an MSc or PhD in biotechnology, molecular biology, protein science, or a related field, eager to apply their expertise to high-impact challenges. Prior experience with protein engineering, display technologies (phage, yeast, or ribosome display), or cell-based assays is advantageous. Job description
• Experimentation: design and execute studies to develop and characterize novel antibodies and nanobodies.
• Optimization: apply molecular biology and protein engineering to enhance binders for affinity, specificity, and stability.
• Assay development: create and validate cell-based / organoid assays to assess therapeutic potential and define the therapeutic window.
• Translational ownership: contribute hands-on to technology transfer, intellectual property (invention disclosures, FTO literature review), and the evolution of the therapeutic pipeline - including preparing materials for, and participating in, tech-transfer, partner, and investor discussions.
• Team: supervise and mentor a research technician, taking responsibility for a small team's output. Profile
• MSc or PhD in a relevant field, with a proven hands-on track record in the relevant workflows.
• Technical strength across: protein engineering and purification; display assays (phage, yeast, or ribosome); ELISA and BLI; flow cytometry, cell sorting, fluorescence microscopy; mammalian cell culture.
• Creativity and "out-of-the-box" thinking; ability to operate under pressure and deliver to timeline and budget.
• Regulatory/drug-development exposure and animal-experimentation experience are a plus. This role is tailored for scientists who
• Are passionate about antibody/nanobody therapeutics and want to see research evolve into tangible clinical solutions.
• Are energised by ownership and by driving a project forward under real-world uncertainty.
• Value an environment where scientific inquiry meets strategic development (IP, spinoffs, and commercialization) and want hands-on exposure to it. Workplace Workplace We offer
• A concrete founding path: a program already on the spinoff track, and the explicit opportunity to grow into a founding, scientific-leadership role as it incorporates.
• Hands-on exposure to IP development, tech transfer, patent strategy, and venture formation - learning company-building from inside a live program, alongside our standing network.
• A pioneering translational research team with a clear path from discovery to drug development.
• An interdisciplinary environment alongside academic and industry experts, and real ownership of a program with translational and commercial potential. chevron_right Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value di

descriptionByLocale.it:
Ricercatore post-dottorato in ottimizzazione per robusti orari ferroviari 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Nonostante l'eccellente qualità dei sistemi di trasporto pubblico in Svizzera, il sistema ferroviario deve aumentare le sue prestazioni (qualità, ad esempio, tempi di viaggio e ritardi) e la capacità (importo dei servizi gestiti) e attirare più viaggiatori per soddisfare gli obiettivi ambiziosi da obiettivi politici e ambientali. Un aspetto chiave dei tradizionali sistemi di trasporto ferroviario è il loro piano, che si basa su percorsi predeterminati, linee e tempi programmati, con poca possibilità di adattarsi a circostanze non pianificate e inaspettate. D'altra parte, ritardi e interruzioni potrebbero influenzare molti servizi in tutta una rete per mezzo di propagazione. Il progetto si concentra sulla pianificazione degli orari che è in grado di minimizzare i ritardi e i loro impatti. Per farlo, l'ottimizzazione su larga scala affronta il problema del timetabling ferroviario. In genere vengono utilizzati approcci di programmazione lineare Integer Misti, matematicamente complessi, e con alcuni limiti, quando si modella la complessità della vita reale. Incorporare robustezza contro ritardi è un ulteriore aspetto importante. Questo progetto presuppone che siamo in grado di quantificare come piccoli ritardi si sviluppano e si propagano in tutta la rete; come le interruzioni più grandi si sviluppano e si propagano nella rete. Dato questo, vogliamo determinare orari robusti, con una scelta adeguata di buffer e riserve di tempo di esecuzione. Quei orari, in ritardo, sono in grado di eseguire quantitativamente meglio (cioè meno ritardi, meno ritardi,...). Questa posizione sarà disponibile, con una data di partenza ideale tra il settembre 2026 e l'aprile 2027, o più avanti d'accordo; la durata prevista del contratto iniziale è di un anno, da estendere sulla base di prestazioni di successo, fino a 2 anni. Sfondo del progetto L'obiettivo di questo progetto è capire come si verificano ritardi e si propagano in una rete ferroviaria di vita reale. Questo espone alcune dinamiche complesse come risposta ad eventi esterni (piccoli ritardi, interruzioni più grandi), e qualche impatto, che può essere caratterizzato da modelli di simulazione. La sfida scientifica consiste nella progettazione di modelli di timetabling in grado di affrontare la complessità delle dinamiche di sistema esistenti, in una varietà di aspetti integrativi. Il progetto è progettato in collaborazione con i player del settore che operano come responsabile delle infrastrutture ferroviarie. Le basi di progetto sui risolutori disponibili per il timetabling non periodico, che includono gli approcci MILP e Logic-Based Benders-Decomposition. Questa ricerca si svolge all'interno di una cooperazione internazionale con il gruppo Complex Systems dell'Università Utrecht, nei Paesi Bassi. Descrizione del lavoro
• espandere e consolidare i modelli di timetabling esistenti per includere vincoli da risorse limitate; e dinamiche complesse derivanti da scelte variabili.
• espandere la portata dei modelli di programmazione per affrontare i problemi multi oggettivi, e le funzioni oggettive non-scalari (come la probabilità di ritardi).
• studiare gli impatti locali e sistemici degli orari quando esposti alle dinamiche di ritardo previste o speculative. Profilo Idealmente, hai (o stai per ricevere) un Dottorato in scienze dei trasporti, scienze della gestione / decisioni, matematica applicata, econometria, statistiche, informatica, fisica o campi correlati. La vostra pista di ricerca è coerente e mostra un track record, o un potenziale chiaro, per analizzare, modellare, controllare e ottimizzare i sistemi di trasporto. Sei altamente motivato e auto-guidato, con una chiara visione di ricerca, ambizione accademica, e eccellenti capacità di comunicazione e scrittura (il fluente parlato e scritto inglese è obbligatorio). • Scienza informatica e capacità di programma software indipendente complesso
• Capacità di modellare e lavorare con design algoritmico, software e dati esistenti forniti da partner industriali
• Conoscenza delle scienze matematiche di ottimizzazione (MILP, IP, LP) e/o controllo
• Lavoro di squadra e commun
descriptionByLocale.en:
Postdoctoral researcher in optimization for robust railway timetables 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken Despite the excellent quality of public transport systems in Switzerland, the railway system needs to increase its performance (quality, for instance, travel time, and delays) and capacity (amount of services run) and attract more travellers to match the ambitious targets from policy and environmental goals. One key aspect of traditional railway transport systems is their plan, which is based on predetermined routes, lines, and scheduled times, with little possibility of adjusting to unplanned and unexpected circumstances. On the other hand, delays and disruption might affect many services throughout a network by means of propagation. The project focuses on timetable planning that is able to minimize delays and their impacts. To do so, large-scale optimisation addresses the railway timetabling problem. Typically Mixed Integer Linear Programming approaches are used, which are mathematically complex, and with some limits, when modelling real-life complexity. Incorporating robustness against delays is an additional important aspect. This project assumes that we are able to quantify how small delays develop and propagate throughout the network; how larger disruptions develop and propagate in the network. Given this, we want to determine robust timetables, with suitable choice of buffers and running time reserves. Those timetables, under delays, are able to perform quantitatively better (i.e. less delays, fewer larger delays,...). This position will be available, with an ideal starting date between September 2026 and April 2027, or further upon agreement; the planned duration of the initial contract is one year, to be extended based on successful performance, for up to 2 years. Project background The focus of this project is to understand how delays occur and propagate in a real-life railway network. This exposes some complex dynamics as response to external events (small delays, larger disruptions), and some impact, which can be characterized by simulation models. The scientific challenge involves designing timetabling models that can deal with the complexity of existing system dynamics, in a variety of integrative aspects. The project is designed in collaboration with industry player operating as railway infrastructure manager. The project bases on available solvers for non-periodic timetabling, which include MILP and Logic-Based Benders-Decomposition approaches. This research is carried out within an international cooperation with the Complex Systems group at Utrecht University, in the Netherlands. Job description
• expand and consolidate existing timetabling models to include constraints from limited resources; and complex dynamics resulting from variable choices.
• expand scope of scheduling models to tackle multi objective problems, and non-scalar objective functions (like probability of delays).
• study local and systemic impacts of timetables when exposed to expected or speculative delay dynamics. Profile Ideally, you have (or are about to receive) a Doctoral Degree in transport sciences, management/ decision sciences, applied mathematics, econometrics, statistics, computer science, physics or related fields. Your research track is consistent and shows a track record, or clear potential, for analysing, modelling, control, and optimisation of transport systems. You are highly motivated and self-driven, with a clear research vision, academic ambition, and excellent communication and writing skills (fluent spoken and written English is mandatory). Moreover, the following skills are expected of a promising candidate:
• Computer science and ability to program independently complex software
• Ability to model and work with algorithmic design, existing software and data provided by industrial partners
• Knowledge of mathematical optimisation (MILP, IP, LP) and/or control sciences
• Team working and commun

Fahrzeit, Verzögerungen) und Kapazität (die Zahl der Dienstleistungen) erhöhen und Reisende mehr anlocken, um den ambitionierten Zielen von politischen und umweltpolitischen Zielen gerecht zu werden. Auf der anderen Seite könnten Verzögerungen und Störungen viele Dienste in einem Netzwerk durch Verbreitung beeinflussen. Das Projekt konzentriert sich auf die Planung von Fahrplänen, die Verzögerungen und deren Auswirkungen minimieren können. Zu diesem Zweck befasst sich die groß angelegte Optimierung mit dem eisenbahnbrechenden Problem. Typischerweise werden gemischte Integer Linear Programming-Ansätze verwendet, die mathematisch komplex sind und mit einigen Grenzen, bei der Modellierung der realen Komplexität. Ein weiterer wichtiger Aspekt ist die Robustheit gegen Verzögerungen. Dieses Projekt geht davon aus, dass wir in der Lage sind, zu quantifizieren, wie sich kleine Verzögerungen im gesamten Netzwerk entwickeln und propagieren; wie sich größere Störungen im Netzwerk entwickeln und propagieren. Dabei wollen wir robuste Zeitpläne mit geeigneter Wahl von Puffern und Laufzeitreserven bestimmen. Diese Zeitpläne können unter Verzögerungen quantitativ besser durchgeführt werden (d.h. weniger Verzögerungen, weniger größere Verzögerungen,...). Diese Position wird mit einem idealen Starttermin zwischen dem 20. September 2026 und dem 20. April 27 oder weiter nach Vereinbarung zur Verfügung stehen; die geplante Laufzeit des ersten Vertrags beträgt ein Jahr, um auf Basis erfolgreicher Leistungen um bis zu 2 Jahre verlängert zu werden. Dies zeigt einige komplexe Dynamiken als Reaktion auf externe Ereignisse (kleine Verzögerungen, größere Störungen) und einige Auswirkungen, die durch Simulationsmodelle charakterisiert werden können. Die wissenschaftliche Herausforderung besteht darin, Zeiterfassungsmodelle zu entwerfen, die sich mit der Komplexität bestehender Systemdynamik in unterschiedlichen integrativen Aspekten befassen können. Das Projekt ist in Zusammenarbeit mit dem als Eisenbahninfrastrukturmanager tätigen Industrieplayer konzipiert. Das Projekt basiert auf verfügbaren Solvents für nicht-periodische Zeitvertreibungen, darunter MILP und Logic-Based Benders-Decomposition Ansätze. Diese Forschung wird in einer internationalen Zusammenarbeit mit der Gruppe Complex Systems an der Universität Utrecht in den Niederlanden durchgeführt. Jobbeschreibung
• Ausbau und Konsolidierung bestehender Zeiterfassungsmodelle, um Einschränkungen aus begrenzten Ressourcen einzubeziehen; und komplexe Dynamiken, die sich aus variablen Entscheidungen ergeben.
• den Umfang der Planungsmodelle erweitern, um mehr objektive Probleme zu lösen, und nicht-skalare objektive Funktionen (wie Wahrscheinlichkeit von Verzögerungen).
• lokale und systemische Auswirkungen von Fahrplänen zu untersuchen, wenn sie einer erwarteten oder spekulativen Verzögerungsdynamik ausgesetzt sind. Profil Idealerweise haben Sie einen Doktorandenabschluss in Transportwissenschaften, Management/Entscheidungswissenschaften, angewandte Mathematik, Ökonometrie, Statistik, Informatik, Physik oder verwandten Bereichen. Sie sind hoch motiviert und selbstfahrend, mit einer klaren Forschungsvision, akademischem Ehrgeiz und exzellenten Kommunikations- und Schreibfähigkeiten ( fließendes gesprochenes und geschriebenes Englisch ist obligatorisch). Darüber hinaus werden folgende Fähigkeiten von einem vielversprechenden Kandidaten erwartet:
• Informatik und Fähigkeit, unabhängig komplexe Software zu programmieren
• Fähigkeit, mit algorithmischem Design, bestehender Software und Daten von Industriepartnern zu modellieren und zu arbeiten
• Kenntnisse der mathematischen Optimierung (MILP, IP, LP) und/oder Kontrollwissenschaften
• Teamarbeit und Kommun

Chercheur postdoctoral en optimisation pour des horaires ferroviaires robustes 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Purée Malgré l'excellente qualité des systèmes de transport en commun en Suisse, le système ferroviaire doit améliorer ses performances (qualité, par exemple, temps de déplacement et retards) et sa capacité (nombre de services offerts) et attirer davantage de voyageurs pour atteindre les objectifs ambitieux de politique et d'environnement. Un aspect clé des systèmes de transport ferroviaire traditionnels est leur plan, qui est basé sur des itinéraires, des lignes et des horaires prédéterminés, avec peu de possibilités d'adaptation aux circonstances imprévues et imprévues. D'autre part, les retards et les perturbations pourraient affecter de nombreux services à travers un réseau par la propagation. Le projet met l'accent sur la planification du calendrier qui permet de minimiser les retards et leurs répercussions. Pour ce faire, l'optimisation à grande échelle s'attaque au problème de la chronologie ferroviaire. Les approches de programmation linéaire intégrales généralement mixtes sont utilisées, qui sont mathématiquement complexes, et avec certaines limites, lors de la modélisation de la complexité de la vie réelle. L'incorporation de la robustesse contre les retards est un autre aspect important. Ce projet suppose que nous sommes en mesure de quantifier la façon dont les petits retards se développent et se propagent dans l'ensemble du réseau; comment les perturbations plus importantes se développent et se propagent dans le réseau. Compte tenu de cela, nous voulons déterminer des calendriers robustes, avec un choix approprié de tampons et de réserves de temps de fonctionnement. Ces délais, en raison de retards, sont en mesure d'améliorer quantitativement (c'est-à-dire moins de retards, moins de retards plus importants,...). Ce poste sera disponible, avec une date de début idéale entre septembre 2026 et avril 2027, ou plus tard après accord; la durée prévue du contrat initial est d'un an, à prolonger sur la base d'une performance réussie, pour une durée maximale de deux ans. Contexte du projet Ce projet vise à comprendre comment les retards se produisent et se propagent dans un réseau ferroviaire réel. Cela expose certaines dynamiques complexes comme réponse à des événements externes (petits retards, perturbations plus importantes) et certains impacts, qui peuvent être caractérisés par des modèles de simulation. Le défi scientifique consiste à concevoir des modèles chronométrés qui peuvent traiter de la complexité de la dynamique du système existante, sous divers aspects intégratifs. Le projet est conçu en collaboration avec les acteurs de l'industrie qui travaillent comme gestionnaire de l'infrastructure ferroviaire. Le projet s'appuie sur des résolveurs disponibles pour l'établissement de délais non périodiques, qui comprennent les approches MILP et Benders-Decomposition basées sur la logique. Ces recherches sont menées dans le cadre d'une coopération internationale avec le groupe des systèmes complexes de l'Université d'Utrecht, aux Pays-Bas. Description de l'emploi
• développer et consolider les modèles de calendrier existants afin d'y inclure les contraintes découlant de ressources limitées et la dynamique complexe résultant de choix variables.
• élargir la portée des modèles de programmation pour s'attaquer aux problèmes multi-objectifs et aux fonctions objectives non scalaires (comme la probabilité de retards).
• étudier les impacts locaux et systémiques des calendriers lorsqu'ils sont exposés à une dynamique de retard prévisible ou spéculative. Profil Idéalement, vous avez (ou êtes sur le point de recevoir) un doctorat en sciences des transports, de la gestion/de la décision, mathématiques appliquées, économétrie, statistiques, informatique, physique ou domaines connexes. Votre parcours de recherche est cohérent et montre un parcours, ou un potentiel clair, pour l'analyse, la modélisation, le contrôle et l'optimisation des systèmes de transport. Vous êtes très motivé et autodidacte, avec une vision de recherche claire, l'ambition académique, et d'excellentes compétences de communication et d'écriture (l'anglais parlé et écrit est obligatoire). En outre, les compétences suivantes sont attendues d'un candidat prometteur:
• Informatique et capacité à programmer des logiciels complexes indépendants
• Capacité de modéliser et de travailler avec la conception algorithmique, les logiciels existants et les données fournies par les partenaires industriels
• Connaissance de l'optimisation mathématique (MILP, IP, LP) et/ou des sciences de contrôle
• Travail d'équipe et communauté

Doktorand in der Optimierung für robuste Bahnfahrpläne 100%, Zürich, befristet Drucken Drucken Trotz der ausgezeichneten Qualität der öffentlichen Verkehrssysteme in der Schweiz muss das Eisenbahnsystem seine Leistungsfähigkeit (z.B. Fahrzeit, Verzögerungen) und Kapazität (die Zahl der Dienstleistungen) erhöhen und Reisende mehr anlocken, um den ambitionierten Zielen von politischen und umweltpolitischen Zielen gerecht zu werden. Ein wesentlicher Aspekt der traditionellen Eisenbahnverkehrssysteme ist ihr Plan, der auf vorgegebenen Strecken, Linien und geplanten Zeiten basiert, mit wenig Möglichkeit, sich auf unplanmäßige und unerwartete Umstände einzustellen. Auf der anderen Seite könnten Verzögerungen und Störungen viele Dienste in einem Netzwerk durch Verbreitung beeinflussen. Das Projekt konzentriert sich auf die Planung von Fahrplänen, die Verzögerungen und deren Auswirkungen minimieren können. Zu diesem Zweck befasst sich die groß angelegte Optimierung mit dem eisenbahnbrechenden Problem. Typischerweise werden gemischte Integer Linear Programming-Ansätze verwendet, die mathematisch komplex sind und mit einigen Grenzen, bei der Modellierung der realen Komplexität. Ein weiterer wichtiger Aspekt ist die Robustheit gegen Verzögerungen. Dieses Projekt geht davon aus, dass wir in der Lage sind, zu quantifizieren, wie sich kleine Verzögerungen im gesamten Netzwerk entwickeln und propagieren; wie sich größere Störungen im Netzwerk entwickeln und propagieren. Dabei wollen wir robuste Zeitpläne mit geeigneter Wahl von Puffern und Laufzeitreserven bestimmen. Diese Zeitpläne können unter Verzögerungen quantitativ besser durchgeführt werden (d.h. weniger Verzögerungen, weniger größere Verzögerungen,...). Diese Position wird verfügbar sein, mit einem idealen Starttermin zwischen August 2026 und Februar 2027, oder weiter nach Vereinbarung; die geplante Dauer des ersten Vertrags beträgt 18 Monate, danach wird ein Eignungskolloquium die weitere Fortsetzung des Promotionsprojekts bestimmen. Das gesamte Promotionsprojekt soll in insgesamt 4 Jahren abgeschlossen werden. Projekt Hintergrund Der Schwerpunkt dieses Projekts ist zu verstehen, wie unterschiedliche Zeitpläne zu komplexen Dynamiken führen, als Reaktion auf externe Ereignisse (kleine Verzögerungen, größere Störungen). Die wissenschaftliche Herausforderung besteht darin, diese Dynamik in bestehende Zeitvertreibsmodelle zu integrieren, um jene Zeitpläne zu identifizieren, die tatsächlich besser sind, unter Verzögerungen. Diese Forschung zielt auf die Verbesserung der Zeitplanplanungsmodelle, die Anpassung der Menge und Platzierung von Puffern und Reservezeiten. Das Projekt ist in Zusammenarbeit mit dem als Eisenbahninfrastrukturmanager tätigen Industrieplayer konzipiert. Das Projekt basiert auf verfügbaren Solvents für nicht-periodische Zeitvertreibungen, darunter MILP und Logic-Based Benders-Decomposition Ansätze. Diese Forschung wird in einer internationalen Zusammenarbeit mit der Gruppe Complex Systems an der Universität Utrecht in den Niederlanden durchgeführt. Jobbeschreibung
• Erstellung und Nutzung von mathematischen Modellen für die umfassende Zeitplanung, mit Einschränkungen für Fahrzeuge, Besatzung und Infrastruktur, in der Lage, die Platzierung von Puffern
• Entwurf und Umsetzung einer Simulationsoptimierungs-Ansicht zur Bewertung von zeltativen Lösungen unter Berücksichtigung der geschätzten Verzögerungsdynamik und der möglichen Umplanungsgrade, um die Robustheit gegenüber kleinen und großen Verzögerungen proaktiv und reaktiv zu verbessern.
• die Nützlichkeit der vorgeschlagenen Entscheidung quantitativ zu verstehen, ihre Empfindlichkeit auf die betrachteten Annahmen zu schätzen; und im Vergleich zur typischen Reaktion im realen Leben Profil Idealerweise haben Sie (oder sind über zu empfangen) einen Master-Abschluss in Transportwissenschaften, Management / Entscheidungswissenschaften, Ökonometrie, Mathematik, Statistik, Informatik, Physik oder verwandten Bereichen. Ihr Forschungspfad ist konsistent und zeigt einen Rekord oder ein klares Potenzial für die Analyse, Modellierung, Steuerung und Optimierung von Transportsystemen. Sie sind hoch motiviert und selbstfahrend, mit einer klaren Forschungsvision, akademischem Ehrgeiz und exzellenten Kommunikations- und Schreibfähigkeiten ( fließendes gesprochenes und geschriebenes Englisch ist obligatorisch). Chercheur au doctorat en optimisation pour des horaires ferroviaires robustes 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Purée Malgré l'excellente qualité des systèmes de transport en commun en Suisse, le système ferroviaire doit améliorer ses performances (qualité, par exemple, temps de déplacement et retards) et sa capacité (nombre de services offerts) et attirer davantage de voyageurs pour atteindre les objectifs ambitieux de politique et d'environnement. Un aspect clé des systèmes de transport ferroviaire traditionnels est leur plan, qui est basé sur des itinéraires, des lignes et des horaires prédéterminés, avec peu de possibilités d'adaptation aux circonstances imprévues et imprévues. D'autre part, les retards et les perturbations pourraient affecter de nombreux services à travers un réseau par la propagation. Le projet met l'accent sur la planification du calendrier qui permet de minimiser les retards et leurs répercussions. Pour ce faire, l'optimisation à grande échelle s'attaque au problème de la chronologie ferroviaire. Les approches de programmation linéaire intégrales généralement mixtes sont utilisées, qui sont mathématiquement complexes, et avec certaines limites, lors de la modélisation de la complexité de la vie réelle. L'incorporation de la robustesse contre les retards est un autre aspect important. Ce projet suppose que nous sommes en mesure de quantifier la façon dont les petits retards se développent et se propagent dans l'ensemble du réseau; comment les perturbations plus importantes se développent et se propagent dans le réseau. Compte tenu de cela, nous voulons déterminer des calendriers robustes, avec un choix approprié de tampons et de réserves de temps de fonctionnement. Ces délais, en raison de retards, sont en mesure d'améliorer quantitativement (c'est-à-dire moins de retards, moins de retards plus importants,...). Ce poste sera disponible, avec une date de début idéale entre août 2026 et février 2027, ou après accord; la durée prévue du contrat initial est de 18 mois, après quoi un colloque d'aptitude déterminera la poursuite du projet de doctorat. Le projet de doctorat total devrait être terminé en 4 ans au total. Contexte du projet Ce projet vise à comprendre comment les différents calendriers entraînent une dynamique complexe en réponse à des événements externes (petits retards, perturbations plus importantes). Le défi scientifique consiste à intégrer ces dynamiques dans les modèles de calendrier existants, afin d'identifier les calendriers qui sont en fait meilleurs, en cas de retard. Cette recherche vise l'amélioration des modèles de planification du calendrier, l'ajustement du montant et de l'emplacement des tampons, et les temps de réserve. Le projet est conçu en collaboration avec les acteurs de l'industrie qui travaillent comme gestionnaire de l'infrastructure ferroviaire. Le projet s'appuie sur des résolveurs disponibles pour l'établissement de délais non périodiques, qui comprennent les approches MILP et Benders-Decomposition basées sur la logique. Ces recherches sont menées dans le cadre d'une coopération internationale avec le groupe des systèmes complexes de l'Université d'Utrecht, aux Pays-Bas. Description de l'emploi
• établir et utiliser des modèles mathématiques pour l'établissement de calendriers à grande échelle, avec des contraintes sur les véhicules, l'équipage et l'infrastructure, capables de régler le placement des tampons
• concevoir et mettre en œuvre une simulation-optimisation pour évaluer les solutions provisoires, en tenant compte de la dynamique estimée des retards et des degrés possibles de rééchelonnement, afin d'améliorer de manière proactive et réactive la robustesse face aux retards petits et importants.
• comprendre quantitativement l'utilité de la décision proposée, estimer sa sensibilité aux hypothèses considérées et comparer à la réaction typique dans la vie réelle Profil Idéalement, vous avez (ou êtes sur le point de recevoir) une maîtrise en sciences des transports, gestion / sciences décisionnelles, économétrie, mathématiques, statistiques, informatique, physique ou domaines connexes. Votre parcours de recherche est cohérent et montre un parcours, ou un potentiel clair, pour l'analyse, la modélisation, le contrôle et l'optimisation des systèmes de transport. Vous êtes très motivé et autodidacte, avec une vision de recherche claire, l'ambition académique, et d'excellentes compétences de communication et d'écriture (l'anglais parlé et écrit est obligatoire). Sarete responsabili per la progettazione e l'attuazione del coinvolgimento degli stakeholder del NCCR CLIM+. Sfondo del progetto La posizione post-dottorale sarà parte integrante del nuovo centro nazionale di competenza nella ricerca NCCR CLIM+. NCCR CLIM+ sostiene la trasformazione della Svizzera verso una società responsabile del clima e forma una nuova generazione di esperti con una forte competenza disciplinare e transdisciplinare. Postdoctoral Position in Stakeholder Engagement 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken We invite applications for a postdoctoral position at the Transdisciplinarity-Lab (TdLab) of the Department of Environmental Systems Science at ETH Zürich. You will be responsible for designing and implementing the stakeholder engagement of the NCCR CLIM+. Project background The postdoctoral position will be an integral part of the newly established National Competence Centre in Research NCCR CLIM+ . NCCR CLIM+ supports Switzerland’s transformation towards a climate-resilient society and trains a new generation of experts with strong disciplinary and transdisciplinary expertise. This project offers the opportunity to collaborate with leading experts in atmospheric and climate science within the NCCR CLIM+ as well as ETH Zurich. Job description In the NCCR CLIM+ storylines are key to achieve actionable knowledge and cross-disciplinary communication. Storylines are scientifically based stories that represent plausible futures and extreme climate outcomes in their physical and social dimensions. You will be responsible to embed the storylines in their societal environment. For each storyline you will
• Identify the most important stakeholders and establish a network that connects them with the storyline’s researchers.
• Develop, implement and evaluate a Theory of Change with the network.
• Design, implement and evaluate the transdisciplinary process of engagement and co-production of knowledge and practices. You are welcome to further develop transdisciplinary methods and theories and to make your achievements known via talks and publications. The position is for three years initially and can be extended. The starting date is as soon as possible. In general, doctoral / postdoctoral researchers at ETH Zurich have a full-time employment. A part-time employment may only be considered in exceptional cases (e.g. child- or familycare, other projects or employment). Profile We are looking for a person who
• Has a doctorate in environmental or sustainability sciences.
• Is experienced in designing, implementing and evaluating transdisciplinary research processes.
• Has excellent interpersonal skills for both, collaborating with researchers of different disciplines as well as with stakeholders of different sectors of society.
• Can handle situations of conflicting communication, power and interests, looking for a pragmatic way forward.
• Is interested in critically questioning transdisciplinary theories and methods to develop them further.
• Is fluent in English and German. Workplace Workplace We offer TdLab’s expertise lies in theories and practices of transdisciplinary research and teaching. We offer a work environment that invites you to take ownership of your project, while getting skilled support as needed. We are looking for collaborators who want to further develop transdisciplinary research and teaching with a mindset of failing forward. Your future colleagues have diverse disciplinary backgrounds. December 2026 or by appointment a committed and experienced person as degree programme coordinator:in HST. The post will be filled as a result of retirement. The degree program HST combines health science, natural science and technological perspectives. In this central function, you coordinate the degree program at bachelor and master level, advise students and lecturers and contribute to the quality assurance and further development of teaching. Job Description As a Degree Programme Coordinator: in HST, you take on a key role at the interface of students, lecturers, study direction, study administration, academic services and department. Your main tasks include: - Coordination and further development of the degree programme HST at bachelor and master level, including planning and implementation of substantive reforms - Support of the study direction in curricular, regulatory and strategic questions, coordination of the teaching offer and financial planning - Processing of course-related inquiries and applications, in particular on study planning, subject crediting, grade conferences and master admission - HST-specific mobility advice for outgoing and incoming students - Analysis and preparation of key figures in the teaching area as well as participation in reporting and quality assurance - Representation of the degree programme in relevant ETH committees, projects and networks in the area of teaching - Assumption of teaching responsibility in the course You have: - A university degree in a field relevant to Health Sciences and Technology - Experience in the university environment, ideally in teaching coordination, study consulting or a comparable function - A good understanding of academic structures and processes in the field of teaching - Very good knowledge of German and English in words and writing - Pronounced communication skills and pleasure in working with different stakeholders - A structured, pragmatic and solution-oriented working method - High service orientation with a clear understanding of roles - Very good organizational ability, reliability and self-initiative - Resilience, discretion and safe appearance even in demanding consulting situations A doctorate, teaching experience and a didactic training are advantageous, but not absolutely necessary.

Un doctorat, une expérience d'enseignement et une formation didactique complémentaire sont un avantage, mais pas absolument nécessaire. descriptionByLocale.it:
PhD in Fenologia di Wildflower 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Il Gruppo Plant Ecology di ETH Zürich, guidato dal professor Janneke Hille Ris Lambers, sta cercando un candidato di dottorato entusiasta per studiare come le comunità di fioritura delle Alpi variano nello spazio e nel tempo, e quali sono le conseguenze di questa variazione per le dinamiche di impianto-pollinatore. Questo argomento è rilevante per la nostra comprensione di come il cambiamento climatico cambierà la tempistica e la sovrapposizione nella fenologia fiorente dei fiori selvatici alpino co-occupanti, e gli impatti di tali nuove comunità di fioritura per le dinamiche pollinatori e il fitness riproduttivo vegetale. Affrontare questi argomenti è stato impegnativo nei sistemi alpini, che ospitano un'alta diversità di piante e impollinatori le cui interazioni variano enormemente su scale spaziali e temporali brevi. Fortunatamente, i recenti sviluppi tecnologici e analitici ci permettono di quantificare le reti di interazione delle specie ad alta risoluzione spaziale e temporale, potenzialmente fornendo nuove informazioni su questo argomento. Descrizione del lavoro Si prevede che lo studente di dottorato prescelto lavorerà in collaborazione con il gruppo Plant Ecology (ETH Zürich) e un team internazionale di collaboratori per affrontare questo argomento. In particolare, il candidato del dottorato condurrà:
• Lavoro sul campo per quantificare la fenologia della fioritura (utilizzando fenocams) e le interazioni plant-pollinatore in tutta la stagione in crescita e gradienti di elevazione.
• Esperimenti per esplorare le implicazioni della fenologia della fioritura alterata per la visitazione di impollinatori e il fitness riproduttivo vegetale.
• Analizza per quantificare la fenologia e le reti di interazione fiorenti per esplorare questioni di interesse, compresa l'applicazione di approcci di apprendimento profondo (per l'identificazione automatizzata dei fiori) e analisi di rete temporale. Lo studente di dottorato avrà l'opportunità di sviluppare le proprie idee all'interno di questo progetto, e sarà anche previsto di contribuire a responsabilità di gruppo all'interno del dipartimento e dell'università (ad esempio l'insegnamento, l'istruzione, l'istruzione, le attività di laboratorio), come è previsto per tutti i membri del gruppo. Profilo
• Entusiasmo e interesse per il progetto
• Conoscenze ecologiche rilevanti (per esempio in fenologia, dinamica vegetale-pollinatore, e / o impatti ecologici del cambiamento climatico)
• Esperienza con metodi di modellazione statistica e/o deep learning
• Esperienza con l'identificazione di impianti e l'identificazione di impollinatori
• Capacità di lavorare in modo indipendente e collaborativo
• Impegno a un posto di lavoro collegiale e inclusivo
• Esperienza di lavoro sul campo e patente valida
• Inglese avanzato (orale e scrittura) Luogo di lavoro Offriamo Il Gruppo Plant Ecology di ETH Zürich conduce ricerche su una diversità di argomenti all'interno del regno dell'ecologia della comunità vegetale, tra cui i conducenti della fenomenologia dei fiori selvatici alpino, i fattori che limitano la rigenerazione delle foreste e il ruolo delle interazioni climatiche e specie che influenzano le popolazioni e le comunità delle piante. Conduciamo progetti e manteniamo studi di monitoraggio a lungo termine nei siti del settore alpino e forestale in Svizzera e negli Stati Uniti (Washington State). Ci impegniamo a promuovere la diversità e l'inclusione in tutte le nostre attività, oltre a condurre la scienza aperta e collaborativa. Per ulteriori informazioni sulle attività del gruppo di ricerca, consultare il nostro sito web. Questo dottorato è completamente finanziato. Sarai assunto come ricercatore a tempo pieno per quattro anni. Lo stipendio annuale è molto competitivo (vedi le norme ETH di Zurigo). La posizione si trova a Zurigo, in Svizzera. Il lavoro a distanza dall'esterno della Svizzera non è possibile a causa di vincoli legali. Gruppi di ricerca di rilievo presso ETH Zürich, l'adiacente Università di Zurigo, WSL (Istituto federale svizzero per la ricerca forestale, neve e paesaggio) e EAWAG (Istituto federale svizzero di scienza e tecnologia acquatica) offrono numerose opportunità di interazione e collaborazione. Zürich è una città cosmopolita con elevati standard di vita e facile accesso ai siti di ricerca forestale e alpina, fuori
descriptionByLocale.en:
PhD in Wildflower Phenology 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Plant Ecology Group at ETH Zürich, led by Professor Janneke Hille Ris Lambers, is seeking an enthusiastic PhD candidate to study how Alpine flowering communities vary over space and time, and what the consequences of this variation are for plant-pollinator dynamics. This topic is relevant to our understanding of how climate change will alter the timing and overlap in flowering phenology of co-occurring Alpine wildflowers, and the impacts of such novel flowering communities for pollinator dynamics and plant reproductive fitness. Addressing these topics has been challenging in Alpine systems, which harbor a high diversity of plants and pollinators whose interactions vary enormously over fine spatial and short temporal scales. Fortunately, recent technological and analytical developments allow us to quantify species interaction networks at high spatial and temporal resolution, potentially providing for new insights into this topic. Job description The chosen PhD student will be expected to work collaboratively with the Plant Ecology Group (at ETH Zürich) and an international team of collaborators to address this topic. Specifically, the PhD candidate will conduct:
• Field work to quantify flowering phenology (using phenocams) and plant-pollinator interactions across the growing season and elevational gradients.
• Experiments to explore the implications of altered flowering phenology for pollinator visitation and plant reproductive fitness.
• Analyses to quantify flowering phenology and interaction networks to explore questions of interest, including the application of deep learning approaches (for automated identification of flowers) and temporal network analyses. The PhD student will have the opportunity to develop their own ideas within this project, and will also be expected to contribute to group responsibilities within the department and university (e.g. teaching, outreach, lab activities), as is expected of all group members. Profile
• Enthusiasm and interest in the project
• Relevant ecological knowledge (e.g. in phenology, plant-pollinator dynamics, and / or ecological impacts of climate change)
• Experience with statistical modelling and / or deep learning approaches
• Experience with identifying plants and identifying pollinators
• Ability to work independently and collaboratively
• Commitment to a collegial and inclusive workplace
• Field work experience and a valid driver's license
• Advanced English (oral and writing) Workplace Workplace We offer The Plant Ecology Group at ETH Zürich conducts research on a diversity of topics within the realm of plant community ecology, including the drivers of Alpine wildflower phenology, the factors that limit forest regeneration, and the role of climate and species interactions in influencing plant populations and communities. We conduct projects and maintain long-term monitoring studies in Alpine and forest field sites in and Switzerland and the USA (Washington State). We are committed to fostering diversity and inclusivity in all our activities, as well as to conducting open and collaborative science. Please see our website for more information on activities in the research group. This PhD is fully funded. You will be hired as a full-time researcher for four years. The annual salary is very competitive (see ETH Zurich regulations ). The position is based in Zurich, Switzerland. Remote work from outside of Switzerland is not possible due to legal constraints. Outstanding research groups at ETH Zürich, the adjacent University of Zürich, WSL (the Swiss Federal Institute for Forest, Snow and Landscape Research) and EAWAG (the Swiss Federal Institute of Aquatic Science and Technology) offer numerous opportunities for interaction and collaboration. Zürich is a cosmopolitan city with high living standards and easy access to forested and alpine research sites, out

PhD in der Wildflower Phenologie 100%, Zürich, befristet Drucken Drucken Die Plant Ecology Group an der ETH Zürich, unter der Leitung von Professor Janneke Hille Ris Lambers, sucht einen begeisterten Doktoranden, um zu studieren, wie die alpinen Blumengemeinden über Raum und Zeit variieren, und welche Konsequenzen dieser Variation für die Pflanzen-Pollinatordynamik sind. Dieses Thema ist relevant für unser Verständnis, wie der Klimawandel das Timing und die Überschneidung in der blühenden Phenologie der ko-verursachten alpinen Wildblumen verändern wird, und die Auswirkungen solcher neuartigen blühenden Gemeinschaften auf die Pollenatordynamik und Pflanzenreproduktive Fitness. Die Bewältigung dieser Themen war in alpinen Systemen eine Herausforderung, die eine hohe Vielfalt von Pflanzen und Bestäubern beherbergt, deren Wechselwirkungen enorm über feine räumliche und kurze zeitliche Skalen variieren. Glücklicherweise erlauben uns jüngste technologische und analytische Entwicklungen die Quantifizierung von Arteninteraktionsnetzwerken bei hoher räumlicher und zeitlicher Auflösung, die möglicherweise neue Einblicke in dieses Thema ermöglichen. Jobbeschreibung Der gewählte Doktorand wird voraussichtlich gemeinsam mit der Plant Ecology Group (in der ETH Zürich) und einem internationalen Team von Mitarbeitern arbeiten, um dieses Thema zu behandeln. Im Einzelnen wird der PhD-Kandidat führen:
• Feldarbeit zur Quantifizierung von blühenden Phenologien (unter Verwendung von Phenocams) und Pflanzen-Pollinator-Interaktionen über die wachsende Saison und Höhengradienten.
• Experimente, um die Auswirkungen der veränderten blühenden Phenologie auf den Besuch von Pollenator und Pflanzenreproduktivität zu untersuchen.
• Analysen zur Quantifizierung von blühenden Phenologie- und Interaktionsnetzwerken, um Fragen von Interesse zu untersuchen, einschließlich der Anwendung von tiefen Lernansätzen (zur automatisierten Identifizierung von Blumen) und zeitlichen Netzwerkanalysen. Der Doktorand wird in diesem Projekt die Möglichkeit haben, eigene Ideen zu entwickeln, und wird auch erwartet, dass er zu Gruppenverantwortungen innerhalb der Abteilung und Universität (z.B. Lehre, Outreach, Laboraktivitäten) beiträgt, wie es von allen Gruppenmitgliedern erwartet wird. Profil
• Begeisterung und Interesse am Projekt

• Erfahrungen mit statistischen Modellierungs- und/oder Deep Learning Ansätzen
• Erfahrung mit der Identifizierung von Pflanzen und der Identifizierung von Bestäubern

Wir führen Projekte durch und halten langfristige Monitoring-Studien in alpinen und Waldgebieten in der Schweiz und in den USA (Washington State). Herausragende Forschungsgruppen an der ETH Zürich, der benachbarten Universität Zürich, der WSL (dem Schweizerischen Bundesinstitut für Wald-, Schnee- und Landschaftsforschung) und der EAWAG (dem Schweizerischen Bundesinstitut für Wasserwissenschaft und Technologie) bieten vielfältige Möglichkeiten für Interaktion und Zusammenarbeit. Doctorat en phénologie des fleurs sauvages 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Le Plant Ecology Group de l'ETH Zürich, dirigé par le professeur Janneke Hille Ris Lambers, cherche un doctorant enthousiaste pour étudier comment les communautés de fleurs alpines varient dans l'espace et le temps, et quelles sont les conséquences de cette variation pour la dynamique des pollinisateurs végétaux. Ce sujet est pertinent pour notre compréhension de la façon dont le changement climatique modifiera le moment et le chevauchement de la phénologie de la floraison des fleurs sauvages alpines qui cohabitent, ainsi que les répercussions de ces nouvelles communautés de fleurs sur la dynamique des pollinisateurs et l'aptitude à la reproduction des plantes. L'examen de ces sujets a été difficile dans les systèmes alpins, qui abritent une grande diversité de plantes et de pollinisateurs dont les interactions varient énormément sur de fines échelles spatiales et temporelles courtes. Heureusement, les récents développements technologiques et analytiques nous permettent de quantifier les réseaux d'interactions avec les espèces à haute résolution spatiale et temporelle, ce qui pourrait fournir de nouvelles perspectives sur ce sujet. Description du poste Le doctorant choisi sera appelé à travailler en collaboration avec le Plant Ecology Group (à l'ETH Zürich) et une équipe internationale de collaborateurs pour aborder ce sujet. Plus précisément, le candidat au doctorat réalisera :
• Travail sur le terrain pour quantifier la phénologie de la floraison (à l'aide de phénocames) et les interactions plante-pollinisateur au cours de la saison de croissance et des gradients d'élévation.
• Des expériences pour explorer les implications de la phénologie de la floraison modifiée pour la visite des pollinisateurs et l'aptitude à la reproduction des plantes.
• Analyses visant à quantifier la phénologie de la floraison et les réseaux d'interaction afin d'explorer les questions d'intérêt, y compris l'application d'approches d'apprentissage profond (pour l'identification automatisée des fleurs) et d'analyses de réseaux temporels. Le doctorant aura l'occasion de développer ses propres idées dans le cadre de ce projet et devra également contribuer aux responsabilités de groupe au sein du département et de l'université (p. ex., enseignement, sensibilisation, activités de laboratoire), comme on s'y attend de tous les membres du groupe. Profil
• Intérêt et enthousiasme pour le projet
• Connaissances écologiques pertinentes (p. ex. en phénologie, dynamique des pollinisateurs végétaux et/ou incidences écologiques des changements climatiques)
• Expérience de la modélisation statistique et/ou des approches d'apprentissage profond
• Expérience de l'identification des plantes et des pollinisateurs
• Capacité de travailler de manière indépendante et en collaboration
• Engagement en faveur d'un milieu de travail collégial et inclusif
• Expérience professionnelle sur le terrain et permis de conduire valide
• Anglais avancé (oral et écrit) Lieu de travail Nous offrons Le Plant Ecology Group de l'ETH Zürich mène des recherches sur une diversité de sujets dans le domaine de l'écologie des communautés végétales, y compris les moteurs de la phénologie des fleurs sauvages alpines, les facteurs qui limitent la régénération des forêts, et le rôle des interactions entre le climat et les espèces dans l'influence des populations et des communautés végétales. Nous menons des projets et nous entretenons des études de surveillance à long terme sur des terrains alpins et forestiers en Suisse et aux États-Unis (État de Washington). Nous nous engageons à favoriser la diversité et l'inclusion dans toutes nos activités, ainsi qu'à mener des activités scientifiques ouvertes et collaboratives. Veuillez consulter notre site Web pour plus d'informations sur les activités du groupe de recherche. Ce doctorat est entièrement financé. Vous serez embauché comme chercheur à temps plein pendant quatre ans. Le salaire annuel est très compétitif (voir les règlements de Zurich). Le poste est basé à Zurich, Suisse. Le travail à distance de l'extérieur de la Suisse n'est pas possible en raison de contraintes juridiques. Des groupes de recherche exceptionnels à l'ETH Zürich, à l'Université adjacente de Zürich, WSL (Institut fédéral suisse de recherche sur les forêts, la neige et le paysage) et EAWAG (Institut fédéral suisse des sciences et technologies aquatiques) offrent de nombreuses possibilités d'interaction et de collaboration. Zürich est une ville cosmopolite avec un niveau de vie élevé et un accès facile aux sites de recherche boisés et alpins

PhD Posizione: termodinamica molecolare e modellazione dei trasporti per la transizione energetica 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato Descrizione Il gruppo Molecular Engineering Thermodynamics (MET) di ETH Zurich sta cercando uno studente di dottorato per sviluppare e migliorare gli strumenti computazionali per la descrizione della scala molecolare del trasporto di massa nelle membrane con un'applicazione ai processi di separazione. Il gruppo MET di ETH Zurich, guidato da Philipp Rehner, è dedicato a collegare rigorosi modelli molecolari fisici alla progettazione di processi sostenibili nell'ingegneria chimica. Per colmare la scala dalle molecole ai processi, applichiamo concetti e strumenti matematici all'avanguardia combinati con metodi computazionali altamente efficienti. Una particolare attenzione è la modellazione di fenomeni interfacciali nelle applicazioni di progettazione di processo. Il nostro focus tecnologico è sulle tecnologie emergenti per la transizione energetica. Contesto del progetto Un approvvigionamento sostenibile delle nostre richieste di energia e materiali deve essere costruito su nuovi processi che caratterizzano alimentatori rinnovabili, approvvigionamento energetico verde e una migliore efficienza energetica. Un design efficiente dei nuovi processi deve tener conto delle interazioni delle molecole e dei materiali con le prestazioni del processo che si verificano nelle interfacce: ad esempio materiali adsorbenti, superfici dello scambiatore di calore o membrane. Il progetto ProMote stabilisce un flusso di lavoro integrato di progettazione di materiali e processi che, per la prima volta, incorpora rigorosi modelli molecolari per fenomeni interfacciali direttamente nella valutazione e nella progettazione dei processi. Per colmare il divario tra il mondo continuum di progettazione di processo e la natura stocastica delle molecole, il progetto ProMote propone l'applicazione della teoria funzionale della densità classica – una descrizione continuum su scala molecolare dei sistemi inomogenei – nella progettazione di processo e, quindi, fondere le scale dalle molecole ai processi. Per superare la sfida computazionale di applicare modelli molecolari a scale di processo, il progetto combina concetti matematici efficienti come differenziazione automatica con backpropagation – lo stesso concetto che alimenta l'apprendimento automatico e l'intelligenza artificiale ovunque – con modelli fisici rigorosi che sono robusti e interpretabili a causa dei loro vincoli fisici. Nel progetto ProMote, il flusso di lavoro di progettazione integrato sarà dimostrato per tre tecnologie emergenti: cattura del carbonio, pompe di calore ad alta temperatura e separazioni della membrana. Mansioni - Il vostro compito primario sarà quello di sviluppare e implementare modelli per la descrizione molecolare delle resistenze di trasporto in materiali micro o nanoporosi - I modelli saranno poi utilizzati per quantificare il trasporto di massa attraverso membrane al fine di valutare le prestazioni dei nuovi materiali a membrana nei processi di separazione industriale - Il tuo ruolo coinvolgerà anche progetti di mentoring e co-supervisione di studenti e tesi - Ti impegni in vari compiti e attività di gruppo e di istituto - Come parte integrante del tuo lavoro, pubblicherai i tuoi risultati in riviste peer-reviewed e li presenterai a conferenze internazionali

PhD Position: Molecular Thermodynamics and Transport Modeling for the Energy Transition 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Molecular Engineering Thermodynamics (MET) group at ETH Zurich is looking for a doctoral student to develop and improve computational tools for the molecular scale description of mass transport in membranes with an application to separation processes. The MET group at ETH Zurich, led by Philipp Rehner, is dedicated to linking rigorous physical molecular models to the design of sustainable processes in chemical engineering. To bridge the scale from molecules to processes, we apply state-of-the art mathematical concepts and tools combined with highly efficient computational methods. A particular focus is on the modeling of interfacial phenomena in process design applications. Our technological focus is on emerging technologies for the energy transition. Project background A sustainable supply of our energy and materials demands must be built on novel processes that feature renewable feedstocks, green energy supply, and improved energy efficiency. An efficient design of novel processes needs to account for the interactions of molecules and materials with the process performance that occur at interfaces: e.g., adsorbent materials, heat exchanger surfaces, or membranes. The ProMote project establishes an integrated material and process design workflow that – for the first time – incorporates rigorous molecular models for interfacial phenomena directly into the evaluation and design of processes. To bridge the gap between the continuum world of process design and the stochastic nature of molecules, the ProMote project proposes the application of classical density functional theory – a molecular-scale continuum description of inhomogeneous systems – in process design and, therefore, to fuse the scales from molecules to processes. To overcome the computational challenge of applying molecular models at process scales, the project combines efficient mathematical concepts like automatic differentiation with backpropagation – the same concept that powers machine learning and artificial intelligence everywhere – with rigorous physical models that are robust and interpretable due to their physical constraints. In the ProMote project, the integrated design workflow will be demonstrated for three emerging technologies: carbon capture, high-temperature heat pumps, and membrane separations. Job description
• Your primary task will be to develop and implement models for the molecular description of transport resistivities in micro- or nanoporous materials
• The models will then be used to quantify mass transport through membranes in order to evaluate the performance of novel membrane materials in industrial separation processes
• Your role will also involve mentoring and co-supervising student projects and theses
• You will engage in various group and institute duties and activities
• As an integral part of your work, you will publish your results in peer-reviewed journals and present them at international conferences Profile
• You meet the requirements for a doctoral program at ETH Zurich and have an excellent Master's or diploma in chemical engineering, process engineering, mechanical engineering, physics, energy science & technology, physical chemistry, or a related field
• Ideally, you already have experience working computationally and developing scientific software
• Experience in Python is highly recommended, additional knowledge of performance-oriented modeling frameworks, either based on Python (e.g., JAX, Pytorch) or other programming languages (e.g., C++, Rust, Julia) are welcome
• You are interested and able to develop thermodynamic models while gaining a solid understanding of the underlying physical processes
• The ability to work independently and excellent communication and writing skills in English complete your profile Workplace Workplace We
