Beschreibung PhD Position: 3-D Geologische Modellierung der Östlichen Penninik 100%, Zürich, befristet Drucken Drucken Die Gruppe Strukturgeologie und Tectonics konzentriert sich auf die schnell deformierenden Zonen, die die tektonischen Plattengrenzen der Erde definieren und viele der Geohazards des Planeten erzeugen. Wir haben eine neue PhD-Position offen für die 3D-geologische Modellierung der östlichen Penninics in den Schweizer Alpen. Projekt Hintergrund Der östliche Penninic nappe Stapel der Schweizer Alpen bewahrt eine komplexe Aufzeichnung von Subduktion, Akkordeon, nappe Emplacement, Metamorphismus und Exhumation. Seine großen tektonischen Grenzen bieten ein außergewöhnliches natürliches Labor zur Rekonstruktion der dreidimensionalen Architektur der Alpen und zur Prüfung, wie geerbte Geometrie, Lithologie und Verformungsgeschichte die krustalen Strukturen beeinflussen. Im Rahmen des Projekts swisstopo swissAlps3D wird dieses Forschungsprojekt die 3-D-geologische Modellierung als Kerninstrument zur Rekonstruktion der Untergrundstruktur der östlichen Penninics in der Schweiz verwenden. Über vier Jahre wird der Kandidat ein hochwertiges, 3-D-geologisches Modell aufbauen, indem er geologische Karten, Strukturdaten, Querschnitte, Tunnel- und Bohrlochinformationen, geophysikalische Zwänge und veröffentlichte metamorphe und thermochronologische Datensätze integriert. Das Projekt wird die Zusammenarbeit mit den benachbarten Modellierungsbemühungen sowie gezielte feldbasierte Arbeiten an ausgewählten tektonischen Grenzen innerhalb des Modellraums beinhalten. Diese Bemühungen zielen darauf ab, die regionale 3-D-Architektur mit Variationen in Lithologie, Verformungsgeweben, metamorpher Geschichte und flüssigkeitsbezogenen Merkmalen entlang der großen krustalen Schnittstellen zu verbinden. In den späteren Phasen des Projekts wird der Kandidat mit dem zugeschriebenen 3-D-Modell eine prozessorientierte Darstellung eines alten Subduktionsinterface-Systems entwickeln und untersuchen, wie seine Geometrie und innere Heterogenität Segmentierung, Stammlokalisierung und Schlupfverhalten beeinflusst haben können. Das von swisstopo geförderte Projekt wird unter der Leitung von Prof. Whitney Behr, in Zusammenarbeit mit swisstopo und Dr. Lukas Nibourel in der Georesources Schweiz Gruppe an der ETH Zürich. Jobbeschreibung - Erstellung und Harmonisierung regionaler geologischer Datensätze, einschließlich Karten, Querschnitte, Strukturmessungen, Tunnel- und Bohrlochdaten und veröffentlichte Einschränkungen - Bauen Sie ein dreiteiliges 3-D-geologisches Modell des östlichen Penninic-Nappe-Stacks mit klarer Dokumentation von Annahmen und Unsicherheiten - Entwicklung eines konsistenten Strukturschemas und einer Einheitslegende in Abstimmung mit swisstopo und benachbarten Modellierungsbemühungen - Führen Sie gezielte Feldarbeiten, um wichtige geometrische Unsicherheiten zu lösen und strukturelle Beobachtungen zu sammeln - Verwenden Sie das 3-D-Modell, um die Architektur, Kontinuität und tektonische Bedeutung der großen krustalen Grenzen zu untersuchen - Modelldokumentation, Berichte, Handschriften und Konferenzpräsentationen vorbereiten Profil - MSc in Geowissenschaften/Geologie oder einem verwandten Bereich - Starkes Interesse an Feldgeologie, Strukturgeologie, Tektonik und/oder 3-D geologische Modellierung - Erfahrung mit geologischer Kartierung, GIS, Querschnittskonstruktion oder 3-D-Modellierungssoftware ist ein Vorteil - Bereitschaft, Feldarbeiten im alpinen Gelände durchzuführen - Solide Englischkenntnisse; Deutsch ist hilfreich, aber nicht erforderlich - Zusammenarbeit, organisiert, unabhängig und vorsichtig mit komplexen Datensätzen und Unsicherheit Arbeitsplatz Arbeitsplatz

Descrizione Poste de doctorat : Modélisation géologique 3D de la penninique orientale 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Le groupe de géologie structurale et de tectonique se concentre sur les zones de déformation rapide qui définissent les limites des plaques tectoniques de la Terre et génèrent de nombreux géorisques de la planète. Nous avons un nouveau poste de doctorat ouvert sur la modélisation géologique 3D des Penniniques de l'Est dans les Alpes suisses. Contexte du projet La pile de nappes penniniques de l'est des Alpes suisses conserve un record complexe de subduction, d'accrétion, de mise en place de nappes, de métamorphisme et d'exhumation. Ses grandes frontières tectoniques constituent un laboratoire naturel exceptionnel pour reconstruire l'architecture tridimensionnelle des Alpes et pour tester comment la géométrie, la lithologie et l'histoire de la déformation héritée influencent les structures à l'échelle de la croûte. Dans le cadre du projet swisstopo swissAlps3D, ce projet de doctorat utilisera la modélisation géologique 3D comme outil de base pour reconstruire la structure souterraine des Penniniques de l'Est en Suisse. Sur quatre ans, le candidat élaborera un modèle géologique 3D de haute qualité en intégrant des cartes géologiques, des données structurelles, des sections transversales, des informations sur les tunnels et les forages, des contraintes géophysiques et des ensembles de données métamorphiques et thermochronologiques publiés. Le projet comprendra une collaboration avec les efforts de modélisation voisins, ainsi que des travaux ciblés sur le terrain portant sur certaines limites tectoniques dans la zone du modèle. Ces efforts visent à relier l'architecture 3D à l'échelle régionale avec des variations dans la lithologie, les tissus de déformation, l'histoire métamorphique et les caractéristiques liées aux fluides le long des principales interfaces croûtales. Dans les étapes ultérieures du projet, le candidat utilisera le modèle 3D attribué pour développer une représentation axée sur le processus d'un ancien système d'interface de subduction et explorer comment sa géométrie et son hétérogénéité interne peuvent avoir influencé la segmentation, la localisation des tensions et le comportement de glissement. Le projet, financé par swisstopo , sera accueilli au sein du Groupe de Géologie structurale et Tectonique à l'ETH Zurich sous la supervision du Prof. Whitney Behr, en collaboration avec swisstopo et le Dr Lukas Niborel dans le groupe Georesources Suisse à l'ETH Zurich. Description du poste - Compiler et harmoniser les ensembles de données géologiques régionales, y compris les cartes, les sections transversales, les mesures structurelles, les données sur les tunnels et les forages, et les contraintes publiées - Construire un modèle géologique 3D en trois parties de la pile de nappes Penniniques Est, avec une documentation claire des hypothèses et des incertitudes - Élaborer un schéma structurel cohérent et une légende unitaire en coordination avec swisstopo et les efforts de modélisation voisins - Effectuer des travaux ciblés sur le terrain pour résoudre les principales incertitudes géométriques et recueillir des observations structurelles - Utiliser le modèle 3D pour étudier l'architecture, la continuité et la signification tectonique des principales frontières crustales - Préparer la documentation modèle, les rapports, les manuscrits et les présentations de conférences Profil - Maîtrise en sciences de la Terre/géologie ou domaine connexe - Fort intérêt pour la géologie de terrain, la géologie structurelle, la tectonique et/ou la modélisation géologique 3D - L'expérience de la cartographie géologique, du SIG, de la construction transversale ou du logiciel de modélisation 3D est un avantage - Volonté de mener des travaux sur le terrain alpin - Compétences en anglais solide; l'allemand est utile mais pas nécessaire - Collaboration, organisation, indépendance et prudence avec des ensembles de données et des incertitudes complexes Lieu de travail Lieu de travail

Doctoral student in induced and natural seismicity forecasting 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Swiss Seismological Service (SED) at the Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences (D-EAPS) is seeking a motivated doctoral student to work at the intersection of statistical seismology and machine learning. This position is part of two EU-funded projects: GeoTwins , which focuses on creating digital twins for geothermal systems, and Earth-AID, which aims to develop an AI-powered decision-support system for geohazards. The position will contribute to advancing earthquake forecasting and risk management and improve our ability to mitigate induced seismicity in real time. Job description The doctoral student will develop, integrate, and evaluate forecasting models of induced and natural earthquakes. The responsibilities include:
• Model Integration: Incorporating state-of-the-art models, specifically ETAS-f and Oracle, into the SED's forecast management and scheduling system
• Systematic Evaluation: Performing rigorous model comparison tests to determine forecast quality
• Surrogate Modeling: Building, training, and evaluating machine learning surrogate models to emulate complex seismic behaviors and accelerate forecasting
• Data Engineering: Populating and managing data lakes with large-scale natural ETAS simulations and synthetic datasets to provide the foundation for AI training
• Scientific Communication: Publishing findings in high-impact journals and presenting at international conferences Profile
• Education: An MSc degree in Geophysics, Physics, Mathematics, Data Science, or a related quantitative field
• Technical Skills: Strong programming proficiency (primarily Python)
• Domain Interest: A deep interest in seismology, induced seismicity, and the application of statistics and machine learning to earth science problems
• Analytical Skills: High-level quantitative skills and a structured approach to complex problem-solving
• Communication: Ability to work effectively in a collaborative environment with full proficiency in English (written and oral) Workplace Workplace We offer The Swiss Seismological Service operates at the unique intersection of academic research and a federal public mandate, fostering an environment where diverse perspectives are essential for addressing complex geohazard challenges. The candidate will be part of a community that values mutual mentorship and collective growth, supported by a world-class academic environment: ETH Zurich is currently ranked #1 globally for Earth Sciences (QS World University Rankings 2026). This is a 100% position with a competitive salary in line with standard ETH doctoral rates, based in the heart of Zurich. chevron_right Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Academic Programs Lead 80%-100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The ETH AI Center is one of the largest AI centers in Europe with over 120 Professors from all 16 departments of ETH Zurich and over 1500 associated PhD students & post-docs. Our mission is to foster interdisciplinary AI research and pave the way from science to society. Project background The Academic Programs Lead will lead a small, high-impact unit responsible for academic community-building, research acceleration, education programs, and impact dissemination at the ETH AI Center. Reporting to the Executive Director, this is a hands-on leadership role: you will set the strategic direction for the unit while personally driving key programs forward. You will own the Center’s research accelerator portfolio - including GPU grants, university partnerships (e.g. the Stanford exchange program), and grant writing support for flagship proposals. You will also shape education offerings in collaboration with faculty, manage relationships with ELLIS and partner institutions, and ensure the unit delivers measurable impact across all its activity areas (e.g. scaling grant programs or supporting high-value research proposals). This role is ideal for someone who thrives as a player-coach: equally comfortable drafting a grant proposal, negotiating a partnership agreement, and aligning a team around priorities. Job description
• Run the Swiss National AI Institute’s GPU starting grants program end-to-end: promote calls, screen eligibility, coordinate reviewer panels with faculty, manage decisions, and handle applicant communications.
• Establish and manage strategic partnerships with peer institutions ( e.g. Stanford exchange program), including negotiating agreements, managing logistics, and maintaining relationships.
• Provide hands-on grant-writing support for Center flagship proposals, coordinating inputs from faculty and research groups.
• Drive education program development in collaboration with faculty leads, including large-scale AI engineering and entrepreneurship courses.
• Manage the ELLIS relationship and coordinate the Center’s engagement with the ELLIS network.
• Set priorities, workplans, and budget for the Academic Programs unit; run a lightweight coordination rhythm with the team.
• Represent the unit to ETH AI Center leadership, the faculty steering committee, and external stakeholders.
• Step in as backup across the unit’s activities when needed, ensuring continuity and quality. Profile Qualifications
• Strong interpersonal and communication skills - able to build trust with faculty, negotiate with external partners, and align diverse stakeholders.
• Proven ability to manage complex programs and portfolios with multiple parallel workstreams and deadlines.
• Experience in grant writing or research funding processes, ideally in a European academic context.
• Strategic thinker who is equally comfortable with hands-on execution.
• Proactive, structured, and solutions-oriented - you drive things to completion without waiting for direction.
• Strong written communication skills, including the ability to draft compelling proposals, agreements, and presentations. Requirements
• A master’s degree or PhD in a relevant field such as computer science, engineering, science policy, technology management, or a related discipline.
• At least 3–5 years of experience in academic research, research management, science program management, academic administration, or a comparable role in a tech or research environment.
• Demonstrated experience managing grants, partnerships, or institutional collaborations.
• A strong understanding of the AI research landscape and academic ecosystem.
• Fluency in English; German is a plus. Workplace Workplace We offer If you are a highly motivated individual with a passion for AI and a desire to make a significant impact in a rapidly evolving field, we would love to hear from

Storage Engineer / Storage Specialist 100%, Zurich, permanent print Drucken Do you think about storage beyond capacity and performance—focusing on availability, integrity, and resilience? Do you want to ensure that mission-critical data is secure, accessible, and recoverable at all times—even in worst-case scenarios? Then this is your opportunity to make a real impact with your expertise. Job description As an experienced Storage Engineer, you take ownership of the stable, secure, and sustainable operation of critical storage services. You independently plan, prioritize, and implement complex tasks while actively shaping and evolving our storage landscape. You design and refine BCM-related storage processes and solutions to ensure availability, recoverability, and organizational resilience. With a strong awareness of risks, you actively work to eliminate single points of failure in critical services. In the area of long-term storage, you operate and continuously develop solutions on high-latency media. You ensure data integrity, long-term availability, and well-structured operational processes, supported by clear and thorough documentation. At the same time, you manage and optimize our SAN infrastructure. You collaborate closely with neighboring infrastructure and service teams, contributing to incident, change, and lifecycle processes, and ensuring the reliability and performance of the overall IT environment. Profile You bring solid hands-on experience, deep technical expertise, and a structured, responsible approach:
• Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a comparable field—or equivalent professional experience
• Several years of experience operating critical IT infrastructures (Enterprise Storage, SAN, Long-Term Storage, Archiving, BCM)
• Strong expertise in Enterprise Storage and Tape Storage
• Advanced knowledge of SAN, Business Continuity Management, and Disaster Recovery
• Experience with Linux (RHEL) and strong Bash scripting skills
• Know-how in automation/scripting and structured operation of complex services
• Experience with lifecycle and IT service management processes
• Good German and advanced English skills What Sets You Apart In line with ETH social and leadership competencies, you go beyond technical expertise:
• You take full ownership of critical services and act reliably—even under pressure
• You think analytically and systemically, delivering sustainable, long-term solutions
• You work in a structured way, prioritize effectively, and maintain high-quality documentation
• You communicate clearly and collaborate effectively with diverse stakeholders
• You continuously seek improvements and bring a strong service mindset
• You value cross-team collaboration and open exchange Why This Role? This position offers you the chance to operate at a high professional level while having real impact:
• High autonomy: You manage complex topics end-to-end
• Visibility & impact: Your work directly enables the reliability of critical services
• Challenging environment: Technically and organizationally complex tasks
• Room to shape: You actively design and improve storage solutions
• Purpose-driven work: You safeguard essential data and organizational resilience In short: A role for professionals who want to take responsibility and make a difference. Workplace Workplace We offer Describe here what particularly distinguishes the work in your department/group e.g.:

chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht Assistente studentesco: Ricerca interdisciplinare in Urban Design, Dati e Piattaforme 10%-30%, Zurigo, stampa a tempo fisso Drucken The Chair of Architecture and Urban Design, Prof. Hubert Klumpner, Dipartimento di Architettura - D-ARCH, Istituto di Paesaggio e Studi Urbani - LUS, sta cercando un Assistente Studentesco a partire dal 2026 agosto o da accordo. La Cattedra Klumpner opera in stretta collaborazione con il Network City and Landscape - NSL, la Albert Einstein School of Public Policy, ed è partner accademico dell'UN-Habitat Informal Urbanism Research Hub. Integrando l'insegnamento, la ricerca e il fare, rispondiamo alle complessità dell'urbanizzazione globale triangolando il design urbano, la politica e costruendo prototipazioni per implementare risposte innovative in America Latina, nei Balcani e nell'Africa meridionale. La piattaforma del catalogo Urban Design Toolbox: Uno spazio per lo scambio di strategie di progettazione - UDTC , un progetto ETH Innovedum, traduce l'innovazione pedagogica in un ambiente aperto e interattivo e stabilisce una piattaforma per i futuri artefatti del corso. La piattaforma cura Urban Design Tools (UDTs) da tutto il mondo, mappando e confrontandole per identificare modelli ricorrenti e sfide specifiche del contesto che possono informare futuri urbani equi e rigenerativi. Questo progetto sarà condotto in collaborazione con il Laboratorio di Visualizzazione e Intelligenza interattiva D-INFK, IVIA Lab , guidato dal Prof. Mennatallah El-Assady. Descrizione del lavoro La fase di implementazione del progetto comprende lo sviluppo di una piattaforma digitale personalizzata per l'UDTC, concepita come uno spazio e-learning per la raccolta, l'organizzazione e lo scambio di strategie di progettazione urbana in casi, territori e temi.
• Sostenere lo sviluppo dell'architettura della piattaforma e del web design della piattaforma UDTC Platform
• Ricerca, raccolta e organizzazione di dataset, materiali di studio e contenuti di riferimento
• Assistere nella creazione di quadri analitici per la classificazione e il confronto delle strategie di progettazione urbana
• Produrre cartografie ed esplorare forme alternative di visualizzazione dei dati
• Organizzare registrazioni delle conferenze, documenti e materiali di archivio per l'integrazione nella piattaforma
• Hai esperienza con i flussi di lavoro GIS e l'analisi spaziale
• Sei esperto in Adobe Creative Suite, in particolare InDesign, Illustrator e Photoshop, oltre ad avere una buona conoscenza di Excel
• La familiarità con gli strumenti di web design e l'elaborazione dei dataset è auspicabile
• Siete in una fase dei vostri studi dove, durante il semestre, è possibile dedicare da 10 a 20 ore alla settimana (potenzialmente più al di fuori del semestre)
• Siete affidabili, proattivi e in grado di lavorare in modo indipendente e collaborativo all'interno di un team interdisciplinare Workplace Workplace Offriamo la massima flessibilità: Sappiamo che i tuoi studi vengono prima. Le ore di lavoro sono concordate con un accordo reciproco e possono essere programmate in modo flessibile intorno al vostro orario di lezione e ai periodi di esame
• Compensazione equa: L'occupazione è su base oraria in conformità con i tassi ufficiali di salario di ETH Zurigo per i dipendenti degli studenti

Stiamo cercando uno studente di dottorato in ML applicata e NLP. Questa posizione di dottorato fa parte del progetto finanziato dalla SNSF “AI responsabile per la magistratura svizzera” presso l’ETH di Zurigo. Il progetto sviluppa e valuta prototipi basati su AI per sostenere il processo decisionale giudiziario, con un focus sull'applicabilità del mondo reale. Combina l'apprendimento automatico, le applicazioni legali e la valutazione empirica in collaborazione con partner giudiziari. PhD Student in Applied ML and NLP 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken As part of the SNSF-funded project “Responsible AI for the Swiss Judiciary”, we work on real-world applications of artificial intelligence for the Swiss judiciary in close collaboration with courts and partners across Switzerland. We are looking for a PhD Student in Applied ML and NLP. This doctoral position is part of the SNSF-funded project “Responsible AI for the Swiss Judiciary” at ETH Zurich. The project develops and evaluates AI-based prototypes to support judicial decision-making, with a focus on real-world applicability. It combines machine learning, legal applications, and empirical evaluation in collaboration with judicial partners. The project offers a unique opportunity to work on real-world, high-stakes AI systems in collaboration with courts, combining cutting-edge AI research with impactful societal applications. Job description The doctoral researcher will focus on the development and evaluation of AI-based research prototypes for legal applications, with a strong emphasis on technical implementation and real-world deployment. Core responsibilities include:
• Developing and implementing AI systems for legal text processing and decision support (e.g., LLMs, retrieval-augmented generation, agentic systems)
• Building production-quality prototypes suitable for pilot deployment in judicial settings, including robust retrieval systems, LLM pipelines, and evaluation infrastructure
• Designing and running systematic evaluations of model performance, robustness, and reliability
• Building datasets, benchmarks, and pipelines for legal AI applications
• Improving model architectures, prompting strategies, and retrieval systems for high-stakes environments
• Conducting pilot evaluations with judicial partners to study how AI tools perform in real decision-making workflows, and translating findings into technical improvements (e.g., new embedding methods, agent architectures, prompting strategies)
• Publishing research results in leading venues in artificial intelligence and computational social science
• The position is designed for a cumulative PhD with a strong methodological and technical focus

descriptionByLocale.en:
Postdoctoral Researcher in Quantitative Socio-Spatial Analysis 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken This position is in the research group “Spatial Development and Urban Policy SPUR” led by Prof. Dr. David Kaufmann, which focuses on sustainable, democratic and just urban development. We are an interdisciplinary research group at the Institute for Spatial and Landscape Development, bringing together perspectives from spatial planning, urban studies, social sciences, and data science. Project background We are searching for a postdoctoral researcher who conducts, leads, and acquires applied research projects on quantitative socio-spatial analysis. The core task is to develop and implement methods, tools and platforms for analyzing, monitoring and visualizing socio-spatial phenomena such as segregation, gentrification, displacement, housing affordability and poverty, with a focus on Switzerland. This includes collecting, analyzing and visualizing spatial registry data for research, applied projects, teaching and public communication. More specifically, the researcher would develop and conduct socio-spatial monitorings of Switzerland as well as to conduct applied research projects with public authorities. Job description The position entails to collaborate across disciplines and to integrate quantitative spatial analysis into different research projects. The researcher's task would also be to develop a website presenting socio-spatial outcomes, indices, and maps for the interested public to engage with, as well as providing open access, downloadable data. The researcher is expected to engage with public authorities, research institutions, NGOs and the public to further develop the applied research portfolio of the SPUR research group, with the longer-term goal of establishing a sub-unit on applied socio-spatial analysis Profile
• A PhD degree (or near completion of) in spatial or urban analytics, quantitative or computational social science or geography, public economics or similar disciplines
• Strong knowledge and skills in data science, spatial analytics and spatial data visualization, including experience in handling large-scale registry datasets. Experience in working with linked Swiss registry datasets is an asset
• Good knowledge and interest in Swiss spatial planning and housing policy, and a curiosity for socio-spatial phenomena and urban issues (e.g., segregation or gentrification)
• Interest in integrating spatial data analysis into interdisciplinary and mixed-methods research projects
• Good knowledge of the relevant academic literature and interest in bringing applied socio-spatial research into academic discourse and academic publications
• Interest in bringing socio-spatial analysis into teaching and public discourse
• Experience in project management and organizational development. Knowledge of website programming is an asset.
• Very good command of written and spoken English and German, good command of French is an asset Workplace Workplace We offer A postdoctoral researcher position initially limited to 2 years, but it can be extended up to 6 years. The intended starting date is summer 2026
• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

descriptionByLocale.it:
Lead Machine Learning Engineer & Lead Systems AI Engineer 60%-100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Il gruppo ETH Zürich Geothermal Energy & Geofluids (GEG) indaga il trasferimento di fluidi reattivi subsuperfici e geotermiche, lo sviluppo e l'utilizzo di simulazioni di computer, esperimenti di laboratorio e analisi di campo. Il nostro obiettivo è quello di ottenere informazioni fondamentali e sviluppare tecnologie sostenibili per affrontare le esigenze della società. L'iniezione o l'estrazione del fluido subsuperficie induce cambiamenti nelle proprietà del serbatoio geologico a causa dei processi accoppiati termoidro-meccanici-chimici-biologici (THMCB). Promuovere la comprensione di questi processi consente lo sviluppo dell'estrazione e del fluido dell'energia subsuperficiale (ad esempio CO2 / H2) e delle tecnologie di stoccaggio dell'energia, nonché le tecnologie di monitoraggio delle stesse. Per sviluppare e migliorare tali tecnologie di subsuperficie e soluzioni di monitoraggio associate, il gruppo GEG sta sviluppando e impiegando simulatori numerici, conducendo analisi sul campo e conducendo esperimenti di trasporto reattivi nel suo laboratorio di trasporto reattivo. Questo laboratorio ospita attualmente uno scanner Tomografia computerizzata a raggi X (XRCT), un laboratorio laser (Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV), Fluorescence indotta dal laser (LIF) e presto uno scanner MRI multi-nuclide. Sfondo del progetto In qualità di Lead Engineer, formerai le basi tecniche delle attività AI, dati e cloud del gruppo GEG e avrai la proprietà end-to-end di iniziative complesse e pluriennali. Siamo alla ricerca di candidati con un forte background in agentic AI, architettura cloud e ingegneria software, ingegneria dei dati e la governance, AI e applicazioni di machine learning. Descrizione del lavoro
• AI Agentic — Progettazione, costruzione e funzionamento di sistemi di agente AI di livello di produzione, coprendo il ciclo di vita completo dall'architettura cognitiva attraverso l'osservabilità, la telemetria e rigorosi protocolli di prova e valutazione.
• Architettura cloud e ingegneria software — Conceive, costruire e gestire architetture cloud complesse e scalabili composte da servizi distribuiti e microservizi. Guida lo sviluppo di software di livello enterprise e si assume la responsabilità per il ciclo di vita di sviluppo completo del software (SDLC), dalla progettazione architettonica attraverso la distribuzione e il funzionamento.
• Ingegneria dei dati e governance — Progettazione e gestione di datadotti end-to-end e prodotti di dati per dati strutturati e non strutturati, compresi i dati geospaziali ove pertinenti. Stabilire e mantenere standard di governance dei dati solidi per garantire qualità, sicurezza e conformità attraverso il paesaggio dei dati.
• AI & applicazioni di machine learning — Applicare metodi di machine learning e AI ai problemi del mondo reale e portarli dal prototipo in un uso affidabile della produzione.
• leadership tecnica — fornire direzione tecnica a scienziati e ingegneri GEG (e esterni), fissare standard architettonici, membri del team di mentore e collaborare orchestrare in più team e stakeholder.
• Gestione del progetto e distribuzione strategica — Progetti strategici pluriennali, tra cui la progettazione della roadmap e la responsabilità del bilancio; fornire iniziative complesse e interfunzionali nel tempo e nell'ambito. Profilo Sei un ingegnere leader che combina una forte fondazione scientifica con una sostanziale esperienza pratica in intelligenza artificiale, dati e cloud engineering, e che è pronto a prendere sia la proprietà tecnica e organizzativa di iniziative complesse. Il candidato di successo porta:
• Laurea magistrale o dottorato in (Geo-)Physics, Matematica, Informatica o disciplina quantitativa strettamente correlata
• 5+ anni di esperienza professionale in ingegneria del software, ingegneria dei dati o un ruolo tecnico comparabile
• Esperienza comprovata nella leadership tecnica e delle persone, tra cui ingegneri guida, impostazione della direzione architettonica, definizione degli standard di ingegneria e membri del team di mentoring
• Competenze solide di gestione del progetto, tra cui il design della roadmap, la responsabilità del bilancio e l'orchestrazione della collaborazione interfunzionale tra mu

Lead Machine Learning Engineer & Lead Systems AI Engineer 60%-100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The ETH Zürich Geothermal Energy & Geofluids (GEG) Group investigates subsurface reactive fluid and geothermal energy transfer, developing and employing computer simulations, laboratory experiments, and field analyses. Our aim is to gain fundamental insights and to develop sustainable technologies to address societal needs. Subsurface fluid injection or extraction induces changes in geologic reservoir properties due to thermo-hydro-mechanical-chemical-biological (THMCB) coupled processes. Advancing the understanding of these processes enables the development of subsurface energy extraction and fluid (e.g. CO2 / H2) and energy storage technologies as well as monitoring technologies thereof. To develop and improve such subsurface technologies and associated monitoring solutions, the GEG group is developing and employing numerical simulators, conducting field analyses, and conducting reactive transport experiments in its reactive transport laboratory. This laboratory currently houses an X-ray Computed Tomography (XRCT) scanner, a laser lab (Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV), Laser-Induced Fluorescence (LIF)), and soon a multi-nuclide MRI scanner. Project background As Lead Engineer, you will shape the technical foundation of the GEG group’s AI, data, and cloud activities and take end-to-end ownership of complex, multi-year initiatives. We are looking for applicants with a strong background in agentic AI, cloud architecture and software engineering, data engineering and governance, AI and machine learning applications. Job description
• Agentic AI — Design, build and operate production-grade AI agent systems, covering the full lifecycle from cognitive architecture through observability, telemetry and rigorous testing and evaluation protocols.
• Cloud architecture & software engineering — Conceive, build and operate complex, scalable cloud architectures composed of distributed services and microservices. Drive enterprise-grade software development and take responsibility for the full Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC), from architectural design through deployment and operation.
• Data engineering & governance — Design and operate end-to-end data pipelines and data products for structured and unstructured data, including geospatial data where relevant. Establish and maintain solid data governance standards to ensure quality, security and compliance across the data landscape.
• AI & machine learning applications — Apply machine learning and AI methods to real-world problems and bring them from prototype into reliable production use.
• Technical leadership — Provide technical direction to GEG (and external) scientists and engineers, set architectural standards, mentor team members and orchestrate collaboration across multiple teams and stakeholders.
• Project management & strategic delivery — Steer multi-year strategic projects, including roadmap design and budget responsibility; deliver complex, cross-functional initiatives on time and within scope. Profile You are a lead engineer who combines a strong scientific foundation with substantial hands-on experience in AI, data, and cloud engineering, and who is ready to take both technical and organizational ownership of complex initiatives. The successful candidate brings:
• A Master's degree or PhD in (Geo-)Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science or a closely related quantitative discipline
• 5+ years of professional experience in software engineering, data engineering or a comparable technical role
• Proven experience in technical and people leadership , including guiding engineers, setting architectural direction, establishing engineering standards and mentoring team members
• Solid project management skills, including roadmap design, budget responsibility and the orchestration of cross-functional collaboration across mu

Ingénieur de l'apprentissage de la machine et des systèmes de plomb Ingénieur de l'IA 60%-100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Le groupe ETH Zürich Geothermal Energy & Geofluids (GEG) étudie le transfert d'énergie par fluide réactif et géothermique sous surface, en développant et en utilisant des simulations informatiques, des expériences de laboratoire et des analyses de terrain. Notre objectif est d'acquérir des connaissances fondamentales et de développer des technologies durables pour répondre aux besoins de la société. L'injection ou l'extraction de fluides souterrains induit des changements dans les propriétés du réservoir géologique en raison des processus thermo-hydromécaniques-chimiques-biologiques (THMCB). L'amélioration de la compréhension de ces processus permet le développement de l'extraction d'énergie souterraine et des fluides (par exemple CO2 / H2) et des technologies de stockage de l'énergie ainsi que de leurs technologies de surveillance. Afin de développer et d'améliorer ces technologies souterraines et les solutions de surveillance qui leur sont associées, le groupe GEG met au point et utilise des simulateurs numériques, effectue des analyses sur le terrain et effectue des expériences de transport réactif dans son laboratoire de transport réactif. Ce laboratoire abrite actuellement un scanner à rayons X (XRCT), un laboratoire laser (Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV), Fluorescence induite au laser (LIF)) et bientôt un scanner IRM multinucléide. Contexte du projet En tant qu'ingénieur principal, vous façonnerez la fondation technique du groupe GEG pour les activités liées à l'IA, aux données et au cloud et prendrez en main des initiatives complexes et pluriannuelles. Nous recherchons des candidats ayant une solide expérience en intelligence artificielle, architecture cloud et génie logiciel, ingénierie des données et gouvernance, applications d'intelligence artificielle et d'apprentissage automatique. Description du poste
• L'IA Agentique — Concevoir, construire et exploiter des systèmes d'agents d'IA de qualité de production, couvrant tout le cycle de vie depuis l'architecture cognitive jusqu'à l'observation, la télémétrie et des protocoles rigoureux d'essai et d'évaluation.
• Architecture Cloud & ingénierie logicielle — Concevoir, construire et exploiter des architectures cloud complexes et évolutives composées de services distribués et de microservices. Diriger le développement de logiciels de qualité entreprise et prendre en charge le cycle de vie complet du développement de logiciels (SDLC), de la conception architecturale au déploiement et à l'exploitation.
• Ingénierie et gouvernance des données — Concevoir et exploiter des pipelines de données et des produits de données de bout en bout pour des données structurées et non structurées, y compris, le cas échéant, des données géospatiales. Établir et maintenir des normes solides de gouvernance des données pour assurer la qualité, la sécurité et la conformité dans l'ensemble du paysage de données.
• Applications d'IA & d'apprentissage automatique — Appliquer les méthodes d'IA et d'apprentissage automatique aux problèmes réels et les amener du prototype à une utilisation de production fiable.
• Leadership technique — Fournir une orientation technique aux scientifiques et ingénieurs du GEG (et de l'extérieur), établir des normes architecturales, encadrer les membres de l'équipe et orchestrer la collaboration entre plusieurs équipes et parties prenantes.
• Gestion de projets et exécution stratégique — Projets stratégiques pluriannuels Steer, y compris la conception de feuilles de route et la responsabilité budgétaire; réalisation d'initiatives complexes et interfonctionnelles dans les délais et les limites de la portée. Profil Vous êtes un ingénieur chef de file qui combine une solide fondation scientifique avec une expérience pratique considérable en ingénierie de l'intelligence artificielle, des données et du cloud, et qui est prêt à prendre à la fois la propriété technique et organisationnelle d'initiatives complexes. La candidate reçue apporte :
• Maîtrise ou doctorat en physique, mathématiques, informatique ou discipline quantitative étroitement liée
• 5 ans et plus d'expérience professionnelle en ingénierie des logiciels, en ingénierie des données ou dans un rôle technique comparable
• Expérience éprouvée en matière de leadership technique et humain, y compris les ingénieurs-guides, l'orientation architecturale, l'établissement de normes d'ingénierie et les membres de l'équipe de mentorat
• Des compétences solides en gestion de projet, y compris la conception d'une feuille de route, la responsabilité budgétaire et l'orchestration d'une collaboration interfonctionnelle dans l'ensemble

chevron ha lasciato Panoramica Chevron ha lasciato Panoramica Assistenza per i materiali da costruzione negli Studio Foundations (m/w/d) 40%-60%, Zurigo, stampa limitata Stampa Per il primo anno corso «Studio Foundations» stiamo guardando 1. Giugno 2026 o d'accordo a:n Architetto:in quanto scientifico:r Assistent:r per la gestione del dipartimento di materiali da costruzione. Le "Studio Foundations" è stato insegnato per la prima volta nel semestre autunnale 2025 come primo corso di anno nel curriculum Bachelor riveduto in Architettura presso ETH Zurich. Il corso fonda il progetto architettonico per circa 400 studenti D-ARCH ed è sviluppato congiuntamente da un collettivo di otto professori: ins, che insegna le aree del design (Roger Boltshauser), Computational Design (Fabio Gramazio), costruzione (Daniel Mettler), materiali da costruzione (Jacqueline Pauli), struttura (Philippe Block), sistemi energetici e climatici (Arno Schlüter Delke) Il concetto didattico del corso si basa sull'integrazione di varie discipline all'interno dell'insegnamento del design. Questo approccio orientato alle competenze promuove una comprensione complessa e sistemica dell'architettura e consente agli studenti di affrontare le sfide architettoniche da diverse prospettive e di affrontare le questioni attuali. Il focus è sulla costruzione semplice e sostenibile in un linguaggio architettonico contemporaneo. Le "Studio Foundations" si concentrano sugli studenti e orchestrano l'applicazione di conoscenze e competenze disciplinari nel design su due semestri. Attraverso l'accesso diretto e sensuale, gli studenti acquisiscono concetti di base come il contesto e il paesaggio, il clima e l'energia, la luce e lo spazio, il significato e la forma, così come il materiale e la struttura e comprendono la loro influenza sul design architettonico. Il corso sottolinea il pensiero interdisciplinare e quindi critico combinando concetti astratti con esperienze reali in diversi standard – dagli spazi abitativi ai paesaggi urbani. La sedia di Jacqueline Pauli è responsabile di fornire conoscenze di base all'intera gamma di materiali da costruzione. Questo si svolge oltre 2-3 settimane di attenzione nel semestre autunnale e un trasferimento diretto ai progetti di progettazione. Nelle settimane di messa a fuoco, gli studenti sviluppano contenuti per un materiale specifico sulle aree tematiche delle proprietà di materiale tecnico, così come l'estrazione di materie prime, processi di produzione, capacità circolatoria e impronta ecologica. Descrizione del lavoro
• Come assistente scientifico: nel campo dei materiali da costruzione, sei responsabile del contenuto e della preparazione formale e della mediazione. Conducono lo scambio con le altre discipline e stabiliscono le relazioni e le interfacce.

PhD Posizione: Rilevazione sismica, localizzazione e caratterizzazione di eventi di esplosione negli impianti di stoccaggio delle munizioni sotterranee 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Il Servizio sismico svizzero (SED) dell'ETH Zurigo invita le applicazioni per una posizione di dottorato all'interno di un progetto pluriennale di ricerca applicata sulla rilevazione, localizzazione e interpretazione di eventi di esplosione negli impianti di stoccaggio delle munizioni sotterranee. La posizione è incorporata in un progetto collaborativo con l'armasuisse Science and Technology e partner dell'industria e delle forze armate svizzere. La ricerca contribuisce alla fondazione scientifica di sistemi di monitoraggio e di cambiamento rapido per le infrastrutture sotterranee. Sfondo del progetto Le tecnologie di rilevamento sismico e fibra ottica offrono soluzioni promettenti per il rilevamento in tempo reale, la localizzazione e la caratterizzazione di esplosioni e relativi eventi pericolosi in strutture sotterranee. Il progetto mira a valutare le tecnologie dei sensori, progettare e ottimizzare le reti di monitoraggio multisensoriale e sviluppare algoritmi di rilevamento e localizzazione avanzati adattati a geometrie sotterranee complesse 3D. La ricerca sarà condotta in stretta collaborazione tra BedrettoLab gestito da ETH e gli impianti di test sotterranei Hondrich gestiti da armasuisse. Il progetto si estende tra il 2026 e il 2029 e comprende campagne sperimentali, installazioni sul campo e raccolta dati, elaborazione dati, sviluppo algoritmico e ottimizzazione del sistema. Descrizione del lavoro
• Campagne sperimentali e valutazione dei sensori: progettazione e analisi delle esplosioni di prova controllate nel BedrettoLab, valutazione dei sensori sismici (ad esempio, diversi tipi di sismometri e tecnologia di rilevamento acustico distribuita)
• Progettazione e installazione di un Multi-Sensor Monitoring Network negli impianti di test sotterranei di Hondrich: definizione della geometria ottimale dei sensori, partecipazione alle installazioni sul campo, calibrazione dei modelli di velocità utilizzando eventi di prova controllati e controllo della qualità dell'acquisizione dati
• Algoritmo Sviluppo: Integrazione di flussi di dati multisensori in framework software sismatici (per esempio SeisComP), modellazione di propagazione dell'onda in complesse geometrie 3D, sviluppo e ottimizzazione di algoritmi di rilevamento eventi, metodi di localizzazione ad alta precisione, magnitudine degli eventi e tecniche di caratterizzazione delle sorgenti, e contributi all'implementazione di sistemi di allarme in tempo reale
• Contributo all'implementazione del sistema di allarme ottimizzato per i costi: l'ottimizzazione dei layout dei sensori ridotti, l'ottimizzazione dei concetti di monitoraggio semplici da usare per le strutture sotterranee future e la stretta collaborazione con vari stakeholder (imprese di ingegneria, forze armate svizzere, armasuisse, collaboratori internazionali) per garantire un efficiente roll-out del sistema Profilo

PhD Position: Seismic Detection, Localization and Characterization of Explosion Events in Underground Ammunition Storage Facilities 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Swiss Seismological Service (SED) at ETH Zurich invites applications for a PhD position within a multi-year applied research project on the detection, localization and interpretation of explosion events in underground ammunition storage facilities. The position is embedded in a collaborative project with armasuisse Science and Technology and partners from industry and the Swiss Armed Forces. The research contributes to the scientific foundation of monitoring and rapid altering systems for underground infrastructure. Project background Seismic and fiber-optic sensing technologies offer promising solutions for the real-time detection, localization and characterization of explosions and related hazardous events in underground facilities. The project aims to evaluate sensor technologies, design and optimize multi-sensor monitoring networks, and develop advanced detection and localization algorithms adapted to complex 3D underground geometries. The research will be conducted in close collaboration between BedrettoLab run by ETH and the underground test facilities Hondrich run by armasuisse. The project spans between 2026 and 2029 and includes experimental campaigns, field installations and data collection, data processing, algorithm development and system optimization. Job description
• Experimental Campaigns and Sensor Evaluation: Design and analysis of controlled test explosions in the BedrettoLab, evaluation of seismic sensors (e.g., different types of seismometers as well as distributed acoustic sensing technology)
• Design and Installation of a Multi-Sensor Monitoring Network in the Hondrich underground test facilities: Definition of optimal sensor geometry, participation in field installations, calibration of velocity models using controlled test events and quality control of data acquisition
• Algorithm Development: Integration of multi-sensor data streams into seismological software frameworks (e.g., SeisComP), wave propagation modeling in complex 3D geometries, development and optimization of event detection algorithms, high-precision localization methods, event magnitude as well as source characterization techniques, and contributions to the implementation of real-time alarm systems
• Contributions to implementation of cost-optimized alarm system: Cost-benefit optimiziation of reduced sensor layouts, optimization of simple-to-use monitoring concepts for future underground facilities, and close collaboration with various stakeholders (engineering companies, Swiss Armed Forces, armasuisse, international collaborators) to ensure efficient roll-out of the system Profile

One particular area of interest is the design and fabrication of active structures through hybrid production methods. We're looking for a highly motivated Postdoc to develop methods for direct ink writing of thermo-electric materials onto non-planar metallic substrates. Project background The position takes place within the recently awarded Meta.Morphos project, funded by the ESA ESDI Phi-Lab Switzerland. The overarching goal of the project is to develop methods to design and produce thermally actuated structures and mechanisms incorporating thermo-electric materials. Such devices have interesting applications in space under significant weight, volumetric, power, and resource constraints. The project consortium includes multiple labs at ETH Zurich and research partners at Inspire AG, as well as industrialization partners. The main focus of this position will be to develop materials and methods for directly depositing and fabricating thermo-electric devices onto non-planar metallic substrates. In a parallel track, the team will develop techniques for the design and manufacture of the structures with predictable material properties. Finally, the two technologies will be combined to create integrated devices. The industrial partners will provide application-specific use cases, environmental testing expertise and facilities, and validation. Job description
• Characterization of powdered materials for ink formulation
• DIW process development for ceramic and TE materials, including parameters optimization and evaluation of resolution
• Setup, programming, and operation of DIW equipment
• Determination of optimal debinding and sintering steps
• Characterization of the sintered materials: density, microstructure, defects, shrinkage, possible distortions and preliminary thermoelectrical properties
• Running validation studies under simulated environmental conditions
• Assisting with industrial transfer of the developed technologies
• Publishing research findings in leading international journals and presenting at conferences
• Active involvement in teaching and lab duties outside of the project (~15-20% of working time) Profile
• PhD in Material Science and Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Physics or Chemistry

Postdoc en écriture directe d'encre des matériaux thermo-électriciens 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Le Advanced Manufacturing Lab (am.) du Département d'ingénierie mécanique et des procédés (D-MAVT) d'ETH Zurich développe des méthodes et des systèmes de fabrication avancés pour surmonter les limites des technologies de traitement des matériaux d'aujourd'hui. Un domaine d'intérêt particulier est la conception et la fabrication de structures actives par des méthodes de production hybrides. Nous recherchons un Postdoc très motivé pour développer des méthodes d'écriture directe d'encre de matériaux thermo-électriques sur des substrats métalliques non planaires. Contexte du projet Le poste a lieu dans le Meta récemment décerné. Projet Morphos, financé par l'ESA ESI Phi-Lab Suisse. L'objectif principal du projet est d'élaborer des méthodes pour concevoir et produire des structures et des mécanismes à action thermique comportant des matériaux thermoélectriques. Ces dispositifs ont des applications intéressantes dans l'espace sous des contraintes importantes de poids, volumétriques, de puissance et de ressources. Le consortium de projets comprend plusieurs laboratoires à l'ETH Zurich et des partenaires de recherche à Inspire AG, ainsi que des partenaires d'industrialisation. L'objectif principal de cette position sera de développer des matériaux et des méthodes pour déposer et fabriquer directement des dispositifs thermoélectriques sur des substrats métalliques non planaires. En parallèle, l'équipe développera des techniques de conception et de fabrication des structures aux propriétés matérielles prévisibles. Enfin, les deux technologies seront combinées pour créer des dispositifs intégrés. Les partenaires industriels fourniront des cas d'utilisation spécifiques à l'application, des compétences et des installations en matière d'essais environnementaux et de validation. All'incrocio tra accademia, industria e imprenditorialità, si tradurrà ricerca AI all'avanguardia in modelli di partnership convincenti e costruire relazioni a lungo termine con le principali organizzazioni globali. Potrai collaborare a stretto contatto con la leadership ETH AI Center, Swiss National AI Institute (SNAI), e le istituzioni partner come l'EPFL AI Center - coinvolgendo ogni giorno con professori e ricercatori ETH, leader C-suite nelle aziende partner, controparti SNAI e EPFL AI Center, e leader di innovazione in tutto l'ecosistema svizzero e europeo AI. We strive to push the boundaries of AI research, foster innovation, and drive impactful projects. As the Industry Partnership Lead, you will have the unique opportunity to work at the forefront of AI research and industry applications. Project background We are looking for a hands-on leader to own and scale the ETH AI Center’s industry engagement function and develop long-term, impactful partnerships. You will operate as a player-coach: driving high-value partnerships end-to-end yourself while building pragmatic structures, processes, and the team setup needed to scale. You should be equally comfortable in a boardroom closing a six-figure collaboration as you are refining a pitch deck, structuring a CRM, or unblocking an internal stakeholder. At the intersection of academia, industry, and entrepreneurship, you will translate cutting-edge AI research into compelling partnership models and build long-term relationships with leading global organizations. You will collaborate closely with ETH AI Center leadership, Swiss National AI Institute (SNAI), and partner institutions such as the EPFL AI Center - engaging daily with ETH professors and researchers, C-suite leaders at partner companies, SNAI and EPFL AI Center counterparts, and innovation leaders across the Swiss and European AI ecosystem. • Drive revenue growth by owning and expanding third-party funding across the ETH AI Center and SNAI, with clear OKRs tracked monthly, quarterly, and annually — fueling the center's mission to strengthen Switzerland's AI ecosystem.

• Shape the partner journey by designing how companies mature their AI capabilities over time through the partnership — from first engagement, to becoming AI-native organizations, to leveraging frontier capabilities such as large-scale AI and open-source foundation models alongside ETH researchers.
• Grow and retain long-term partners through regular expectation management and joint goal-setting, helping them navigate AI trends, spot opportunities for joint research, and learn from both leading ETH researchers and peer companies — making them visible in the ecosystem and accelerating Switzerland's transformation into an AI-native economy.
• Lead and scale the partnerships team as a player-coach, setting the standard through execution while building scalable processes, CRM systems, and reporting infrastructure for data-driven decision-making.
• Align internal stakeholders across ETH, SNAI, and partner institutions, and represent the ETH AI Center externally at senior-level meetings and events, positioning it as the leading partner for enabling AI transformation in Switzerland and beyond. Profile
• 6+ years of experience in business development, partnerships, or sales in complex environments (e.g. deep tech, research, enterprise, or startups)
• Experience in leading a team (3-10 people)

• Strong ability to operate both strategically and operationally – you think in systems but execute hands-on
• Proven track record of personally closing high-value, multi-stakeholder deals
• Experience building or scaling partnership, sales, or business development functions

chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht PhD Posizione degli studenti in Clima Extremes and Migration Research 100%, Zurigo, stampa a tempo determinato Drucken Il Gruppo di Politica Pubblica e il Laboratorio di Politica Immigrazione presso ETH Zurich invitano le domande per una posizione degli studenti PhD a partire dal 2026 settembre o su una data concordata. Sarete parte di un team di ricerca collaborativo e interdisciplinare che studia la migrazione e la politica pubblica con metodi di scienza sociale quantitativi. Il vostro progetto PhD si trova al nexus della ricerca sulle migrazioni e degli estremi climatici ed è incorporato nel programma di ricerca NCCR CLIM+ su Climate Extremes and Society , una grande iniziativa di ricerca che riunisce i ricercatori attraverso le discipline e le istituzioni svizzere per studiare gli estremi del clima e rafforzare la resilienza sociale. Basandosi sulla competenza del Laboratorio di Politica dell’immigrazione, la vostra ricerca estenderà il nostro programma in questa nuova area esaminando come gli shock legati al clima possono influenzare la mobilità attraverso e all’interno dei confini. Descrizione del lavoro Stiamo cercando uno studente di dottorato per contribuire al nostro programma di ricerca sugli estremi climatici e la migrazione.
• Il progetto mira a fornire prove causali sul modo in cui e come gli estremi climatici influenzano la migrazione, un'area in cui le prove esistenti rimangono limitate
• Un componente fondamentale della posizione coinvolgerà la combinazione dei dati di migrazione globale con dati ad alta risoluzione di estinzione del clima e strategie di identificazione credibili per esaminare come gli shock ambientali influenzano diverse forme di migrazione, tra cui la ricerca di asilo, i movimenti dei rifugiati e la migrazione del lavoro
• Oltre a questo progetto, avrete la flessibilità per sviluppare in modo indipendente ulteriori argomenti di ricerca allineati con la missione La posizione si trova nel team di Dominik Hangartner dell'ETH di Zurigo, con opportunità di collaborare con i ricercatori affiliati attraverso il programma NCCR CLIM+
• • I candidati più forti avranno la maggior parte dei seguenti:
• Laurea magistrale in un programma di scienze sociali con una preferenza per la scienza politica, l’economia, la sociologia, la scienza dei dati, la scienza computazionale, o in una disciplina strettamente correlata
• Formazione quantitativa forte e conoscenza dei metodi statistici per l’inferenza causale dai dati osservazionali
• Forte controllo di una lingua di programmazione statistica In linea con i nostri valori, ETH Zurich incoraggia una cultura inclusiva. Promuoviamo l'uguaglianza di opportunità, la diversità di valore e nutrire un ambiente di lavoro e di apprendimento in cui i diritti e la dignità di tutto il nostro staff e gli studenti sono rispettati. Visita il nostro sito Equal Opportunities and Diversity per scoprire come garantiamo un ambiente equo e aperto che permetta a tutti di crescere e fiorire. La sostenibilità è un valore fondamentale per noi – stiamo costantemente lavorando verso un futuro neutro dal clima. Curioso? Anche noi. PhD Student Position in Climate Extremes and Migration Research 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Public Policy Group and the Immigration Policy Lab at ETH Zurich invite applications for a PhD student position starting in September 2026 or on a mutually agreed date. You will be part of a collaborative and interdisciplinary research team studying migration and public policy with quantitative social science methods. Your PhD project sits at the nexus of migration research and climate extremes and is embedded in the NCCR CLIM+ research program on Climate Extremes and Society , a major research initiative that brings together researchers across disciplines and Swiss institutions to study climate extremes and strengthen societal resilience. Building on the Immigration Policy Lab’s expertise in migration, your research will extend our agenda into this new area by examining how climate-related shocks may affect mobility across and within borders. Job description We are looking for a PhD student to contribute to our research program on climate extremes and migration.
• The project aims to provide causal evidence on whether and how climate extremes influence migration, an area where existing evidence remains limited
• One core component of the position will involve combining global migration data with high-resolution climate-extremes data and credible identification strategies to examine how environmental shocks influence different forms of migration, including asylum seeking, refugee movements, and labor migration
• Beyond this project, you will have flexibility to independently develop additional research topics aligned with the mission of IPL and the NCCR CLIM+
• The position is located in the team of Dominik Hangartner at ETH Zurich, with opportunities to collaborate with affiliated researchers across the NCCR CLIM+ program
• In addition to research, you will have small administrative and teaching responsibilities amounting to 10% of your time Profile Strong candidates will have most of the following:
• Master’s degree in a social science program with a preference for Political Science, Economics, Sociology, Data Science, Computational Social Science, or in a closely related discipline
• Strong quantitative training and knowledge of statistical methods for causal inference from observational data
• Strong command of a statistical programming language (preferably R), and ability to use modern coding tools effectively
• Experience with geospatial data
• Experience or interest in studying migration, forced displacement, asylum processes, climate change, climate impacts, and related topics
• Ability to collaborate effectively with project team members
• Interest in transdisciplinary collaboration across the social and natural science
• Proficiency and excellent writing skills in English
• Experience of or interest in translating basic research into policy-relevant insights Workplace Workplace We offer
• Highly collaborative work environment within a very motivated and supportive team
• Opportunity to develop a network with academics and practitioners
• Career mentoring by experienced researchers
• Salary and pension benefits according to ETH standards
• Research and travel allowance chevron_right Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future . Curious? So are we. chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht PhD Student Position in Climate Extremes and Migration Research 100%, Zurich, tirage à durée déterminée Drucken Le Public Policy Group et l'Immigration Policy Lab à l'ETH Zurich invitent les candidats à un doctorat à partir de septembre 2026 ou à une date convenue d'un commun accord. Vous ferez partie d'une équipe de recherche collaborative et interdisciplinaire qui étudiera la migration et les politiques publiques avec des méthodes quantitatives de sciences sociales. Votre projet de doctorat s'inscrit dans le lien entre la recherche sur les migrations et les extrêmes climatiques et s'inscrit dans le programme de recherche NCCR CLIM+ sur les extrêmes climatiques et la société , une initiative de recherche majeure qui rassemble des chercheurs de diverses disciplines et institutions suisses pour étudier les extrêmes climatiques et renforcer la résilience sociétale. Forte de l'expertise du laboratoire de la politique d'immigration en matière de migration, votre recherche étendra notre programme dans ce nouveau domaine en examinant comment les chocs climatiques peuvent affecter la mobilité à travers et à l'intérieur des frontières. Description du poste Nous cherchons un doctorant pour contribuer à notre programme de recherche sur les extrêmes climatiques et la migration.
• Le projet vise à fournir des données causales sur l'influence des extrêmes climatiques sur la migration, un domaine où les données existantes demeurent limitées
• Un élément essentiel de la position consistera à combiner les données sur la migration mondiale avec des données à haute résolution sur les extrêmes climatiques et des stratégies d'identification crédibles pour examiner comment les chocs environnementaux influencent les différentes formes de migration, y compris la demande d'asile, les mouvements de réfugiés et la migration de main-d'œuvre
• Au-delà de ce projet, vous aurez la flexibilité de développer indépendamment des sujets de recherche supplémentaires alignés sur la mission de l'IPL et du CCNR CLIM+
• Le poste est situé dans l'équipe de Dominik Hangartner à l'ETH Zurich, avec l'occasion de collaborer avec des chercheurs affiliés dans le cadre du programme CLIM+ du CCNR
• En plus de la recherche, vous aurez de petites responsabilités administratives et d'enseignement équivalant à 10 % de votre temps Profil Des candidats forts auront la plupart des fonctions suivantes :
• Maîtrise en sciences sociales avec une préférence pour les sciences politiques, l'économie, la sociologie, la science des données, la science sociale computationnelle ou dans une discipline étroitement liée
• Formation quantitative solide et connaissance des méthodes statistiques pour l'inférence causale à partir de données d'observation
• Forte maîtrise d'un langage de programmation statistique (de préférence R) et capacité d'utiliser efficacement les outils modernes de codage
• Expérience des données géospatiales
• Expérience ou intérêt pour l'étude des migrations, des déplacements forcés, des processus d'asile, des changements climatiques, des impacts climatiques et des sujets connexes
• Capacité de collaborer efficacement avec les membres de l'équipe de projet
• Intérêt pour la collaboration transdisciplinaire dans le domaine des sciences sociales et naturelles
• Compétence et excellentes compétences en écriture en anglais
• Expérience ou intérêt pour la traduction de la recherche fondamentale en informations pertinentes sur les politiques en milieu de travail Nous offrons
• Un environnement de travail hautement collaboratif au sein d'une équipe très motivée et solidaire
• Possibilité de développer un réseau avec des universitaires et des praticiens
• Co Conformément à nos valeurs , ETH Zurich encourage une culture inclusive. descriptionByLocale.en:
## Internship - Measurement Systems for Industrial Process Monitoring

**100%, Zurich, fixed-term**

---

## Descrizione

inspire AG è il centro di competenza svizzero leader per l’innovazione di prodotto e la manifattura avanzata. Come partner strategico dell’ETH Zurich, la nostra missione è trasferire conoscenze e tecnologie dalla ricerca accademica alle industrie meccaniche, elettriche e metallurgiche svizzere.

### Contesto del progetto

Cerchiamo uno stagista motivato per supportare l’allestimento, l’integrazione e la validazione di sistemi di misurazione per un progetto di ricerca orientato all’industria nel campo della manifattura avanzata. L’attenzione è rivolta alla preparazione di un sistema di sensori e monitoraggio per le prime prove sperimentali su un banco di prova industriale.

---

## Mansioni

- Definire parametri di processo e metriche di qualità rilevanti per la validazione sperimentale.
- Selezionare, posizionare e integrare tecnologie di misurazione adatte, come sensori di pressione e flusso, sistemi di imaging e attrezzature aggiuntive per il monitoraggio del processo.
- Implementare l’architettura di acquisizione dati, inclusi interfacce hardware, frequenze di campionamento, elaborazione dei segnali e registrazione automatica dei dati.
- Integrare il sistema di misurazione in un ambiente di banco di prova industriale e preparare prove preliminari rappresentative.

---

## Requisiti

### Esperienza richiesta

- Cittadinanza CH/EU/EFTA o valido permesso di lavoro svizzero.
- Laurea triennale/magistrale in Ingegneria Meccanica, Meccatronica, Ingegneria di Processo, Fisica o discipline affini.
- Interesse per il lavoro sperimentale, la tecnologia di misurazione, i sensori o i processi di manifattura industriale.
- Conoscenze di base di programmazione e analisi dati, preferibilmente in Python, MATLAB o LabVIEW.
- Esperienza con sistemi di acquisizione dati, sistemi di imaging, misurazione di particelle o flussi, o metrologia di superficie/processo è un plus.

### Competenze personali richieste

- Automotivato, strutturato e pratico in ambienti di laboratorio e banco di prova.
- Forte mentalità analitica con abitudini di lavoro sperimentale precise e affidabili.
- Comfort con il lavoro in team interdisciplinari orientati all’industria.
- Buone capacità comunicative in inglese o tedesco.

---

## Cosa offriamo

Questo stage della durata di 6 mesi offre un’opportunità unica per lavorare all’interfaccia tra ricerca applicata, tecnologia di misurazione e sviluppo di processi industriali. Contribuirai direttamente allo sviluppo di un framework di misurazione integrato che supporta la comprensione, l’ottimizzazione e la validazione dei modelli di processo.

Curioso? Anche noi.

---
## Contatto

Inviaci la tua candidatura completa (lettera di presentazione, trascrizioni, CV, referenze) con riferimento **"Measurement Systems Internship"** al nostro dipartimento HR (hr@inspire.ch).

Per domande di carattere tecnico, contatta il Dr. Markus Maier, Head of Machine Concepts (markus.maier@inspire.ch).

La data di inizio è da concordare. Visita anche i nostri siti [www.inspire.ch](http://www.inspire.ch) e [https://mohr.ethz.ch/](https://mohr.ethz.ch/).

Descrizione Posizione del dottorato: Modellazione di attrito in sospensioni colloidali 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Alla cattedra di Solid Mechanics (SMEC) dell'Istituto per i materiali da costruzione dell'ETH di Zurigo, ci proponiamo di capire come i materiali deformano, degradano, rompono e infine falliscono. La nostra ricerca è guidata dalla curiosità sui meccanismi fisici che sottomettono al fallimento e dall'ambizione di tradurre questa comprensione in materiali e strutture più affidabili e resilienti. Combinando la modellazione numerica, gli esperimenti di laboratorio e le analisi teoriche, cerchiamo di collegare i processi microscopici con il comportamento macroscopico dei sistemi ingegneristici e naturali e di sviluppare strumenti predittivi per il fallimento meccanico. Il nostro team è altamente interdisciplinare e internazionale, che riunisce ricercatori con sfondi in scienza dei materiali, meccanica e fisica applicata. Lavoriamo attraverso una vasta gamma di argomenti, tra cui la meccanica dei sistemi di particelle (colloidale e granulare), materiali progettati e topologicamente interlocked, la meccanica della fragilità nel collagene, la meccanica dei terremoti, la frattura dei materiali morbidi e la modellazione del fallimento nei processi multifisici come la degradazione del cemento a corrosione. Ciò che unisce questi sforzi è una curiosità condivisa sul perché i materiali complessi falliscono e l'impegno a sviluppare nuovi concetti, esperimenti e modelli che avanzano la nostra comprensione della meccanica fallita. Stiamo cercando uno studente di dottorato motivato e innovativo con uno sfondo in meccanica computazionale per lavorare su un progetto focalizzato sulla meccanica dei sistemi colloidali. Il candidato PhD condurrà la ricerca in un progetto collaborativo con i partner del Dipartimento dei Materiali ETH per scoprire i ruoli di attrito scorrevole e rotolante, e la loro combinazione, nelle proprietà reologiche delle sospensioni colloidali. descriptionByLocale.en:
PhD position: Modeling friction in colloidal suspensions 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken At the Professorship of Solid Mechanics (SMEC) in the Institute for Building Materials at ETH Zurich, we aim to understand how materials deform, degrade, break, and ultimately fail. Our research is driven by curiosity about the physical mechanisms that underlie failure and by the ambition to translate this understanding into more reliable and resilient materials and structures. By combining numerical modeling, laboratory experiments, and theoretical analyses, we seek to link microscopic processes with the macroscopic behavior of both engineering and natural systems and develop predictive tools for mechanical failure. Our team is highly interdisciplinary and international, bringing together researchers with backgrounds in materials science, mechanics, and applied physics. We work across a broad range of topics, including the mechanics of particle systems (colloidal and granular), architected and topologically interlocked materials, the mechanics of fragility in collagen, the mechanics of earthquakes, fracture of soft materials, and modeling failure in multiphysical processes such as corrosion-driven degradation of concrete. What unites these efforts is a shared curiosity about why complex materials fail and a commitment to developing new concepts, experiments, and models that advance our understanding of failure mechanics. We are seeking a motivated, innovative PhD student with a background in computational mechanics to work on a project focused on the mechanics of colloidal systems. The PhD candidate will conduct research in a collaborative project with partners from the ETH Department of Materials to uncover the roles of sliding and rolling friction, and their combination, in the rheological properties of colloidal suspensions. Job description
• You will conduct a computational and theoretical investigation of the influence of inter-particle friction on the rheology of concentrated suspensions
• The work will focus on applying physics-based models that connect behavior across scales, from the geometry of single colloidal particles to the macroscopic response of the suspension
• Your responsibilities include implementing coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations and performing rigorous verification and validation using datasets provided by our collaborators
• The candidate will work in close collaboration with experimental researchers within the project, providing modeling insights and helping to interpret experimental observations
• The position provides a stimulating environment for scientific growth and collaboration Profile

Unsere Forschung wird von der Neugier über die physikalischen Mechanismen, die Misserfolg und den Ehrgeiz, dieses Verständnis in zuverlässigere und widerstandsfähigere Materialien und Strukturen zu übersetzen, angetrieben. Durch die Kombination von numerischer Modellierung, Laborexperimenten und theoretischen Analysen versuchen wir, mikroskopische Prozesse mit dem makroskopischen Verhalten sowohl technischer als auch natürlicher Systeme zu verknüpfen und prädiktive Werkzeuge für mechanischen Ausfall zu entwickeln. Unser Team ist sehr interdisziplinär und international und verbindet Forscher mit Hintergründen in der Materialwissenschaft, Mechanik und angewandter Physik. Descrizione Position du doctorat: Modélisation du frottement dans les suspensions colloïdales 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Au Professeur de Mécanique Solide (SMEC) à l'Institut des matériaux de construction à l'ETH Zurich, nous voulons comprendre comment les matériaux déforment, dégradent, brisent et finalement échouent. Nos recherches sont motivées par la curiosité au sujet des mécanismes physiques qui sous-tendent l'échec et par l'ambition de traduire cette compréhension en matériaux et structures plus fiables et plus résistants. En combinant la modélisation numérique, les expériences de laboratoire et les analyses théoriques, nous cherchons à lier les processus microscopiques au comportement macroscopique des systèmes d'ingénierie et des systèmes naturels et à développer des outils prédictifs pour la défaillance mécanique. Notre équipe est hautement interdisciplinaire et internationale, réunissant des chercheurs ayant des connaissances en sciences des matériaux, en mécanique et en physique appliquée. Nous travaillons sur un large éventail de sujets, y compris la mécanique des systèmes de particules (colloïdaux et granulaires), les matériaux architecturés et topologiques entrelacés, la mécanique de la fragilité du collagène, la mécanique des tremblements de terre, la fracture des matériaux mous et l'échec de la modélisation dans des processus multiphysiques tels que la dégradation du béton par la corrosion. Ce qui unit ces efforts est une curiosité commune sur la raison pour laquelle les matériaux complexes échouent et un engagement à développer de nouveaux concepts, des expériences et des modèles qui font progresser notre compréhension de la mécanique de défaillance. Nous recherchons un doctorant motivé et innovateur ayant une formation en mécanique informatique pour travailler sur un projet axé sur la mécanique des systèmes colloïdaux. Le candidat au doctorat effectuera des recherches dans le cadre d'un projet de collaboration avec des partenaires du département des matériaux de l'ETH afin de découvrir les rôles du frottement glissant et du roulement, et leur combinaison, dans les propriétés rhéologiques des suspensions colloïdales.
