descriptionByLocale.it:
Descrizione Posizione del dottorato in studi numerici e sperimentali di sistemi granulari non sferica e deformabile 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo ETH Zurich è una delle università leader a livello mondiale ed è rinomata per la sua eccellenza nell'istruzione, nella ricerca fondamentale all'avanguardia e negli sforzi per mettere in pratica nuove conoscenze e innovazioni. Il Laboratorio di Scienza e Ingegneria Energetica (D-MAVT) sta lavorando attivamente allo sviluppo di strumenti numerici e sperimentali per sondare sistemi granulari mono e multifase (particolati). Sfondo del progetto I sistemi granulari sono onnipresenti in natura (ad esempio valanghe rocciose o dune) e di fondamentale importanza per l'industria. Tuttavia, nonostante il loro uso diffuso e il loro verificarsi, molti fenomeni importanti, come la segregazione, le instabilità della superficie o il jamming, cioè la transizione tra uno stato fluido- a uno stato solido, sono scarsamente compresi. Questo progetto esplora specificamente l'effetto della deformabilità delle particelle e della non-sfericità sulle dinamiche e reologia dei sistemi granulari. Le particelle flessibili si deformano sotto stress, mentre la deformazione a sua volta colpisce le forze di contatto e la trasmissione dello stress dando origine a fenomeni reologici complessi come il jamming transitorio o l'ordine orientativo indotto dallo stress. Anche se deformabili, i sistemi di particelle asferiche dovrebbero essere ricchi di fenomeni fisici, sono stati in gran parte evitati a causa di difficoltà nel fare misurazioni sperimentali in tali sistemi e nella loro descrizione numerica. Questa posizione PhD fa parte di un progetto congiunto che combina le competenze di due gruppi di ricerca ( Laboratory of Energy Science and Engineering , Prof. Müller e l'Institute for Biomedical Imaging Magnetic Resonance Technology , Prof. Prüssmann) e gli studenti di dottorato assunti dai due gruppi coinvolti dovrebbero collaborare quotidianamente. Descrizione del lavoro L'obiettivo dello studente di dottorato assunto dal Laboratorio di Scienze e Ingegneria dell'Energia è quello di
• Avanzare strumenti numerici per modellare sistemi granulari non sferica e deformabile
• Stabilire tecniche sperimentali basate sulle telecamere come la foto-elasticimetria per determinare le forze di contatto e i campi di stress in tali sistemi
• Sviluppare e utilizzare modelli basati su machine-learning per correlare deformazione delle particelle e forze di contatto nei sistemi 3D Profilo

PhD position in numerical and experimental studies of non-spherical and deformable granular systems 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken ETH Zurich is one of the worldwide leading universities and is renowned for its excellence in education, cutting-edge fundamental research and efforts to put new knowledge and innovations directly into practice. The Laboratory of Energy Science and Engineering (D-MAVT) is working actively on developing numerical and experimental tools to probe single- and multiphase granular (particulate) systems. Project background Granular systems are ubiquitous in nature (e.g. rock avalanches or dunes) and of fundamental importance to industry. However, despite their widespread use and occurrence, many important phenomena, such as segregation, surface instabilities or jamming, i.e. the transition between a fluid- to solid-like state, are poorly understood. This project explores specifically the effect of particle deformability and non-sphericity on the dynamics and rheology of granular systems. Flexible particles deform under stress, while the deformation in turn affects the contact forces and stress transmission giving rise to complex rheological phenomena such as transient jamming or stress-induced orientational ordering. Although deformable, aspherical particle systems are expected to be rich in physical phenomena, they have been largely avoided owing to difficulties in making experimental measurements in such systems and in their numerical description. This PhD position is part of a joint project that combines the expertise of two research groups ( Laboratory of Energy Science and Engineering , Prof. Müller and the Institute for Biomedical Imaging Magnetic Resonance Technology , Prof. Prüssmann) and the PhD students hired by the two groups involved are expected to collaborate on a daily basis. Job description The objective of the PhD student hired by the Laboratory of Energy Science and Engineering is to
• Advance numerical tools to model non-spherical and deformable granular systems
• Establish camera-based experimental techniques such as photo-elasticimetry to determine contact forces and stress fields in such systems
• Develop and use machine-learning based models to correlate particle deformation and contact forces in 3D systems Profile
• Applicants for this PhD position are expected to have a very good MSc degree in Mechanical Engineering, Physics or related disciplines
• Previous experience in numerical modelling or imaging techniques is desirable

Beschreibung PhD-Position in numerischen und experimentellen Studien nicht-sphärischen und verformbaren körnigen Systemen 100%, Zürich, befristet Drucken Drucken Die ETH Zürich ist eine der weltweit führenden Universitäten und ist bekannt für ihre Exzellenz in der Bildung, innovative Grundlagenforschung und die Bemühungen, neue Kenntnisse und Innovationen direkt in die Praxis umzusetzen. Das Laboratory of Energy Science and Engineering (D-MAVT) arbeitet aktiv an der Entwicklung von numerischen und experimentellen Werkzeugen, um ein- und mehrphasige körnige (partikuläre) Systeme zu Sonden. Projekt Hintergrund Granularsysteme sind in der Natur allgegenwärtig (z.B. Stein Lawinen oder Dünen) und von grundlegender Bedeutung für die Industrie. Trotz ihres weit verbreiteten Einsatzes und Auftretens sind jedoch viele wichtige Phänomene wie Seigerung, Oberflächeninstabilitäten oder Verklemmung, d.h. der Übergang zwischen einem fluid- zu festartigen Zustand schlecht verstanden. Dieses Projekt untersucht gezielt die Wirkung von Partikelverformbarkeit und Nicht-Sphericität auf die Dynamik und Rheologie von körnigen Systemen. Flexible Partikel deformieren sich unter Spannung, während die Verformung wiederum die Kontaktkräfte und die Spannungsübertragung beeinflusst, was zu komplexen rheologischen Erscheinungen wie z.B. transientes Verklemmen oder spannungsinduzierte Orientierungsordnungen führt. Obwohl verformbare, asphärische Partikelsysteme an physikalischen Phänomenen reich sein sollen, wurden sie aufgrund von Schwierigkeiten bei der experimentellen Messung in solchen Systemen und ihrer numerischen Beschreibung weitgehend vermieden. Diese PhD-Position ist Teil eines gemeinsamen Projekts, das die Expertise zweier Forschungsgruppen (Labor of Energy Science and Engineering, Prof. Müller und das Institut für biomedizinische Bildgebung Magnetische Resonanztechnik, Prof. Prüssmann) und die von den beiden beteiligten Gruppen eingestellten Doktoranden sollen täglich zusammenarbeiten. Descrizione Position du doctorat dans les études numériques et expérimentales de systèmes granulaires non sphériques et déformables 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken L'ETH Zurich est l'une des plus grandes universités du monde et est réputée pour son excellence en éducation, ses recherches fondamentales de pointe et ses efforts pour mettre en pratique directement les nouvelles connaissances et innovations. Le Laboratoire des sciences de l'énergie et de l'ingénierie (D-MAVT) travaille activement au développement d'outils numériques et expérimentaux pour sonder les systèmes granulaires monophasés et multiphasés (particules). Contexte du projet Les systèmes granulaires sont omniprésents dans la nature (par exemple les avalanches rocheuses ou les dunes) et ont une importance fondamentale pour l'industrie. Cependant, malgré leur utilisation et leur présence généralisées, de nombreux phénomènes importants, tels que la ségrégation, les instabilités de surface ou le brouillage, c'est-à-dire la transition entre un état de type fluide et un état solide, sont mal compris. Ce projet explore spécifiquement l'effet de la déformabilité des particules et de la non-sphéricité sur la dynamique et la rhéologie des systèmes granulaires. Les particules flexibles se déforment sous contrainte, tandis que la déformation à son tour affecte les forces de contact et la transmission de la contrainte donnant lieu à des phénomènes rhéologiques complexes tels que le brouillage transitoire ou l'ordre d'orientation induit par le stress. Bien que déformables, les systèmes de particules asphériques devraient être riches en phénomènes physiques, ils ont été largement évités en raison des difficultés à effectuer des mesures expérimentales dans ces systèmes et dans leur description numérique. Ce poste de doctorat fait partie d'un projet conjoint qui combine l'expertise de deux groupes de recherche (Laboratory of Energy Science and Engineering, Prof. Müller et l'Institut de technologie de résonance magnétique d'imagerie biomédicale, Prof. Prüssmann) et les doctorants engagés par les deux groupes concernés sont censés collaborer quotidiennement. Description du poste L'objectif du doctorant engagé par le Laboratoire des sciences de l'énergie et du génie est de
• Outils numériques avancés pour modéliser des systèmes granulaires non sphériques et déformables
• Mettre en place des techniques expérimentales basées sur la caméra, telles que la photo-élastimétrie, pour déterminer les forces de contact et les champs de contrainte dans ces systèmes
• Développer et utiliser des modèles basés sur l'apprentissage automatique pour corréler déformation des particules et forces de contact dans les systèmes 3D Profil
• Les candidats à ce poste de doctorat devraient avoir un très bon diplôme de maîtrise en génie mécanique, physique ou disciplines connexes

We are excited to announce an opening for a Postdoctoral Fellow to work within the Volcanology and Magmatic Petrology group, led by Prof. Olivier Bachmann. • A demonstrable ability to conduct and publish high-quality research.
• Strong analytical skills, particularly with in-situ techniques (e.g., EPMA, LA-ICP-MS, SIMS).
• Experience in field work, geochronology (e.g., U-Pb, Ar-Ar) and/or numerical modelling of igneous processes.
• Excellent written and oral communication skills in English. German speaking would be an added value. Il nostro team studia diverse culture matematiche storiche e contemporanee da una moltitudine di approcci metodologici. Sfondo del progetto Stiamo cercando uno studente di dottorato di condurre ricerche sullo sviluppo, la pratica, o ruoli sociali e culturali della matematica (compresi gli aspetti matematici di altre scienze) dai punti di vista della storia, della filosofia o delle discipline umanistiche vicine. Research in this field is advanced by applying a range of methods, including field studies, laboratory studies, remote sensing, and modeling. The Atmospheric Chemistry Group at ETH currently focuses on modeling, with expertise in exploring the model-observation interface. This hire will lead a complementary sub-group in Atmospheric Chemistry that will focus on the collection of new observational constraints on atmospheric composition. In particular, we solicit applicants with expertise in: (1) biosphere-atmosphere exchange of trace gases and/or particles (2) remote sensing (ground-based and/or satellite) of short-lived atmospheric constituents. We will also consider excellent applicants working in other topics involving field measurements of atmospheric chemistry. Job description

descriptionByLocale.it:
Posizione post-dottorale: Mechanotyping di sistemi cellulari complessi 100%, Basilea, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Invitiamo le applicazioni per una posizione di ricerca postdoctoral focalizzata sulla mechanotyping di sistemi cellulari complessi, combinando strumenti nanotecnologici all'avanguardia, biologia cellulare avanzata e biologia quantitativa a livello di sistemi. Il progetto mira a scoprire come le proprietà meccaniche, le forze e i fenotipi fisici si integrano con le reti molecolari per regolare la funzione di sistemi cellulari complessi su più scale biologiche. Sfondo del progetto Le cellule sono sistemi meccanicamente eterogenei composti da proteine, membrane e compartimenti con proprietà fisiche distinte. Parallelamente, percepiscono continuamente e rispondono a diversi spunti meccanici dal loro ambiente, tra cui adesione, rigidità, tensione, taglio, pressione e confinamento. Questi segnali sono integrati in ampie scale spaziali e temporali, dai nanometri ai tessuti, per regolare il comportamento cellulare collettivo. La mechanobiologia cerca di capire come le cellule, i tessuti e i organoidi percepiscono, elaborano e rimodellano i segnali meccanici, e come questi processi governano funzioni biologiche fondamentali come l'omeostasi, la crescita, la differenziazione, la migrazione, lo sviluppo e l'apoptosi. Nonostante i grandi progressi, una comprensione multiscala di come le informazioni meccaniche vengono generate e integrate in sistemi multicellulari complessi rimane limitata. Il progresso nel campo richiede lo sviluppo di modelli multicellulari ingegnerizzati come sistemi di riferimento meccanico, nuovi strumenti per misurare quantitativamente e manipolare meccanica su scale, e quadri teorici per interpretare la complessità meccanobiologica. Questo progetto postdoctoral affronta queste sfide combinando sistemi di modello, probing meccanico avanzato e analisi integrativa per chiarire come le proprietà meccaniche regolano la funzione biologica a livello molecolare, cellulare e multicellulare, in ultima analisi supportando i progressi in mechanodiagnostics e mechanomedicine. Descrizione del lavoro Potrai lavorare all'interfaccia di mechanobiologia, nanotecnologia, biologia dei sistemi e biologia quantitativa, sviluppando e applicando approcci sperimentali e analitici innovativi per caratterizzare gli stati meccanici cellulari e i loro ruoli normativi. Le direzioni di ricerca includono:
• Mechanotipazione quantitativa di singole cellule, tessuti e sistemi multicellulari (ad esempio, organoidi, sferoidi)
• Sviluppo e applicazione di piattaforme nanotecnologiche per il rilevamento della forza, la manipolazione e la fenotipazione meccanica
• Tecniche biologiche avanzate delle cellule, tra cui immagini live-cell, microscopia super-risoluzione e reporter codificati geneticamente
• Sistemi di biologia approcci per integrare fenotipi meccanici con reti molecolari, di segnalazione e trascrizionali
• Modellazione quantitativa e analisi data-driven degli stati cellulari multiparametri
• Approcci ad alto rendimento e multiscala per collegare le proprietà meccaniche ai risultati cellulari funzionali La posizione offre una sostanziale libertà di modellare nuove condotte sperimentali che colmano misurazioni fisiche con un'intuizione biologica a livello di sistemi. Lavorazione indipendente su un progetto interdisciplinare impegnativo e complesso a più alti livelli scientifici presso il Dipartimento di Scienze e Ingegneria dei Biosistemi, ETH Zürich di Basilea in collaborazione con gruppi leader a livello internazionale in biologia cellulare, organoide e computazionale. Profilo
• Grado di dottorato o equivalente nei settori della biologia cellulare, della mechanobiologia, della bionanotecnologia, della biologia dei sistemi, della biologia quantitativa (phenotyping), dell'analisi dei biosistemi computazionali e di altre discipline correlate
• Esperienza in biologia delle cellule umane e animali, sistemi cellulari e organoidi
• Competenza in micro-/nanofabricazione, microscopia ottica avanzata e nanooscopia, analisi delle immagini, analisi computazionale
• Interesse ad essere addestrato in biofisica molecolare e cellulare, bionanotecnologia, biologia cellulare e dei tessuti, m ottica ad alta estremità
descriptionByLocale.en:
Postdoctoral Position: Mechanotyping of Complex Cellular Systems 100%, Basel, fixed-term print Drucken We invite applications for a postdoctoral research position focused on the mechanotyping of complex cellular systems, combining cutting-edge nanotechnological tools, advanced cell biology, and systems-level quantitative biology. The project aims to uncover how mechanical properties, forces, and physical phenotypes integrate with molecular networks to regulate the function of complex cellular systems across multiple biological scales. Project background Cells are mechanically heterogeneous systems composed of proteins, membranes, and compartments with distinct physical properties. In parallel, they continuously sense and respond to diverse mechanical cues from their environment, including adhesion, stiffness, tension, shear, pressure, and confinement. These cues are integrated across wide spatial and temporal scales, from nanometers to tissues, to regulate collective cellular behavior. Mechanobiology seeks to understand how cells, tissues, and organoids perceive, process, and remodel mechanical signals, and how these processes govern fundamental biological functions such as homeostasis, growth, differentiation, migration, development, and apoptosis. Despite major advances, a multiscale understanding of how mechanical information is generated and integrated in complex multicellular systems remains limited. Progress in the field requires the development of engineered multicellular models as mechanical reference systems, new tools to quantitatively measure and manipulate mechanics across scales, and theoretical frameworks to interpret mechanobiological complexity. This postdoctoral project addresses these challenges by combining model systems, advanced mechanical probing, and integrative analysis to elucidate how mechanical properties regulate biological function across molecular, cellular, and multicellular levels, ultimately supporting advances in mechanodiagnostics and mechanomedicine. Job description You will work at the interface of mechanobiology, nanotechnology, systems biology, and quantitative biology , developing and applying innovative experimental and analytical approaches to characterize cellular mechanical states and their regulatory roles. Research directions include:
• Quantitative mechanotyping of single cells, tissues, and multicellular systems (e.g., organoids, spheroids)
• Development and application of nanotechnological platforms for force sensing, manipulation, and mechanical phenotyping
• Advanced cell biological techniques, including live-cell imaging, super-resolution microscopy, and genetically encoded reporters
• Systems biology approaches to integrate mechanical phenotypes with molecular, signaling, and transcriptional networks
• Quantitative modeling and data-driven analysis of multi-parameter cellular states
• High-throughput and multi-scale approaches to link mechanical properties to functional cellular outcomes The position offers substantial freedom to shape novel experimental pipelines that bridge physical measurements with systems-level biological insight . Independent working on an interdisciplinary challenging and complex project at highest scientific levels at the Department of Biosystems Science and Engineering, ETH Zürich in Basel in collaboration with internationally leading groups in cell, organoid and computational biology. Profile
• PhD degree or equivalent in the fields of cell biology, mechanobiology, bionanotechnology, systems biology, quantitative biology (phenotyping), computational biosystems analysis, and other related disciplines
• Experience in human and animal cell biology, cellular systems, and organoids
• Expertise in micro-/nanofabrication, advanced optical microscopy and nanooscopy, image analysis, computational analysis
• Interest in getting trained in molecular and cellular biophysics, bionanotechnology, cell and tissue biology, high end optical m

Postdoctoral Position: Mechanotyping komplexer zellulärer Systeme 100%, Basel, befristet Drucken Drucken Wir laden Anwendungen für eine postdoctorale Forschungsposition ein, die sich auf die Mechanotypisierung komplexer zellulärer Systeme konzentriert, die innovative nanotechnologische Werkzeuge, fortschrittliche Zellbiologie und quantitative Biologie auf Systemebene kombinieren. Das Projekt zielt darauf ab, herauszufinden, wie sich mechanische Eigenschaften, Kräfte und physikalische Phänotypen in molekulare Netzwerke integrieren, um die Funktion komplexer zellulärer Systeme über mehrere biologische Skalen zu regulieren. Projekt Hintergrund Zellen sind mechanisch heterogene Systeme aus Proteinen, Membranen und Kompartimenten mit unterschiedlichen physikalischen Eigenschaften. Parallel dazu erfassen und reagieren sie kontinuierlich auf vielfältige mechanische Queues aus ihrer Umgebung, einschließlich Haftung, Steifigkeit, Spannung, Scherung, Druck und Eingrenzung. Diese Queues sind über weite räumliche und zeitliche Skalen integriert, von Nanometern bis zu Geweben, um kollektives zelluläres Verhalten zu regulieren. Die Mechanobiologie versucht zu verstehen, wie Zellen, Gewebe und Organoide mechanische Signale wahrnehmen, verarbeiten und umgestalten und wie diese Prozesse grundlegende biologische Funktionen wie Homöostase, Wachstum, Differenzierung, Migration, Entwicklung und Apoptose regeln. Trotz der großen Fortschritte bleibt ein mehrstufiges Verständnis dafür, wie mechanische Informationen erzeugt und in komplexe multizelluläre Systeme integriert werden. Fortschritte in diesem Bereich erfordern die Entwicklung von multizellulären Modellen als mechanische Referenzsysteme, neue Werkzeuge zur quantitativen Messung und Manipulation von Mechaniken über Skalen und theoretische Rahmen zur Interpretation mechanobiologischer Komplexität. Dieses postdoctorale Projekt befasst sich mit diesen Herausforderungen durch die Kombination von Modellsystemen, fortschrittlicher mechanischer Probierung und integrativer Analyse, um zu klären, wie mechanische Eigenschaften die biologische Funktion über molekulare, zelluläre und multizelluläre Ebenen regeln und letztlich Fortschritte in der Mechanodiagnostik und Mechanomedicin unterstützen. Jobbeschreibung Sie arbeiten an der Schnittstelle von Mechanobiologie, Nanotechnologie, Systembiologie und quantitativer Biologie, entwickeln und anwenden innovative experimentelle und analytische Ansätze, um zelluläre mechanische Zustände und ihre regulatorischen Rollen zu charakterisieren. Zu den Forschungsrichtungen gehören:
• Quantitative Mechanotypisierung von Einzelzellen, Geweben und multizellulären Systemen (z.B. Organoiden, Sphäroiden)
• Entwicklung und Anwendung nanotechnologischer Plattformen zur Krafterfassung, Manipulation und mechanischen Phänotypisierung
• Fortgeschrittene zellbiologische Techniken, einschließlich Live-Zell-Bildgebung, hochauflösende Mikroskopie und genetisch kodierte Reporter
• Systembiologie Ansätze zur Integration mechanischer Phänotypen mit molekularen, Signalisierungs- und Transkriptionsnetzwerken
• Quantitative Modellierung und datengesteuerte Analyse von multiparameterzellulären Zuständen
• Hochdurchsatz- und Multi-Skala-Ansätze zur Verknüpfung mechanischer Eigenschaften mit funktionellen zellulären Ergebnissen Die Position bietet erhebliche Freiheit, neue experimentelle Pipelines zu formen, die physikalische Messungen mit system-level biologischen Erkenntnissen überbrücken. Unabhängige Arbeiten an einem interdisziplinären herausfordernden und komplexen Projekt auf höchstem wissenschaftlichen Niveau am Department of Biosystems Science and Engineering, ETH Zürich in Basel in Zusammenarbeit mit international führenden Gruppen in Zell-, Organoid- und Rechenbiologie. Profil
• PhD-Abschluss oder Äquivalent in den Bereichen Zellbiologie, Mechanobiologie, Biotechnologie, Systembiologie, quantitative Biologie (Phenotyping), rechnerische Biosysteme-Analyse und andere damit verbundene Disziplinen
• Erfahrung in der Human- und Tierzellbiologie, Zellsystemen und Organoiden
• Expertise in der Mikro-/Nanofabrikation, fortschrittliche optische Mikroskopie und Nanomikroskopie, Bildanalyse, Rechenanalyse
• Interesse an der Ausbildung in molekularer und zellulärer Biophysik, Biotechnologie, Zell- und Gewebebiologie, High-End-Optik m
descriptionByLocale.fr:
Position postdoctorale : Mécanotypage de systèmes cellulaires complexes 100%, Bâle, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Nous invitons à présenter des demandes pour un poste de recherche postdoctorale axé sur le mécanotypage de systèmes cellulaires complexes, combinant des outils nanotechnologiques de pointe, la biologie cellulaire avancée et la biologie quantitative de systèmes. Le projet vise à découvrir comment les propriétés mécaniques, les forces et les phénotypes physiques s'intègrent aux réseaux moléculaires pour réguler la fonction de systèmes cellulaires complexes à plusieurs échelles biologiques. Contexte du projet Les cellules sont des systèmes mécaniquement hétérogènes composés de protéines, de membranes et de compartiments ayant des propriétés physiques distinctes. En parallèle, ils sentent et réagissent continuellement à divers indices mécaniques de leur environnement, y compris l'adhérence, la rigidité, la tension, le cisaillement, la pression et le confinement. Ces repères sont intégrés à de larges échelles spatiales et temporelles, des nanomètres aux tissus, pour réguler le comportement cellulaire collectif. La méchanobiologie cherche à comprendre comment les cellules, les tissus et les organoïdes perçoivent, traitent et remodelent les signaux mécaniques, et comment ces processus régissent les fonctions biologiques fondamentales telles que l'homéostasie, la croissance, la différenciation, la migration, le développement et l'apoptose. Malgré des progrès importants, une compréhension à plusieurs échelles de la façon dont l'information mécanique est générée et intégrée dans des systèmes multicellulaires complexes demeure limitée. Le progrès sur le terrain exige le développement de modèles multicellulaires conçus comme systèmes de référence mécanique, de nouveaux outils pour mesurer quantitativement et manipuler la mécanique à travers les échelles, et de cadres théoriques pour interpréter la complexité méchanobiologique. Ce projet postdoctoral répond à ces défis en combinant des systèmes modèles, une analyse mécanique avancée et une analyse intégrative afin d'élucider la façon dont les propriétés mécaniques régulent la fonction biologique à tous les niveaux moléculaire, cellulaire et multicellulaire, soutenant finalement les progrès en mécanodiagnostique et en mécanomédecine. Description du poste Vous travaillerez à l'interface de la mécanisation, de la nanotechnologie, de la biologie des systèmes et de la biologie quantitative, en développant et en appliquant des approches expérimentales et analytiques novatrices pour caractériser les états mécaniques cellulaires et leurs rôles réglementaires. Les orientations de recherche comprennent :
• Mécanotypage quantitatif de cellules, tissus et systèmes multicellulaires uniques (par exemple, organoides, sphéroïdes)
• Développement et application de plates-formes nanotechnologiques pour la détection de force, la manipulation et le phénotypage mécanique
• Techniques biologiques cellulaires avancées, y compris l'imagerie des cellules vivantes, la microscopie à super résolution et les reporters génétiquement codés
• Approches de biologie des systèmes pour intégrer les phénotypes mécaniques aux réseaux moléculaires, de signalisation et de transcription
• Modélisation quantitative et analyse basée sur les données des états cellulaires multiparamètres
• Approches à haut débit et à plusieurs échelles pour lier les propriétés mécaniques aux résultats cellulaires fonctionnels La position offre une grande liberté de façonner de nouveaux pipelines expérimentaux qui relient les mesures physiques avec des aperçus biologiques au niveau des systèmes. Indépendant travaillant sur un projet interdisciplinaire difficile et complexe aux plus hauts niveaux scientifiques du Département des sciences et de l'ingénierie des biosystèmes, ETH Zürich à Bâle, en collaboration avec des groupes de premier plan internationaux en biologie cellulaire, organolytique et computationnelle. Profil
• Doctorat ou équivalent dans les domaines de la biologie cellulaire, de la méchanobiologie, de la biotechnologie, de la biologie des systèmes, de la biologie quantitative (phénotypage), de l'analyse des biosystèmes informatiques et d'autres disciplines connexes
• Expérience en biologie des cellules humaines et animales, systèmes cellulaires et organoides
• Expertise en micro/nanofabrication, microscopie optique avancée et nanooscopie, analyse d'images, analyse informatique
• Intérêt pour une formation en biophysique moléculaire et cellulaire, en bionanotechnologie, en biologie cellulaire et tissulaire, en optique de pointe

Il laboratorio studia la regolazione genica dei mammiferi e le vie di elaborazione del RNA. I progetti si basano su una combinazione di saggi strutturali, biochimici e cellulari, tra cui crio-elettrone e microscopia leggera, editing genico, sequenziamento di prossima generazione, proteomica e ricostituzione di grandi complessi proteici-RNA da proteine ricombinanti. Utilizzando questi strumenti il laboratorio mira a determinare la base molecolare del meccanismo delle malattie al fine di trovare nuovi obiettivi per il trattamento. Descrizione del lavoro Il gruppo di ricerca è alla ricerca di un collaboratore aperto e flessibile. Il vostro lavoro nell'organizzazione di laboratorio aiuterà a mantenere il laboratorio senza intoppi, mentre la vostra collaborazione impegnata sosterrà l'avanzamento dei nostri diversi progetti di ricerca. I compiti principali includono lavorare a stretto contatto con altri membri del laboratorio per assistere i loro progetti, regolando in modo flessibile la domanda. Nello specifico, si sta effettuando esperimenti da clonazione di costrutti ad espressione proteica e purificazione da cellule batteriche e insetti. Potrai coltivare le linee cellulari della cultura dei tessuti mammiferi, trasformarli per esperimenti, generare linee cellulari stabili e analizzare i modelli di espressione come ad esempio immunofluorescenza, blotting occidentale o RT-qPCR. Potrai documentare diligentemente il tuo lavoro di laboratorio compreso il mantenimento e l'aggiornamento di database interni. Inoltre, sarete responsabili di organizzare e coordinare in modo indipendente le riparazioni e la manutenzione di attrezzature di laboratorio. Laboratory Technician (Technical Assistant) in RNA Biology and Disease Mechanisms 80%-100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The RNA Biology and Disease laboratory at the Institute of Molecular Biology and Biophysics (Department of Biology), ETH Zurich, invites applications for a laboratory technician to support its daily research activities and laboratory operations. The lab studies mammalian gene regulation and RNA processing pathways. Projects rely on a combination of structural, biochemical and cellular assays, including cryo-electron and light microscopy, gene editing, next-generation sequencing, proteomics and reconstitution of large protein-RNA complexes from recombinant proteins. Using these tools the laboratory aims to determine the molecular basis of disease mechanism in order to find novel targets for treatment. Specifically, you will be carrying out experiments from cloning of constructs to protein expression and purification from bacterial and insect cells. You will culture mammalian tissue culture cell lines, transform them for experiments, generate stable cell lines, and analyse expression patterns e.g.by immunofluorescence, western blotting or RT-qPCR. descriptionByLocale.it:
Ricercatore post-dottorato: Stimolazione idraulica e comportamento proppant in roccia cristallina 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo La Cattedra di Ingegneria Geologia e il BedrettoLab all'ETH di Zurigo invita le applicazioni per una posizione Postdoctoral Researcher all'interno del progetto europeo di ricerca UPLIFT, concentrandosi sulle tecnologie di stimolazione idraulica eco-compatibile nelle formazioni cristalline della roccia. La posizione si basa sull'ETH di Zurigo e coinvolge ricerche sperimentali presso il Laboratorio sotterraneo di Bedretto. La stimolazione idraulica è una tecnologia chiave per migliorare la permeabilità nei serbatoi geotermici. Mentre la stimolazione multistadio con proppants e additivi chimici è ampiamente applicata nell'industria del petrolio e del gas, la sua accettazione in Europa rimane limitata a causa delle preoccupazioni ambientali. Gli approcci di stimolazione dell'acqua sono più comunemente accettati, ma la loro efficacia rispetto ai metodi a base di proppant in particolare nella roccia cristallina rimane insufficientemente compresa. Il Bedretto Underground Laboratory offre un ambiente unico e altamente strumentale per indagare i processi siero-idro-termo-meccanici accoppiati durante la stimolazione idraulica. All'interno del progetto UPLIFT, saranno condotti esperimenti di laboratorio e di campo controllati per valutare solo le tecniche di stimolazione a base di proppanto e chimicamente assistita. L'obiettivo è quello di sviluppare strategie di stimolazione sicure, efficienti e ecologiche per applicazioni geotermiche in tutta Europa. Descrizione del lavoro

The position is based at ETH Zurich and involves experimental research at the Bedretto Underground Laboratory. Hydraulic stimulation is a key technology for enhancing permeability in geothermal reservoirs. While multi-stage stimulation using proppants and chemical additives is widely applied in the oil and gas industry, its acceptance in Europe remains limited due to environmental concerns. Water-only stimulation approaches are more commonly accepted, yet their effectiveness compared to proppant-based methods particularly in crystalline rock remains insufficiently understood. The Bedretto Underground Laboratory provides a unique, highly instrumented environment to investigate coupled seismo-hydro-thermo-mechanical processes during hydraulic stimulation. Within the UPLIFT project, controlled laboratory and field-scale experiments will be conducted to evaluate water-only, proppant-based, and chemically assisted stimulation techniques. PhD Position: Optimization of shut-in strategies to reduce induced seismicity 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Chair of Engineering Geology and the BedrettoLab at ETH Zurich invite applications for a PhD position within a research project on poroelastic effects and induced seismicity in geothermal systems. The position focuses on post-shut-in seismicity and the design of safer operational protocols. Induced seismicity in geothermal systems often continues after injection or production is stopped, a phenomenon known as post-shut-in or trailing seismicity. In many cases, the largest seismic events occur after shut-in, posing challenges for hazard mitigation and operational safety. Despite extensive modelling efforts, the governing mechanisms are still not fully understood, and field observations of pressure and deformation during shut-in, that may improve our process understanding, are rare. This project exploits the unique monitoring capabilities of the Bedretto Underground Laboratory to investigate these processes and to develop experimentally validated guidelines for safer shut-in strategies. Job description
• Investigate pressure, deformation, and seismicity data from hydraulic stimulation experiments to derive conceptual models of post-shut-in processes
• Develop hydromechanical models to reproduce observed shut-in behaviour and test competing hypotheses (e.g., pressure diffusion vs. poroelastic effects)
• Develop/apply earthquake source physics models to understand induced seismicity processe
• Design and execute controlled hydraulic stimulation and production experiments with different shut-in protocols
• Quantify how different shut-in strategies influence seismicity rates and magnitudes
• Derive recommendations for optimized shut-in procedures to minimize induced seismic hazard
• Publish results, present at conferences, and contribute to project reporting Profile

• Interest in induced seismicity, geomechanics, and field experiments

descriptionByLocale.en:
Postdoc position: Production-induced seismicity in fractured reservoirs 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Swiss Seismological Service (SED) and the BedrettoLab at ETH Zurich invite applications for a Postdoctoral Researcher position within a two-year research project on poroelastic effects and induced seismicity in geothermal systems. The position focuses on production-induced seismicity in fractured reservoirs and combines field experiments, data analysis, and numerical modelling. Project background Geothermal energy projects can induce seismicity during both fluid injection and fluid production through by complex hydromechanical processes in fractured rock. Development of simple and standardized modelling approaches to assess production-induced seismicity would benefit from insitu observations to identify relevant or missing hydromechanical processes and to calibrate models with. The project leverages the unique infrastructure of the Bedretto Underground Laboratory, where dense multiparametric monitoring networks provide unprecedented observations of pressure, deformation, and seismicity. The project aims at validating modelling approaches and practical workflows for assessing seismic hazard related to fluid production in Swiss geothermal projects (e.g. in Vaud and Geneva). Job description
• Analyse high-resolution pressure, deformation, and seismic datasets from past and new production experiments to identify governing hydromechanical processes
• Develop and apply coupled hydromechanical models (continuum and discontinuum) to reproduce observed behaviour and quantify poroelastic effects in fractured reservoirs
• Develop and apply earthquake source physics models to understand processes underlying induced seismicity
• Plan and conduct controlled production experiments at the BedrettoLab to test hypotheses and validate models
• Translate modelling results into simplified and scalable workflows for assessing production-induced seismicity in geothermal projects
• Apply developed methods to realistic geothermal scenarios (e.g., Swiss hydrothermal systems) and contribute to best-practice guidelines
• Publish results in peer-reviewed journals, present at conferences, and collaborate with academic, governmental, and industry stakeholders Profile
• PhD in Geophysics, Geomechanics, Earth Sciences, Physics, Engineering, or a related field
• Strong background in hydromechanics, reservoir modelling, induced seismicity, earthquake source physics
• Experience with numerical modelling tools (e.g., MOOSE, PorePy, or similar)
• Programming skills (Python, MATLAB, or similar)
• Experience with field data and/or underground experiments is an advantage
• Ability to work independently and lead research activities
• Strong analytical and communication skills in English (German or French is a plus) Workplace Workplace We offer
• A fully funded postdoctoral position (initially 2 years, with possible extension)
• Employment according to ETH Zurich regulations
• Access to the Bedretto Underground Laboratory, a world-leading research infrastructure
• A highly interdisciplinary environment bridging geophysics, geomechanics, energy research and earthquake physics
• Opportunities to lead publications and develop an independent research profile
• Close collaboration with ETH Zurich, the Swiss Seismological Service, and external stakeholders such as Swiss Federal Office of Energy, Canton de Genève, Canton de Vaud Supervision and Environment The position is jointly hosted by the Swiss Seismological Service (SED) at ETH Zurich in close collaboration with the BedrettoLab and the Chair of Engineering Geology. The postdoctoral researcher will work closely with experts in hydromechanics, induced seismicity, geothermal energy and earthquake source physics, and will interact with ongoing national and international projects. chevron_right Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainabi

descriptionByLocale.en:
Machine Learning Scientist (AI-based Weather Forecasting) 100%, Locarno, fixed-term print Drucken Recent advances in AI-based weather prediction have demonstrated remarkable skill and computational efficiency. However, most current machine-learning weather prediction (MLWP) systems rely primarily on NWP analyses for initialization and only partially exploit the wealth of available satellite observations. With the advent of the Meteosat Third Generation (MTG), new high-frequency and high-resolution measurements of clouds, moisture, temperature, and lightning activity provide unprecedented opportunities for substantially improving regional forecasts. Project background Within the framework of a Research Fellowship supported by EUMETSAT, we are advancing the integration of geostationary satellite observations into a next-generation regional MLWP system. The project builds on an existing graph-based, stretched-grid regional forecasting model developed at MeteoSwiss and is embedded in the Anemoi framework initiated by ECMWF. The objective is to develop and evaluate novel multi-encoder-decoder architectures capable of ingesting various satellite data streams (e.g. radiances, cloud products, lightning observations, hyperspectral soundings) and integrating them into high-frequency forecasting cycles with lead times from short-range to up to 10 days ahead. The work will be carried out in close collaboration with national and international partners and contributes directly to the future operational exploitation of MTG data. Job description We are looking for a Scientific Programmer / Software Developer to join our motivated and interdisciplinary team. In this role, you will:
• Develop and implement machine-learning model architectures enabling the direct ingestion of next generation satellite data (e.g. MTG FCI, LI, IRS) into state-of-the-art regional forecasting models in Anemoi
• Contribute to the evolution of a multi-encoder-decoder MLWP framework within the Anemoi ecosystem
• Train, fine-tune, and evaluate models using large-scale meteorological and satellite datasets
• Quantify the impact of satellite data on forecast skill across variables and lead times
• Collaborate closely with scientists, ML researchers, and operational forecasting teams to ensure that forecast outputs meet the needs of diverse users
• Disseminate results through scientific publications, conference presentations, and exchanges with EUMETSAT and partner institutions We value people who enjoy solving complex problems, collaborating across disciplines, and contributing across different stages of the workflow as the system matures. This is a fixed-term contract of 1 year, with the possibility of extension for up to an additional 2 years. The main workplace is located at MeteoSwiss Locarno-Monti with regular visits to Zürich. The amount of remuneration will be in accordance with the salary system of ETH Zürich. Profile We welcome applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds who meet most (not necessarily all) of the following criteria:
• PhD in computer science, data science, natural sciences (e.g. physics, meteorology) or a related field. Candidates with an MSc and proven professional experience may also be considered
• Experience working with satellite data (e.g. geostationary observations, radiances, retrieval products)
• Strong programming skills in Python
• Experience in machine learning, ideally including deep learning architectures such as graph neural networks, transformers, or spatio-temporal models
• Experience with high-performance or distributed computing environments
• Good understanding of meteorological processes and numerical weather prediction
• Interest in DevOps practices and sustainable software engineering
• Ability to work independently on research questions while contributing to a collaborative team environment
• Motivation to work in a diverse, interdisciplinary, and international environment •

Student Research Assistant – Development and assembly of instruments for atmospheric research 10%-30%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Atmospheric Physics group at ETH Zurich is looking for a Student Research Assistant to support the development and assembly of instruments used during field campaigns . Our research group studies the crucial role of clouds and aerosols in the climate system, aiming to better understand how cloud microphysical processes drive both precipitation formation and the radiative impact of clouds. Project background This role directly supports our research efforts by building the instruments we deploy in the field. The primary instrument is a custom holographic imager developed within our group. It uses in-line open-path holography to capture 2D images of cloud particles in a well-defined volume. With this we can reconstruct the position, shape, and size of cloud droplets as small as 5.5 µm and ice crystals up to several millimeters. Our latest development is a lightweight version named HOLIMOAir. With two units already completed, the plan is to build an additional 2–3 units by the end of the year. This includes making adaptations to ensure they are suitable for wind tunnel measurements and deployment in the Antarctic. Job description
• Building further HOLIMOAir units and develop upgrades for other instrumentation
• Mechanical assembly of instrument housing and optical components
• Soldering of cable assemblies and PCBs, testing of electronics
• Upgrading of sofware running on instrumentation
• Support instrument integration, calibration, and field campaign preparation
• Assist with maintenance and basic documentation Profile
• Enrolled student at ETH Zurich or another Swiss university
• Background or strong interest in mechatronics, optics, electronics with hands-on experience
• Manual dexterity and careful working style, workshop and/or electronics experience is a plus
• Basic python programming skills, linux command line experience a plus
• Interest in experimental or field-based research Workplace Workplace We offer
• Direct involvement in cutting-edge atmospheric research
• Flexible working hours (10–15 h/week during semester, possibility for more during breaks)

L'obiettivo primario è quello di favorire l'interazione tra circa 150 membri ZNZ, gruppi di ricerca basati su ETHZ, UZH e i quattro ospedali universitari, nella ricerca e nella formazione di neuroscienze. Ciò include lo sviluppo di infrastrutture innovative, il finanziamento per progetti collaborativi, la promozione della traduzione dei risultati della ricerca nella pratica clinica, la costruzione e il mantenimento dei rapporti con altri centri di ricerca in Svizzera e a livello internazionale, e la valorizzazione della consapevolezza pubblica dei risultati dei membri ZNZ. Il Direttore Generale lavora a stretto contatto con il comitato direttivo ZNZ, responsabile della strategia generale del centro. Sfondo del progetto Il paesaggio della ricerca di neuroscienze all'interno della rete ZNZ è vario. I ricercatori provenienti da sfondi tra cui biologia, medicina, psicologia, biochimica, fisica, ingegneria, informatica e economia indagano domande fondamentali su come il cervello funziona in salute e malattia. Questo spinge lo sviluppo di nuove tecnologie diagnostiche, terapie e “intelligenti”. Negli ultimi anni, i membri ZNZ hanno contribuito in modo significativo ai progressi nelle terapie per la demenza, la sclerosi multipla e le lesioni del midollo spinale, così come per le tecnologie di neuroriabilitazione, l'imaging cerebrale all'avanguardia, le applicazioni ad ultrasuoni focalizzate, la ricerca sul sonno, le neuroeconomia e le reti neurali artificiali. Descrizione del lavoro Il Direttore Generale opera in gran parte in modo indipendente e si assume una significativa responsabilità per il successo complessivo del Centro. Poiché il ruolo comporta un'interazione continua con un'ampia gamma di stakeholder, porta un alto livello di visibilità. La soluzione dei problemi attraverso più consiglieri può essere complessa e richiede un forte coordinamento e giudizio.

ZNZ Managing Director 80%-100%, Zurich, permanent print Drucken The Managing Director is responsible for implementing the objectives of the Neuroscience Center Zurich (ZNZ), a highly interdisciplinary research network jointly supported by ETH Zurich (ETHZ) and the University of Zurich (UZH). The primary goal is to foster interaction among approximately 150 ZNZ members—research groups based at ETHZ, UZH, and the four university hospitals—in neuroscience research and training. This includes developing innovative infrastructure, securing funding for collaborative projects, promoting the translation of research findings into clinical practice, building and maintaining relationships with other research centers in Switzerland and internationally, and enhancing public awareness of the achievements of ZNZ members. The Managing Director works closely with the ZNZ Steering Committee, which is responsible for the center’s overall strategy. Project background The landscape of neuroscience research within the ZNZ network is diverse. Researchers from backgrounds including biology, medicine, psychology, biochemistry, physics, engineering, computer science, and economics investigate fundamental questions about how the brain functions in health and disease. This drives the development of new diagnostics, therapies, and “intelligent” technologies. In recent years, ZNZ members have contributed significantly to advances in therapies for dementia, multiple sclerosis, and spinal cord injury, as well as to neurorehabilitation technologies, state-of-the-art brain imaging, focused ultrasound applications, sleep research, neuroeconomics, and artificial neural networks. Job description The Managing Director operates largely independently and bears significant responsibility for the overall success of the Center. As the role involves continuous interaction with a wide range of stakeholders it carries a high level of visibility. Problem-solving across multiple advisory boards can be complex and requires strong coordination and judgment. The Managing Director leads a small team and is responsible for:
• Promoting scientific collaboration among ZNZ research groups
• Providing organizational and financial support for selected ZNZ projects
• Maintaining and strengthening relationships with external research partners
• Managing ZNZ PhD grants and coordinating travel support for students
• Directing the International PhD Program in Neuroscience at UZH and ETH Zurich
• Overseeing the Specialized Master’s Program in Interdisciplinary Brain Sciences at UZH and ETH Zurich
• Leading communication with stakeholders, including newsletters, social media, and public events
• Participating in steering committees of related units at UZH
• Organizing regular events for ZNZ members, such as annual symposia and strategy meetings Profile

• Several years of postdoctoral or relevant professional experience
• Experience or knowledge in neuroscience or a related discipline

Student Research Assistant – Unity Frontend Development for Digital Einstein 10%-30%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Digital Character AI team at ETH Zurich's Computer Graphics Laboratory is looking for a Student Research Assistant to support the frontend development of our interactive AI avatar platforms. Our work focuses on lifelike digital humans powered by large language models, affective computing, and real-time rendering — deployed at high-profile events such as the World Economic Forum, Berlin Science Week, and GITEX. You can learn more about the Digital Einstein project here . Project background Digital Einstein is an award-winning AI avatar platform that brings Albert Einstein to life as an interactive conversational agent. Built on a Unity-based frontend integrated with speech recognition and real-time facial and body animations, it has been showcased at major international events. The backend is implemented in Python and orchestrates large language models for dialogue management and response generation. We are currently extending the platform to a new Digital Curie installation. As our team scales up, we are looking for a student assistant to primarily help maintain and further develop the Unity frontend for both avatars — with the option to also contribute to the Python/LLM backend. chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht PhD Posizione: Agro-Economic Analysis of Legume-Cereal Mixtures (Progetto PhenoMix) 100%, Zurigo, stampa a tempo fisso Drucken Questa posizione studentesca di dottorato fa parte del progetto “ PhenoMix: fenotipazione multidimensionale del campo delle miscele di colture ”, sostenuto dalla Fondazione Nazionale di Scienza Svizzera. La posizione è ospitata dal gruppo Crop Science; un gruppo di lavoro vibrante e interdisciplinare nell'Istituto di Scienze Agrarie presso il Dipartimento di Scienze Ambientali dell'ETH di Zurigo. La ricerca fenotipante del nostro gruppo si concentra sullo sviluppo di metodi e modelli per determinare i tratti di rilevanza per l'allevamento di colture e test di varietà. Il gruppo di ricerca Agroscope Extension Arable Crops (Competence Division Plants and Plant Products) sviluppa soluzioni ecologiche per il controllo delle malattie, dei parassiti e delle infestanti e valuta le varietà vegetali per la loro idoneità in condizioni svizzere. Ci vuole un approccio olistico per creare sistemi agricoli sostenibili, convenienti e affidabili dal clima. Il progetto PhenoMix è un progetto congiunto di quattro gruppi di ricerca all'ETH di Zurigo, al Centro svizzero per la scienza dei dati e all'agroscopio. L'obiettivo generale di PhenoMix è quello di testare l'ipotesi che l'attuale tecnologia di fenotipazione del campo ad alto rendimento in combinazione con le valutazioni dei servizi fisiologici dell'impianto e dell'ecosistema può fornire una svolta per determinare genotipi che possono essere combinati con successo in miscele legume-cere agroecologicamente vantaggiose. Diverse varietà di legumi (peci, lenticchie) e cereali (wheat, avena, orzo) saranno coltivate in stand puri e in miscele sul campo fenotyping piattaforma FIP del gruppo Crop Science, in un campo sperimentale confinante e nei campi del contadino. I pacchetti di lavoro PhenoMix affrontano fenotyping, ecofisiologia vegetale, scienza dei dati e prestazioni agronomic-economiche con quattro studenti di dottorato, due postdoc e diversi tecnici assegnati a tali pacchetti di lavoro. Lo studente medico agro-economico istituirà e monitorerà esperimenti sul campo in loco e on-farm indagando su diverse miscele lentili-cereali valutando vari servizi ecosistemici. Descrizione del lavoro Questo progetto di dottorato formerà una pietra angolare importante nel mosaico dell'intero progetto con compiti specifici e in allineamento con gli altri studenti di dottorato PhenoMix e postdocs per i quali il reclutamento sta anche accadendo attualmente. Complessivamente i compiti del progetto includono:
• Pianificazione, conduzione e valutazione del campo e esperimenti di laboratorio post-raccolta
• Esecuzione di analisi statistiche, compresi gli approcci basati su AI
• Presentazione dei risultati a eventi nazionali e internazionali e pubblicazione in riviste peer-reviewed e in pratica-oriented
• Organizzazione di laboratori nazionali per coltivatori, industria alimentare e consumatori
• Assistenza nella creazione di lotti, manutenzione, monitoraggio e raccolta in tutti i pacchetti di lavoro di PhenoMi x. Questa posizione a tempo pieno è finanziata per quattro anni. PhD Position: Agro-Economic Analysis of Legume-Cereal Mixtures (PhenoMix project) 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken This doctoral student position is part of the project “ PhenoMix: Multidimensional field phenotyping of crop mixtures ”, supported by the Swiss National Science Foundation. The position is hosted by the Crop Science group; a vibrant and interdisciplinary working group in the Institute of Agricultural Sciences at the Department of Environmental Systems Science at ETH Zurich. Our group’s phenotyping research focuses on the development of methods and models to determine traits of relevance for crop breeding and variety testing. The Agroscope research group Extension Arable Crops (Competence division Plants and Plant Products) develops ecological solutions for disease, pest and weed control and evaluates crop varieties for their suitability under Swiss conditions. It takes a holistic approach to create sustainable, cost-efficient, and climate-resilient arable farming systems. Project background PhenoMix is a joint project of four research groups at ETH Zurich, the Swiss Data Science Center and Agroscope. The overall objective of PhenoMix is to test the hypothesis that current high throughput field phenotyping technology in combination with plant physiological and ecosystem service assessments can provide a breakthrough to determine genotypes that can be successfully combined in agroecologically beneficial legume-cereal mixtures. Different varieties of legumes (peas, lentils) and cereals (wheat, oats, barley) will be grown in pure stands and in mixtures on the field phenotyping platform FIP of the Crop Science group, on a neighbouring experimental field and on farmer’s fields. The PhenoMix Work Packages address phenotyping, plant ecophysiology, data science, and agronomic-economic performance with four doctoral students, two postdocs and several technicians assigned to those work packages. The Agro-Economic doctoral student will establish and monitor on-site and on-farm field experiments investigating several lentil-cereal mixtures by assessing various ecosystem services. Job description This doctoral project will form an important cornerstone in the mosaic of the entire project with specific tasks and in alignment with the other PhenoMix doctoral students and postdocs for which recruiting is also going on currently. Overall tasks of the project include:
• Planning, conducting and evaluating field and post-harvest laboratory experiments
• Performing statistical analyses, including AI-based approaches
• Presentation of results at national and international events and publication in peer-reviewed and in practice-oriented journals
• Organisation of national workshops for growers, food industry and consumers
• Assistance in plot establishment, maintenance, monitoring, and harvest across all Work Packages of PhenoMi x. This full-time position is funded for four years. Salary and social benefits are provided according to ETH Zurich rules. The place of work will be at Agroscope in 8046 Zurich-Affoltern. Profile
• A MSc degree in agricultural sciences, biology, ecology or in a related field.
• Strong interest in applied interdisciplinary research and enjoyment of complex field experiments

chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht Ricercatore Postdoctoral a Construction Heritage and Preservation 100%, Zurigo, stampa a tempo determinato Drucken La cattedra di Construction Heritage and Preservation è attualmente alla ricerca di un ricercatore post-dottorato a partire dal settembre 2026 o su accordo. La cattedra di patrimonio edilizio e conservazione si occupa di sfide teoriche e pratiche di raccolta, valutazione e conservazione dei monumenti. È affiliato all'Istituto per la conservazione e la storia delle costruzioni (IDB) e all'Istituto per la tecnologia in architettura (ITA) . La conoscenza dei metodi di costruzione tradizionali, dei materiali, dei principi di progettazione architettonica e dei processi di costruzione è essenziale per una gestione professionale e responsabile degli edifici storici. Per quanto riguarda il futuro sviluppo del patrimonio edilizio sembra altrettanto importante considerare i processi più giovani e anche attuali. I nuovi materiali da costruzione, i metodi di costruzione e i “trends” influiscono sempre più sull’architettura e nel settore dell’edilizia è possibile riconoscere un’accelerazione dell’implementazione di nuove idee e tecnologie. Attualmente, vi è una mancanza di conoscenza circa l'invecchiamento e la riparabilità di tali nuove costruzioni e la ricerca sulle conseguenze a lungo termine per lo stock di edifici sembra insufficiente. La ricerca si concentra su diversi stock edilizi, sia più vecchi che più giovani (e anche molto giovani), domande del loro valore come monumenti e sfide relative alla loro conservazione. In questo contesto, i lavori di ingegneria strutturalmente eccezionali in Svizzera e gli esempi costruiti di processi e metodi di costruzione di nuova concezione sono di particolare interesse. Le attività didattiche includono corsi elettivi e seminari di base che permettono agli studenti di studiare e discutere le questioni attuali in dettaglio. La lezione si concentra sulle basi teoriche e pratiche di conservazione. Inoltre, la cattedra offre i programmi di formazione continua accademica che combinano in modo completo e metodologico elevati standard accademici con rilevanza pratica e impartiscono competenze professionali specifiche. Postdoctoral Researcher at Construction Heritage and Preservation 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Professorship of Construction Heritage and Preservation is currently searching for a postdoctoral researcher to start in September 2026 or upon agreement. Project background The Professorship of Construction Heritage and Preservation engages with theoretical and practical challenges of methodical collecting, assessing and preserving of monuments. It is affiliated with the Institute for Preservation and Construction History (IDB) as well as the Institute for Technology in Architecture (ITA) . Knowledge of traditional construction methods, materials, architectural design principles and building processes is essential for a professional and responsible handling of historic buildings. With regard to the future development of the building stock it seems equally important to consider younger and even current processes. New building materials, construction methods and “trends” are increasingly affecting architecture and an accelerated implementation of new ideas and technologies can be recognised in the building sector. Currently, there is a lack of knowledge about the aging and reparability of such new constructions and research on long-term consequences for the building stock seems inadequate. Research focusses on diverse building stocks, both older and younger (as well as very young), questions of their value as monuments and challenges concerning their conservation. Within this context, the structurally outstanding engineering works in Switzerland as well as the built examples of newly developed construction processes and methods are of special interest. Teaching activities include elective courses and core seminars which allow students to study and discuss current issues in-depth. The lecture concentrates on the theoretical and practical basics of preservation. Furthermore, the professorship offers the academic continuing education programs which comprehensively and methodologically combine high academic standards with practical relevance and impart specific professional skills. Job description As a postdoctoral researcher, your responsibilities will include:
• Formulating and writing proposals for research grant applications (SNF, Innosuisse, EU Horizon, etc.)
• Contributing to ongoing research projects, including scientific publication efforts
• Co-leading publication projects
• Supporting teaching activities within the professorship, including further education programmes (MAS/CAS)
• Supporting the supervision of doctoral researchers within the professorship, and
• Taking on short- and medium-term projects within the framework of the Competence Center for Preservation at IDB Profile
• You have a Master's degree and a PhD in architecture, civil engineering, art history or technology history, or related fields
• You have experience of applying for and successfully obtaining third-party funding for research projects
• Knowledge of Swiss and international architectural heritage and building cultures is an asset
• You can demonstrate excellent written and oral communication skills in German and English Workplace Workplace We offer
• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht PhD candidato per lo sviluppo di modelli multi-fisici di trasformatori a media frequenza ad alta potenza 100%, Zurigo, stampa a tempo fisso Drucken Il Laboratorio per sistemi elettronici ad alta potenza (HPE) presso il Dipartimento di tecnologia dell'informazione e ingegneria elettrica di ETH Zurigo conduce la ricerca internazionale leader sui sistemi di convertitori elettronici di potenza, che sono necessari, per esempio, nei futuri sistemi di distribuzione di energia elettrica per i Un'altra ricerca si concentra sui modulatori a impulsi a stato solido per applicazioni mediche (trattamento tomografia computer/cancro) e sugli acceleratori (CERN). Per la progettazione e l'ottimizzazione dei vari sistemi elettronici di potenza, sviluppiamo modelli multi-fisici avanzati / gemelli digitali / prototipi virtuali a livello di componenti e sistemi. Per un nuovo progetto di ricerca su Solid-State-Transformers per i futuri data center, stiamo cercando un: PhD candidate (100%) per lo sviluppo di modelli multi-fisici di trasformatori ad alta potenza a media frequenza Descrizione del lavoro Siamo alla ricerca di individui altamente motivati con un eccezionale background accademico che sono interessati a perseguire un dottorato nell'importante e multidisciplinare area di ricerca di modellazione e ottimizzazione di trasformatori ad alta potenza, a media frequenza (MFT). I trasformatori compatti e altamente efficienti che operano a frequenze kilohertz sono componenti chiave dei convertitori DC-DC ad alta potenza, che sono il componente principale dei trasformatori a stato solido (SST). Tali SST sono necessari, per esempio, in futuri data center AI, dove il consumo di energia per rack di computer aumenta a livelli di diverse centinaia di kilowatt o addirittura megawatt. Per trasferire l'energia in modo efficiente dalla rete a CPU/GPU, sono necessarie tensioni di sistema più elevate nei centri di dati / rack per computer, e sistemi di convertitori elettronici di potenza efficienti basati su SST sono essenziali per il controllo del flusso di potenza altamente dinamico. Per spingere i limiti di efficienza e densità di potenza di questi SST si svilupperà modelli multi-fisici di trasformatori, che descrivono non solo le perdite (HF) nell'avvolgimento e nel nucleo, ma anche la distribuzione di raffreddamento / temperatura nel trasformatore, risonanze nell'avvolgimento a causa di capacità parassitarie, e isolamento elettrico. Si lavorerà anche sull'ottimizzazione della geometria del nucleo e dell'avvolgimento, lo sviluppo di concetti di raffreddamento avanzati per gli avvolgimento e il core, e la progettazione di soluzioni per collegare efficacemente gli avvolgimento ad alta corrente. Utilizzando i modelli e i concetti sviluppati, si identificherà le barriere tecnologiche per la potenza trasferibile e l'efficienza dei MFT. I modelli sviluppati dovrebbero essere integrati in procedure di ottimizzazione per sistemi di convertitori elettronici di potenza in modo computazionalmente efficiente. Ciò è essenziale per ottenere efficienze di sistema eccezionali e densità di potenza, così come ottenere un vantaggio competitivo. I modelli fanno parte anche di un continuo e più ampio progetto di sviluppo del framework di modellazione presso HPE, offrendo l'opportunità di collaborare con altri candidati PhD su diversi aspetti di modellazione. Per verificare i nuovi concetti e modelli sviluppati, si progetta e costruisce prototipi MFT, compresi i sistemi di conversione, per operare i MFT in condizioni realistiche. Profilo

• Buone capacità di comunicazione

PhD candidate for developing multi-physics models of high-power medium frequency transformers 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The Laboratory for High Power Electronic Systems (HPE) at the Department of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering of ETH Zurich conducts internationally leading research on power electronic converter systems, which are required, for example, in future energy distribution systems for the integration of renewable energy sources or in traction applications/electric vehicles. Another research focus is on solid-state pulse modulators for medical applications (computer tomography/cancer treatment) and accelerators (CERN). For the design and optimisation of the various power electronic systems, we develop advanced multi-physics models/digital twins/virtual prototypes at the component and system level. For a new research project on Solid-State-Transformers for future data centres, we are looking for a: PhD candidate (100%) for developing multi-physics models of high-power medium frequency transformers Job description We are looking for highly motivated individuals with an outstanding academic background who are interested in pursuing a PhD in the important and multidisciplinary research area of modelling and optimising high-power, medium-frequency transformers (MFTs). Compact, highly efficient transformers that operate at kilohertz frequencies are key components of high-power DC-DC converters, which are the core component of solid-state transformers (SSTs). Such SSTs are required, for example, in future AI data centres, where power consumption per computer rack increases to levels of several hundred kilowatts or even megawatts. To transfer energy efficiently from the grid to CPUs/GPUs, higher system voltages are required in data centres/computer racks, and efficient power electronics converter systems based on SSTs are essential for controlling the highly dynamic power flow. For pushing the efficiency and power density limits of these SSTs you will develop multi-physics models of transformers, which describe not only the (HF) losses in the winding and the core, but also the cooling/temperature distribution in the transformer, resonances in the winding due to parasitic capacitances, and electrical insulation. You will also work on optimising the core and winding geometry, developing advanced cooling concepts for the windings and core, and designing solutions for efficiently connecting the high-current windings. Using the models and concepts developed, you will then identify technological barriers to the transferable power and efficiency of MFTs. The developed models should be integrated into optimisation procedures for power electronic converter systems in a computationally efficient way. This is essential for achieving outstanding system efficiencies and power densities, as well as gaining a competitive edge. The models are also part of an ongoing, wider modelling framework development project at HPE, offering the opportunity to collaborate with other PhD candidates on different modelling aspects. For verifying the new concepts and developed models, you will design and build MFT prototypes, including converter systems, to operate the MFTs under realistic conditions. Profile

• Fundamental knowledge of power electronic converter systems
• Good communication skills
• Fluency in English
• The willingness to fully commit yourself as part of an international team.
• In addition, you should be interested in the detailed modelling and design of magnetic components and the optimisation of power electronic systems. Workplace Workplace We offer

chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht PhD-Kandidat für die Entwicklung von Multi-Physik-Modellen von Hochleistungs-Mittelfrequenztransformatoren 100%, Zürich, Festdruck Drucken Das Labor für High Power Electronic Systems (HPE) am Department of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering der ETH Zürich führt international führende Forschungen zu Stromelektronik-Konvertersystemen durch, die beispielsweise in zukünftigen Energieverteilungssystemen für die Integration erneuerbarer Energieträger oder Zugfahrzeuge benötigt werden. Ein weiterer Forschungsschwerpunkt sind Festkörper-Impulsmodulatoren für medizinische Anwendungen (Computertomographie/Krebsbehandlung) und Beschleuniger (CERN). Für die Gestaltung und Optimierung der verschiedenen leistungselektronischen Systeme entwickeln wir fortschrittliche multiphysikalische Modelle/digitale Zwillinge/virtueller Prototypen auf Bauteil- und Systemebene. Für ein neues Forschungsprojekt zu Solid-State-Transformern für zukünftige Rechenzentren suchen wir einen: PhD-Kandidat (100%) für die Entwicklung von Multi-Physik-Modellen von Hochleistungs-Mittelfrequenztransformatoren Jobbeschreibung Wir suchen hoch motivierte Personen mit einem hervorragenden akademischen Hintergrund, die daran interessiert sind, einen Doktortitel im wichtigen und multidisziplinären Forschungsbereich der Modellierung und Optimierung von hochleistungsfähigen, mittelfrequenten Transformatoren (MFTs) zu verfolgen. Kompakte, hocheffiziente Transformatoren, die bei Kilohertz-Frequenzen arbeiten, sind Schlüsselkomponenten von Hochleistungs-DC-Wandlern, die Kernkomponente von Festkörpertransformatoren (SSTs). Solche SSTs sind beispielsweise in zukünftigen KI-Datenzentren erforderlich, wo der Stromverbrauch pro Computer-Rack auf mehrere hundert Kilowatt oder sogar Megawatt ansteigt. Um Energie effizient vom Netz auf CPUs/GPUs zu übertragen, sind höhere Systemspannungen in Rechenzentren/Computer-Racks erforderlich und effiziente Stromelektronik-Wandlersysteme auf Basis von SSTs sind für die Steuerung des hochdynamischen Leistungsflusses unerlässlich. Um die Effizienz- und Leistungsdichtegrenzen dieser SSTs zu schieben, entwickeln Sie mehrphysikalische Modelle von Transformatoren, die nicht nur die (HF) Verluste in der Wicklung und dem Kern beschreiben, sondern auch die Kühl-/Temperaturverteilung im Transformator, Resonanzen in der Wicklung durch parasitäre Kapazitäten und elektrische Isolation. Sie arbeiten auch daran, die Kern- und Wickelgeometrie zu optimieren, fortschrittliche Kühlkonzepte für Wicklungen und Kern zu entwickeln und Lösungen für eine effiziente Verbindung der Hochstromwicklungen zu entwickeln. Mit den entwickelten Modellen und Konzepten werden Sie dann technologische Barrieren für die übertragbare Leistung und Effizienz von MFTs identifizieren. Die entwickelten Modelle sollten rechnerisch effizient in Optimierungsverfahren für stromelektronische Wandlersysteme integriert werden. Dies ist wichtig, um hervorragende Systemeffizienzen und Leistungsdichten zu erzielen und einen Wettbewerbsvorteil zu gewinnen. Die Modelle sind auch Teil eines laufenden, breiteren Modellierungs-Rahmenentwicklungsprojekts bei HPE und bieten die Möglichkeit, mit anderen PhD-Kandidaten zu verschiedenen Modellierungsaspekten zusammenzuarbeiten. Um die neuen Konzepte und entwickelten Modelle zu überprüfen, entwerfen und bauen Sie MFT-Prototypen, einschließlich Konvertersysteme, um die MFTs unter realistischen Bedingungen zu betreiben. Profil
• Sie müssen einen Diplom/M.Sc.-Abschluss in der Elektrotechnik mit ausgezeichneten Noten
• Grundkenntnisse von Stromelektronik-Konvertersystemen
• Gute Kommunikationsfähigkeiten
